timeline.summary: Applicant Christina Marazza presented a proposal to open a cat-only boarding and grooming franchise at 7 McDonald Avenue, which sits in a Professional Business Office (PBO) zoning district that does not currently permit the use, requiring a zoning text amendment. The Board received a letter declaring intent to act as lead agency under SEQRA and referred the matter to the town and county planning boards; no zoning decision was made this meeting.

cases.name: Summit Club at Armonk (formerly Brynwood) — Amended and Restated Water District Contribution Agreement
cases.address: Summit Club at Armonk (formerly Brynwood), Armonk

timeline.summary: Following a planning board recommendation the prior night to require a third-party hydrogeologist (Bill Canavan) to review the applicant's well/water-supply submission to NYSDEC and Westchester DOH before it goes to the state and county, the Board debated at length with applicant's counsel (Mark Weingarten) and engineers, and with town counsel and a resident who summarized the planning board discussion (citing consultants Jim Jensen and Mike Pollock's concerns about aquifer drilling and off-site discharge to the Byron River). The Board ultimately adopted the resolution with four changes (including the hydrogeologist-review requirement) and approved/authorized the supervisor to sign the amended water agreement with three changes, plus a separate recommendation that the planning board consider a performance bond to protect resident wells within 1,500 feet of the new wells.

cases.name: Tax Certiorari Consent Judgment — Board of Assessors
cases.applicant: Property owner (name garbled in ASR transcript)

timeline.summary: The Board authorized special counsel William Maker of Maker, Bajal & Decostenzo LLP to execute a consent judgment resolving a multi-year tax certiorari proceeding against the Board of Assessors (several index numbers spanning roughly 2018-2021 tax years). The item passed without discussion.

cases.name: Community Center / Emergency Shelter Renovation — Bathroom Change Order 8

timeline.summary: Following a board tour of the community center (which doubles as the town's emergency shelter, referenced against Superstorm Sandy usage), the Board debated a roughly $15,000 total change-order package including about $4,500 for taller bathroom shower doors with sweeps versus a cheaper shower-curtain alternative, plus a separate kitchen change order (refrigerator relocation) that the board opted to rebid rather than approve as priced. The Board approved change order 8 (the bathroom door change) by roll-call vote, with Councilman Hussain casting the lone 'no' vote, preferring to first negotiate a better price with the contractor; the kitchen change order was held back for rebidding.

cases.name: Mount Misery / Miller Hill (North White Plains) — Open Space Designation

timeline.summary: Following years of advocacy by North White Plains resident Nora, who presented Revolutionary War-era cannonballs found on the property and detailed the site's role protecting American soldiers, the Board received letters from the North Castle Historical Society, the Landmarks Preservation Committee, and open space advocates, and voted to schedule a public hearing on July 27, 2022 to consider designating Mount Misery/Miller Hill as protected open space for its historical significance.

cases.name: Mount Misery / Miller Hill (North White Plains) — Open Space Designation

timeline.summary: The Board closed the public hearing and adopted the resolution formally designating the town-owned parcel at 16 Nethermont Avenue as permanently preserved open space for its Revolutionary War historical significance (a defensive post during the 1776 Battle of White Plains). A companion resolution, also adopted (subject to permissive referendum), authorized the town to purchase the adjacent parcel at 18 Nethermont Avenue for up to $165,000 from fund balance, require a professional appraisal, and provide public access with interpretive signage; an anonymous donor separately committed to funding a sign.

cases.name: Rocky Ridge Swim & Tennis Club — Waiver Request for Illegal Shipping-Container Storage
cases.address: Rocky Ridge Swim & Tennis Club (R1A zone)

timeline.summary: Facing an active code-enforcement trial for a site-plan violation (roughly 100 shipping containers plus a commercial tree-service operation's vehicles stored on site, generating about 23% of the nonprofit's $270,000 annual operating budget), the financially strapped club's attorney asked the Board to waive Town Code 114-4(b)'s restriction on processing applications during litigation so it could pursue legalizing the use via a zoning text amendment or use variance. Building Inspector Rob detailed extensive additional violations found on a same-day site visit (debris, overflowing dumpsters, unauthorized parking-lot expansion, wood-chip dumping). Board members and a public commenter (Ed) argued granting the waiver would reward over a year of unaddressed illegal activity and set a bad precedent; the Board voted unanimously to deny the waiver, leaving the matter to proceed through the pending court case, while noting a narrower use-variance route (versus a townwide zoning text change) could be revisited later.

cases.name: Praise Church, 901 North Broadway (North White Plains) — Special Use Permit for House of Worship
cases.address: 901 North Broadway, Suite 24, North White Plains

timeline.summary: Pastor David Martinez presented Praise Church's application to relocate into leased space at 901 North Broadway to hold worship services and community/family programs. The Board received the application materials and referred it to the town and county planning boards; Director of Planning Adam Kaufman advised that based on the applicant's (outdated) submitted materials, the mixed-use building likely lacks sufficient code-required off-street parking for a house-of-worship use layered onto the building's other tenants, meaning the applicant would probably need to seek a parking variance from the Zoning Board of Appeals and submit an updated building-use/parking layout before a town board hearing could be scheduled.

cases.name: Resolution Supporting State Assembly Bill A9079 / Senate Bill S8378 (Freshwater Wetlands Pesticide Prohibition)

timeline.summary: At the request of the town's state legislators, the Board adopted a resolution supporting proposed state legislation adding a new Environmental Conservation Law section prohibiting pesticide use near local freshwater wetlands, after brief discussion about whether to first route it through the conservation board (ultimately done in parallel rather than delaying the vote).

cases.name: Proposed Amendments to Town Code of Ethics (Chapter 27) — Disclosure Form & Training
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle Board of Ethics

timeline.summary: Board of Ethics chair Brett Summers asked the town board to schedule a public hearing on amendments expanding financial-disclosure requirements (including whether to add department heads to the list of covered individuals) and adding ethics training for department heads and volunteer board/committee members. A former union official spoke at length arguing that department heads (e.g., a highway foreman) likely do not meet the Taylor Law's legal definition of 'management,' cautioning the board to weigh that distinction as the item goes to labor counsel. The board discussed but did not vote to schedule the hearing this meeting, targeting a September hearing date.

cases.name: Filming & Photography Permit — Independent Short Film Production
cases.address: Local gas station/mini-mart and adjacent office complex, Armonk
cases.applicant: Lisa Hammer and Levi Wilson (writer-director-producer), with production manager Jen Emma

timeline.summary: Filmmakers Lisa Hammer and Levi Wilson requested approval for a special same-week meeting to permit filming of a self-funded, semi-autobiographical short film (a proof-of-concept for a planned feature) at a gas station/mini-mart and neighboring office property in Armonk, whose owners had voluntarily offered their lots for use. The police department had already reviewed and signed off on the application; the Board asked a few clarifying questions about the film's theme and had no substantive concerns, and unanimously approved the permit and authorized the supervisor to sign, with the applicants agreeing to credit the town and provide promotional materials.

cases.name: Volta EV Charging Kiosks — 670 North Broadway (North White Plains Stop & Shop)

timeline.summary: Volta Charging presented a proposed zoning text amendment to permit its advertising-supported EV charging kiosks (7-foot-tall displays with front/back digital screens) at the North White Plains Stop & Shop, arguing the town's code currently doesn't address EV charging at all and that the draft legislation on file would bar Volta's ad-subsidized model, which offers free level-two charging paid for by advertising revenue. Board members raised concerns about the size and aesthetics of the displays, the precedent of allowing advertising-based charging stations, whether the town could hold the applicant to a no-audio/no-video restriction if their business model changed, and whether nearby residents/shoppers not using the charger were unfairly subjected to ads; a member reported informal neighborhood feedback was unfavorable on the advertising aspect.

cases.name: Downtown Parking Lot Expansion (Former Verizon Parcel, West Side Main Street)
cases.address: West side Main Street / Kent Place, Armonk

timeline.summary: Engineer Joe presented a design for additional downtown parking behind Main Street (former Verizon-owned land near Kent Place/Whippoorwill), redesigned to allow two-way traffic circulation with head-in parking. The Board discussed next steps (easements, subdivision/site-plan review with the Planning Board, lead-agency designation, and financing) and floated the longer-term concept of a formal West Side parking district with differentiated employee/consumer parking and time limits, to be worked out later.

cases.name: Temporary Outdoor Dining Permit Extension

timeline.summary: With the COVID-era temporary outdoor-dining regulations set to expire October 1st, the Board extended them through January 3, 2023 to give restaurants continued flexibility while directing the Town Attorney and Director of Planning to draft permanent outdoor-dining code provisions before then. One restaurant with an oversized tent was advised to downsize to avoid a separate New York State time-limit rule.

cases.name: Quarry Heights / Old Orchard Street Water District Extension Study

timeline.summary: The Board authorized the Water & Sewer Director to pursue a preliminary engineering study for extending public water (purchased via a Westchester Joint Water Works master connection) to roughly 43 properties in the Quarry Heights/Old Orchard Street/Starkey area currently on temporary or private water service, as a first step toward a possible new water district and to position the project for state grant funding, which typically requires projects to be "shovel ready."

cases.name: PFAS Water Treatment & Public Notification (Water Districts 2 & 4)

timeline.summary: The Board approved an amendment to the Town's existing WSP engineering agreement to move Water District 4's School Street well into design for PFAS/PFOA treatment (likely ion exchange), after the county health department approved WSP's action plan; a parallel Langan Engineering proposal for Water District 2 (Whippoorwill/Coleman Hill area) was still pending. The bulk of the meeting was consumed by a heated public exchange in which resident Jen Clark challenged the Water & Sewer Director and board over why the public school (on Water District 2, which had a PFAS detect at/near the 10 ppt threshold) was not receiving bottled water like some private-well households near the old landfill, calling the Town's website-only messaging inadequate.

cases.name: Town Brokerage Account for Treasury Investments

timeline.summary: The Board authorized the Director of Finance to open a new JP Morgan brokerage account to invest a portion of the Town's fund balance directly in U.S. Treasuries rather than leaving it in lower-yield checking/bank instruments, an idea that emerged from the FY2023 budget work sessions given rising interest rates.

cases.name: Cross Road Parcel Sale Request (Old Hickory Way)
cases.address: 1 Old Hickory Way / Cross Road, Bedford

timeline.summary: The Board received a request from prospective buyers to purchase roughly 3.334 acres of town-owned land contiguous to 1 Old Hickory Way, and referred it to the Planning Board, Highway Superintendent and Town Assessor. A board member flagged that the parcel carries an emergency-access easement serving other homes on the long Old Hickory Way cul-de-sac, and asked that police and fire also weigh in and that neighboring residents be specially notified if the matter advances to a public hearing.

cases.name: Alana Court Guide Rail Installation

timeline.summary: Following a 2022 ice-storm incident in which a Town plow driver nearly went off a 40-foot drop-off on Alana Court, retired Highway Superintendent Mike Giaccio read a statement on behalf of Highway Superintendent Jamie Norris recommending a roughly 340-foot guide rail (reduced from 375 feet to lessen visual impact on the adjacent resident). The Board received letters from the Highway Superintendent and Town Administrator affirming the safety determination; no board vote on the guide rail itself was required since it is a staff/administrative safety decision, but members voiced support.

cases.name: Virginia Road Sidewalks, Curbing & Drainage — SAM Grant Application

timeline.summary: The Board authorized the Supervisor and Town Attorney to sign a $200,000 State and Municipal Facilities (SAM) grant application, secured through State Senator Shelley Mayer's office, for sidewalk, curbing and drainage construction along Virginia Road.

cases.name: Old Mount Kisco Road Water & Sewer Infrastructure Dedication

timeline.summary: Applicant's counsel (Cory Salomon, Zarin & Steinmetz) asked the Board to accept dedication of new water main (Water District 4) and sanitary sewer main (Sewer District 2) infrastructure built by the developer of the senior housing project on Old Mount Kisco Road, via receipt and approval of the bills of sale; a separate request to reduce the developer's performance bonds was withdrawn for this meeting pending resolution of road-restoration work, to be coordinated with the Highway Superintendent once paving is scheduled. The Board approved the dedication (including the associated bills of sale) unanimously, which enables the developer to proceed with sewer/water lateral hookups without shortcutting any remaining approval steps.

cases.name: Temporary Outdoor Dining & Restaurant Parking Regulations — Extension

timeline.summary: The Board adopted a resolution extending its temporary COVID-era outdoor dining permit regulations (which allow restaurants to use parking-lot space for tents/patios) to October 31, 2023, after hearing that several restaurant owners still wanted the accommodation. The Board directed staff to use the extension period to develop a permanent framework, including possibly reducing off-street parking requirements for restaurants that build permanent outdoor dining structures, and asked for data on which restaurants are using tents and how much parking capacity is affected.

cases.name: Airport Campus — Reworked Townhouse/Age-Restricted Apartment Alternative
cases.address: Airport Campus / 113 King Street and associated properties
cases.applicant: Airport Campus developer (in contract with Toll Brothers; represented by Tony Beniziano)

timeline.summary: The Board received the applicant's amended zoning petition splitting the property into a 4.5-acre RMFSCH parcel (age-restricted apartments, with a negotiated FAR cap above 0.4 tied to converting office to residential use) and a 34-acre RMFA parcel (fee-simple townhouses), plus the preliminary FEIS, and referred both to the town and county planning boards and town consultants. Discussion covered a proposed larger water storage tank (170,000+ gallons) that could let the town extend public water service toward the hamlet, the fate of a historic 1820s house on the property (the applicant is discussing relocating rather than demolishing it, with the town historical society expected to weigh in), and a still-unresolved dispute over whether a conservation easement restricts use of part of the site ("Cooney Hill") as a standalone development parcel.

cases.name: NY State Housing Compact / Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Mandate — Town Opposition

timeline.summary: The Town Board hosted State Assemblyman Chris Burdick and State Senator Shelley Mayer to discuss Governor Hochul's proposed Housing Compact, focusing on the TOD provision that would mandate minimum 25-units-per-acre zoning within a half mile of the North White Plains train station (an estimated ~2,600 potential new units) and an ADU mandate that would bar municipalities from requiring off-street parking for ADUs near transit, exacerbating North White Plains' documented on-street parking shortage. Town Planner Adam Kaufman presented a slide deck (praised by both legislators) documenting the town's existing record of approved multi-family and affordable housing to counter the narrative that suburbs like North Castle block housing. Both legislators committed to fighting to strip the TOD provision entirely from their chambers' one-house budget responses and asked residents to keep emailing as negotiations continued through late March.

cases.name: Breezemont Day Camp — Special Permit Zoning Text Amendment
cases.address: 63 Cox Avenue area, Armonk (Breezemont Day Camp)
cases.applicationType: local law (zoning text amendment creating a new special-use-permit category for day camps)
cases.applicant: HZBR LLC (Breezemont Day Camp), represented by Kirkpatrick Law LLC

timeline.summary: The board adopted a zoning text amendment creating a new special-permit category allowing day camps in residential districts, intended to let the long-operating (since 1932), previously non-conforming Breezemont Day Camp eventually seek legal conforming status; the amendment itself does not change the camp's current operations. Neighbors (represented by Brian Burns reading a letter from Bill O'Brien and Anita Finelli) said the camp is generally a good neighbor but asked that loudspeaker/megaphone use and late-night music at counselor parties be curtailed, since sound carries to nearby homes; the board incorporated a sound-amplification restriction and a submission/annual-monitoring requirement to the Building Inspector into the adopted local law. A related resident concern about speeding on Cox Avenue was raised and referred to the Police Chief for review of existing traffic-calming measures.

cases.name: Cycle for Survival Fundraiser — Special Event Permit
cases.applicant: CSM Sport & Entertainment (for Memorial Sloan Kettering)

timeline.summary: The board approved a special event permit for the annual Cycle for Survival indoor-cycling fundraiser benefiting rare-cancer research at Memorial Sloan Kettering, held annually in the town for several years. A board member who is a cancer survivor treated at Memorial Sloan Kettering spoke personally about the cause's significance to her.

cases.name: Volunteer Firefighter Length-of-Service Award (LOSAP) Eligibility — Five-Year to Two-Year Threshold
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (request presented by Armonk Fire Department volunteers, incl. Alex)
cases.lastStatus: deferred — board to revisit for a public hearing in the fall, after Westchester County acts

trajectory.status: deferred — board to revisit for a public hearing in the fall, after Westchester County acts

timeline.status: deferred — board to revisit for a public hearing in the fall, after Westchester County acts
timeline.summary: Armonk Fire Department volunteers asked the board to reduce, from five years to two years, the length-of-service threshold at which volunteer firefighters become eligible for a modest annual tax-related benefit (calculated at roughly $2,800/year per additional qualifying volunteer at current town tax rates), arguing the two-year mark is the critical retention point where volunteers are most likely to leave without some show of appreciation. The board was broadly sympathetic and agreed the cost was minor relative to the value of retention, but the Supervisor preferred to follow past town practice of waiting for Westchester County to adopt its own version of the enabling legislation first (expected in the fall) rather than being one of only a handful of municipalities acting ahead of the county, while leaving open the option to move first if the county doesn't act by fall.

cases.name: Eagle Ridge (former IBM/MBIA Campus) — Rezoning to Multi-Family Senior Housing
cases.address: Adjacent to the former IBM property (MBIA campus), North Castle
cases.applicationType: local law / rezoning (site adjacent to Westchester County Airport)
cases.applicant: Toll Brothers (represented by Corey Salomon, Zarin & Steinmetz; Josh Weissman)
cases.lastStatus: public hearing continued/adjourned to June 14 and later June 28, 2023

trajectory.status: public hearing continued/adjourned to June 14 and later June 28, 2023

timeline.status: public hearing continued/adjourned to June 14 and later June 28, 2023
timeline.summary: The board continued a public hearing on a local law to reclassify the former IBM/MBIA office campus from Office Business (OB-H) to a multi-family senior-housing zoning district (RMF-A/RMF-SCH), a conceptual ~88-unit project. Applicant's counsel asked the board's informal blessing to present a conceptual site plan to the Planning Board ahead of formal rezoning approval, which the board did not object to. The bulk of the meeting was a detailed discussion of airport noise: Planning Board member and Airport Advisory Board liaison Michael Pollock presented flight-frequency and noise-complaint data for the adjacent runway, prompting board debate over whether potential future-resident noise complaints should factor into the zoning decision versus being treated as a market/disclosure issue, with several members favoring a simple buyer-notification mechanism (offering plan language, construction sound-mitigation standards) rather than treating airport proximity as a reason to reconsider the zoning.

cases.name: Grant-Writing Services Contract — J. O'Connell and Associates
cases.lastStatus: approved, conditioned on Town Administrator confirming scope includes structured input from town advisory boards/committees

trajectory.status: approved, conditioned on Town Administrator confirming scope includes structured input from town advisory boards/committees

timeline.status: approved, conditioned on Town Administrator confirming scope includes structured input from town advisory boards/committees
timeline.summary: The board approved a two-year, ~$3,900/month contract with J. O'Connell and Associates (grant-writing consultants who have worked with Somers, Pleasantville, and Yorktown) to pursue infrastructure and other grant funding, after discussing the firm's downstate track record and the value of the engagement (framed as likely to return multiples of its cost). The board debated how broadly to solicit project ideas for the consultant to pursue — a narrower department-head-only process versus also soliciting ideas from town advisory boards, committees, and community groups (e.g., Historical Society cemetery restoration, bicentennial signage) — and approved the contract on condition that Town Administrator Kevin Hay confirm with the firm that broader community input can be incorporated without materially expanding cost or timeline.

cases.name: Sustainability Committee Rename & Municipal Food-Scrap Composting Program
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (Recycling Committee, presented by co-chairs Neil Singer and Olivia Bremer)
cases.lastStatus: discussed, no vote (work session) — board directed committee to refine and return with a location/staffing recommendation

trajectory.status: discussed, no vote (work session) — board directed committee to refine and return with a location/staffing recommendation

timeline.status: discussed, no vote (work session) — board directed committee to refine and return with a location/staffing recommendation
timeline.summary: The Recycling Committee, seeking to rebrand as the North Castle Sustainability Committee, presented a proposal for a municipal food-scrap composting drop-off program modeled closely on Scarsdale's program, citing a potential 40% (or higher) reduction in household waste. The committee sought board guidance on number of drop-off locations (one central site vs. simultaneous sites in Armonk and North White Plains), staffing/hours, and initial budget for bins, signage, and pickup (roughly $10,000-$15,000 range depending on scope). The board was supportive of moving forward quickly but was split on whether to launch with one location first to prove the model or launch two locations simultaneously; the board also discussed a related e-waste drop-off effort and cost concerns, and asked that the committee coordinate closely with Town Administrator Kevin Hay on budget and execution.

cases.name: Recycling Committee Renamed to Sustainability Committee — Mission Statement & Budget

timeline.summary: The Board approved renaming the Recycling Committee to the Sustainability Committee, adopted a new mission statement (revised to present tense and to reference a town board liaison generically rather than naming Councilman Berra specifically), and approved a committee structure requiring 6/12/18-month phased plans, with an annual budget of 'up to $10,000' rather than a flat figure, to allow the town flexibility.

cases.name: Request to Relocate AFFH Affordable Units Off-Site — The Byram (585 Main Street) & Summit Club
cases.applicant: Frank Madonna Sr. (The Byram) and Summit Club

timeline.summary: Developer Frank Madonna Sr. requested the Board allow relocating two AFFH affordable units from The Byram (585 Main Street) to a different site (paralleling a similar off-site relocation the Summit Club had previously been granted), citing high common-charge/carrying costs and COVID-era construction cost overruns, and separately argued the town's 80%-of-market-unit-size rule was unfair for multifamily buildings. The Board declined to take any vote on the letter, with several members (led by Matt Milim) arguing it would be improper to grant a one-off exception to the code's stated 'strong preference' for on-site AFFH units without a broader public code-change process, especially given other pending projects (Eagle Ridge, Gateway, the Lumberyard) were watching for precedent. The Board agreed to schedule a future work session on AFFH policy generally rather than act on the individual request.

cases.name: 5 North Granite Road — Petition to Rezone to Professional Business Office (PBO)

timeline.summary: A new petition was introduced to rezone a 1.79-acre lot (currently split between PBO and R-1A) entirely into the Professional Business Office district to allow additional parking for an existing office use. The board received the engineering letter and planning staff report, noted informal concern from two nearby residents about existing lighting issues, and directed the applicant to consider outreach to neighbors and additional landscape screening. The matter was referred to town and county planning boards with a public hearing scheduled for September 27, 2023.

cases.name: Sewer District 2 Wastewater Treatment Plant — EFC Water Infrastructure Improvement Grant Application

timeline.summary: The Board authorized submission of a $712,000 grant application to the New York State Environmental Facilities Corporation's Water Infrastructure Improvement Program to help fund Sewer District 2 wastewater treatment plant upgrades, a second attempt after an earlier unsuccessful application, and authorized the Supervisor to sign the application and related resolution.

cases.name: Police Officer James Kehoe — Promotion to Sergeant
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle Police Department

timeline.summary: The Police Chief recommended promoting Officer James Kehoe, a 7.5-year veteran of the department, to the vacant budgeted sergeant position effective August 12, 2023, following the retirement of a detective sergeant and promotion of another sergeant to lieutenant. The board approved the promotion without objection.

cases.name: Resident Letter Opposing Gas-Powered Leaf Blower Restrictions

timeline.summary: The Board received a resident letter and heard extended public comment opposing any town restriction on gas-powered leaf blowers, framed around cost/practicality concerns for small landscaping businesses and broader objections to environmental regulation. The board took no policy action; the letter was simply received into the record.

cases.name: St. Nersess Armenian Seminary, 46 Bedford Road — Special Use Permit for Building Modifications

timeline.summary: Roughly a decade after its original 2012 special permit, the seminary sought approval for two small additions: a two-room addition to the married-students building for visiting guest lecturers, and a smaller residence to allow the retiring dean to remain on campus semi-retired while a new dean takes over. The Board declared itself lead agency, referred the matter to town and county planning boards, and scheduled a public hearing (targeting mid-to-late October), noting the seminary's actual activity level (currently only four enrolled students) has stayed well below what was originally anticipated or feared at approval.

cases.name: 5 North Greenwich Road — R-1A to PBO Rezoning for Additional Parking
cases.applicant: Reno Montforte (property owner, via Krypton Engineering)
cases.lastStatus: hearing closed; petition returned to applicant without prejudice

trajectory.status: hearing closed; petition returned to applicant without prejudice

timeline.status: hearing closed; petition returned to applicant without prejudice
timeline.summary: The applicant sought to rezone the residential half of a 1.79-acre lot from R-1A to PBO to add 12 parking spaces (beyond code minimums) for physical therapy and office tenants at an already fully-built-out building; the owner also controls several adjoining parcels, which numerous neighbors argued signaled a broader plan to assemble and further commercialize the block. Around two dozen Byron Brook Place and North Greenwich Road residents testified in organized opposition (a 210-plus signature petition, maps, and photos), citing an unpermitted car-show event with loud music and blocked streets, traffic safety at a nearby school bus stop, drainage/runoff concerns, property devaluation, and fear of a domino effect of further rezonings. After extended board discussion about the risk of future variances for additional structures if the parcel were rezoned, the Board closed the public hearing and effectively returned the petition to the applicant without prejudice rather than continue it, at the residents' request for finality; the applicant may reapply later.

cases.name: Stop & Shop Companies — Tax Certiorari Consent Judgment

timeline.summary: The Board authorized the Town Attorney to execute a consent judgment resolving a tax certiorari matter brought by the Stop & Shop Companies, with no discussion recorded.

cases.name: Town DPW Storage/Compost Yard — Environmental Concerns
cases.address: Middle Patent Road to Banksville Road (town-owned parcel near Windmill wells)

timeline.summary: A resident (Joe) told the Board during public comment that a long, narrow town-owned parcel between Middle Patent Road and Banksville Road — environmentally sensitive due to proximity to the Windmill community's wells and a headwater branch of the Mianus River — is being used to store soil, stone, brush, wood chips, and equipment beyond its originally intended small composting footprint, and urged the town to contract with a licensed outside processing facility instead. Board members recalled a prior (2022) vote to have the site cleaned up and expressed surprise it had not been fully addressed; the Supervisor directed the town administrator to research current conditions and report back rather than speculate.

cases.name: J.G. Ormont, LLC v. Town of North Castle — Tax Certiorari Consent Judgment

timeline.summary: The Board authorized the Town Attorney to execute a consent judgment resolving a tax certiorari matter brought by J.G. Ormont, LLC against the Town, with no discussion recorded.

cases.name: Summit Club Golf Course — Temporary Special Use Permit Extension (Maintenance Building / Public Golf Use)
cases.applicant: Summit Club Partners (via JMC Planning and Landscape Architecture)

timeline.summary: The Board granted a one-year extension (through December 31, 2024) of the temporary special use permit allowing continued public use of the golf course while the applicant finalizes the location, engineering, and pricing (now estimated near $5 million) of a proposed permanent maintenance building, correcting a resolution date reference from the 2023 to the 2024 golf season.

cases.name: Windmill Wells — PFOA Treatment Pilot Study (Langan Engineering)

timeline.summary: The Board approved an amendment to the Langan Engineering consulting agreement for a Health Department-mandated PFOA treatment pilot study at the Windmill wells, extending the required test run from 12 to 16 weeks per the equipment manufacturer's recommendation and covering rental of a 20,000-gallon frac tank to haul away test water (since there is no sewer connection on site and discharge to wetlands is prohibited), at an added not-to-exceed cost of $66,800; the town is separately negotiating to discharge the water at the wastewater plant instead, which could yield significant savings, and framed the pilot as a step toward a permanent treatment system that could save roughly $800,000 versus alternatives, potentially aided by grant funding.

cases.name: 2024 Organizational Agenda — Annual Authorizations, Policies and Contracts

timeline.summary: The board reconvened from executive session and adopted the annual organizational package: designation of four depositories, ACH/facsimile payment authorization, statutory appointments (Deputy Supervisor, records/registrar officers, finance director, assessor, consultants and town counsel), legal-notice and meeting-schedule policies, the $0.67/mile mileage rate (matching the new IRS federal standard), the master fee schedule, procurement/investment/vehicle/ethics and workplace policies, salary payment dates, and numerous 2024 professional-service, legal, engineering, stormwater, fire, ambulance, hydrant and intermunicipal agreements. Nearly all passed by unanimous voice vote. The Long Pond Park District agreement (item 33) required a roll call because Councilman Berra recused, passing with the other members and the Supervisor voting aye and Berra abstaining.

cases.name: 2024 Appointment of Departmental and Committee Liaisons

timeline.summary: The Supervisor presented his slate of liaison appointments to departments, boards and committees, framing them as a supervisor's prerogative for the new administration. Councilman Milim objected to being removed as Building Department liaison, noting he had served in that role since 2014 without complaints and citing a precedent where a prior member's shared-liaison request had been honored. Councilwoman DiGiacinto similarly asked to be named a Planning Board liaison alongside others, saying she had raised it privately with the Supervisor and would mention it publicly if not addressed. The Supervisor said he had crafted the list based on his own observations, was open to future discussion, but wanted to proceed tonight; the slate was adopted by voice vote with the objections 'duly noted.'

cases.name: Promotion of Detective Anthony Sabatella to Police Sergeant

timeline.summary: The Police Chief requested board approval to promote Detective Anthony Sabatella, a 10-year member of the department, to the budgeted position of Sergeant effective January 13, 2024, citing his record as School Resource Officer, detective and field training officer and his top placement on the civil-service exam. Board members were enthusiastic and multiple members offered to make the motion. It passed unanimously by voice vote, followed by congratulations and a group photo.

cases.name: North Castle Library Truss Repair — Change Orders
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (library caretaker Catherine/Felix; existing contractor)

timeline.summary: Councilman Hussain, the library liaison, raised the status of structural truss repairs keeping part of the library closed. The Town Administrator (Kevin) reported that outreach to eight firms produced no competing bids and that the existing contractor's four change orders totaled roughly $24,000, with the remaining work being mostly sheetrock closing-up (change orders 3 and 4 of about $9,400 and $5,800). The board debated whether to authorize a spending range now versus gathering more pricing; Councilman Milim pressed for exact figures on the remaining work while Councilman Berra urged going back to the original contractor now. No formal action was taken; the board agreed to gather information offline and bring a change order to the next meeting to reopen the library.

cases.name: Water Infrastructure Improvement Act / EFC Project Finance Agreement — Sewer District No. 2
cases.applicant: Sal Mesiti, Director of Water & Sewer Operations

timeline.summary: The board received a memo from Water/Sewer Director Sal Mesiti regarding a Water Infrastructure Improvement Act award and a project finance agreement with the New York State Environmental Facilities Corporation for a Sewer District No. 2 upgrade. This is the second grant secured for the project, in addition to a $2.9 million DEC grant, with the EFC reimbursing pay applications as construction progresses. The board voted to receive the memo and to authorize Sewer District 2 to enter the finance agreement and accept the roughly $2.968 million grant, praising the Water/Sewer department's work.

cases.name: Staying Alive Charity 11th Annual 5K Fun Run

timeline.summary: The board considered a request from the Staying Alive Charity to hold its 11th annual 5K Fun Run in the Windmill community on Saturday, October 5, 2024. Members confirmed the date would not conflict with the Armonk art show (set for September 28-29). The motion passed, contingent on the charity obtaining the necessary fire, police and insurance approvals, with members praising the event and the charity.

cases.name: Bid Award to Vinco Builders — Exterior Accessible Ramp at Community Center & Library
cases.address: North Castle Community Center and Library

timeline.summary: The board considered awarding a bid to Vinco Builders for an exterior ADA-accessible ramp to the library/community-center back deck and authorizing the Supervisor to sign the agreement. Because the library fund balance was insufficient, roughly $53,000 of the cost (net of a grant) would come from the town's fund balance, drawing the library balance to near zero. Councilman Milim questioned the relatively high cost, the lack of earlier estimates and whether the existing internal ADA route was adequate, while Councilwoman DiGiacinto voiced concern about depleting the library fund balance so early in the year. Councilman Hussain, the library liaison, endorsed the long-deliberated project (including the Trex decking choice), and the board approved it.

cases.name: 2024 Consulting Service Agreements — Weatherworks, Empire (Drug/Alcohol Testing) and KSCJ (Pool Water System)

timeline.summary: The board authorized three service agreements: with Weatherworks for 2024 weather-consulting services; with Empire Consulting for 2024-2025 DOT drug- and alcohol-testing of highway personnel (subject to correcting a typo listing 2023); and with KSCJ Consulting to rehabilitate the town pool's water-supply well and disinfection system to satisfy the Westchester County Department of Health and open the pool for the season. Recreation Superintendent Matt Traynor and the Town Administrator explained the pool well defect, and members expressed confidence in the KSCJ/Kellard work. All three passed by voice vote.

cases.name: Landmarks Preservation Committee — Reduced Required Meeting Frequency (Chapter 195)
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle Landmarks Preservation Committee

timeline.summary: At the LPC's request, the Board adopted a local law reducing the committee's required meeting frequency from six to four times per year (matching the state minimum), while the LPC noted it would still meet more often as needed. A related idea to expand LPC membership beyond its current 8-of-9 seats was raised but not finalized in time for this hearing and will require a separate local law and new public hearing.

cases.name: Work Session — Public Water Main Extension to Lombardi Park
cases.address: Lombardi Park / School Street / Wampus Avenue, Armonk
cases.applicant: Water & Sewer Department (Sal) with Keller engineering (Joe Ciamelli)

timeline.summary: The board weighed alternatives for supplying potable water to Lombardi Park after its private well failed to meet Health Department standards. Rather than an emergency ~$461,000 dedicated service line (or ~$375,000 in well treatment), the board favored installing a larger public water main up School Street, which shaves ~1,000 feet, adds three fire hydrants, and enables future district extension. Consensus was to fund it with ARPA money (must be designated in 2024) and place engineer approval on the next meeting agenda; a district extension and public hearing up School Street would follow. No vote taken — work session only.

cases.name: RFP — Engineering Services for Water District 1 Distribution System Rehabilitation

timeline.summary: The board authorized Sal to issue an RFP for engineering services (design through construction management) to rehabilitate the nearly 100-year-old Water District 1 distribution system in North White Plains, similar to the earlier Water District 2 project. The scope emphasizes chasing grant money and heavy public-relations/coordination given construction disruption. Motion by DiGiacinto, seconded by Rende; adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: Resident Request — Legislation to Ban Gas-Powered Leaf Blowers / Outdoor Equipment
cases.applicant: Resident Chris Hughes; Sustainability Committee (John Edmondson)

timeline.summary: The board received a resident letter urging a ban on gas-powered leaf blowers, and the Sustainability Committee (John Edmondson) reported researching a broader ban on gas outdoor equipment, noting many county municipalities and a California statewide model. The board discussed pollution data, two-stroke engines, enforcement (some laws bar charging via generators), cost impacts on residents and landscapers, and the need for a transition period. Consensus was to have the Sustainability Committee continue researching and monitoring pending state legislation and bring a formal presentation later.

cases.name: 2024 NYS Association of Towns Membership, Dues, and Voting Delegate

timeline.summary: The board approved 2024 membership in the NYS Association of Towns, authorized the Comptroller to pay the (budgeted) annual dues, and designated Supervisor Rende as the town's voting delegate for the February annual meeting. DiGiacinto noted the association's dues invoice recurringly overcharges the town ($1,950 vs. the correct $1,650). Rende agreed to report back on how he votes. Adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: Shared Cost with Byram Hills School District — Additional Championship Sign Panel
cases.applicant: Town / Byram Hills Central School District (Signs Inc.)

timeline.summary: The board approved splitting with the Byram Hills school district the $2,075 cost (~$1,037 each) of an additional panel for the sign recognizing Byram Hills state-championship teams, designed by Signs Inc. to match the original. DiGiacinto, tasked with the sign, pressed to proceed now; Berra supported the concept but wanted design, panel count, and cost details reviewed offline and criticized designing without circulating to colleagues. Hussain sought consistency in the rendering's curvature and spacing. Adopted by voice vote; the board opted to let Signs Inc. handle installation.

cases.name: Graham Restoration Change Orders 3 & 4 — Armonk Library Trusses
cases.address: North Castle Public Library, Armonk branch

timeline.summary: The board approved change orders 3 and 4 with Graham Restoration for the structural truss repair at the Armonk library, negotiated with a $1,500 reduction. Scaffolding and coverings had kept part of the library closed, and members were eager to reopen. Rende and Berra criticized the items as things that should never have been change orders and called for tighter procurement and staff diligence, with Hussain suggesting a retrospective. Hussain made the motion; adopted by voice vote with the $1,500 reduction.

cases.name: Old Business Item B — Tabled

timeline.summary: An unspecified old-business Item B was formally tabled by motion and voice vote with no substantive discussion.

cases.name: 250th Anniversary of American Independence — Celebration Planning (Work Session)
cases.applicant: North Castle Historical Society (Ed Woodyard, Tom Rice, Connie Kehoe)

timeline.summary: The Historical Society presented on North Castle's pivotal role in the 1776 Battle of White Plains and asked the board to authorize a broad-based celebration committee and appropriate roughly $40,000 (primarily for a promotional video and repair/replacement of five historic markers plus a new Mount Misery marker) ahead of a July 4, 2026 celebration. No formal vote was taken; the board was uniformly supportive and Supervisor Rende offered to convene an organizing committee meeting at his office. Members raised ideas about broadening awareness beyond town (county/state/national), engaging schools in video production, and eventually commemorating the 21 local Revolutionary patriots. Funding mechanism and a total cost estimate remain to be worked out.

cases.name: Probationary Appointment of Matthew Barsanti to Police Officer

timeline.summary: The Police Chief presented Matthew Barsanti, a six-year transfer from the NYC Department of Environmental Protection police, recommending his appointment to a budgeted police-officer position effective February 17, 2024 after a thorough background investigation and panel interviews. The board moved the item up on the agenda so family could attend. The motion was made and approved by voice vote (all in favor), and Supervisor Rende administered the oath of office.

cases.name: Food-Scrap Composting Program Launch (Sustainability Committee)

timeline.summary: Councilman Berra, backed by resident committee member Stefan, presented the town's brand-new food-scrap composting program: a $25 kit (counter, mid-size, and drop bins with compostable bags, sold through the Clerk's office) with drop-off at Lombardi Park. They explained accepted materials, methane/landfill and cost-savings benefits, and stressed doing it correctly to avoid contamination. This was an informational rollout, not a vote; enthusiasm was high and Supervisor Rende noted he'd bought a kit.

cases.name: Local Law Amending Chapter 288 — Senior Citizen and Disability Tax Exemptions

timeline.summary: A public hearing was held on the Assessor-requested amendment addressing optional state criteria for senior-citizen and persons-with-disabilities exemptions, specifically whether IRA required-minimum-distributions may be excluded from income; the Assessor recommended including them (i.e., not allowing the exclusion) to prevent abuse. No public spoke and the board was supportive. Berra flagged a drafting issue in paragraph D referencing 'federal or state income tax return.' The board closed the hearing and adopted the local law, subject to the Assessor reviewing whether to delete the 'or state income tax return' language.

cases.name: Water District 4 — Lombardi Park Water Main Extension (School Street Route)

timeline.summary: After a failed well at Lombardi Park, the board pursued a public water main up School Street (~1,000 ft) rather than a costly ~2,000 ft private service line through school property, praised as a superior, future-proof solution by counsel and Sal. The board received the engineer's cost estimate and Kellard proposal (the proposal had been missing from packets but was uploaded during the meeting; total ~$70,625), approved the Kellard proposal and the Spinelli survey proposal, and adopted the final order placing Lombardi Park into District 4 by unanimous 5-0 roll call. A separate District 4 extension proceeding for the School Street homes will follow with resident notification/work session.

cases.name: Local Law Amending Chapter 114 — Application Processing Restrictions (Tax Delinquency)

timeline.summary: The board received a proposed amendment extending the existing 'application processing restrictions' law to bar property owners with delinquent taxes from processing development applications until cured, retaining a board waiver provision for appropriate cases. It was prompted by concern over specific delinquent development properties. Rende raised whether small residential/estate sales could be caught; counsel advised the waiver process (a simple letter, twice-monthly meetings) handles that and declined to build in a dollar-threshold exemption. The board received the law and scheduled a public hearing for February 28, 2024. Berra flagged several drafting inconsistencies to send to counsel by email.

cases.name: Authorization for 2024 In-Rem Tax Foreclosures

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Town Attorney to commence 2024 in-rem foreclosure proceedings against roughly 30 tax-delinquent property owners who had received demand letters, with title searches to follow once the list narrows. Counsel noted one owner already made a several-hundred-thousand-dollar payment and intends full payment by March. Rende voiced concern that owners can pay 'just enough' to stay out of in-rem indefinitely, reinforcing the value of the Chapter 114 tax law. Counsel also noted a coming law change directing surplus foreclosure proceeds to the county for redistribution rather than the town. Approved by vote.

cases.name: NYSDOT Highway Work Permit — Gas Station/Convenience Market, 375 Main Street (Route 128)
cases.applicant: Shell station developer (via Town for NYSDOT permit)

timeline.summary: The board approved a NYSDOT commercial access highway work permit application and checklist for frontage improvements (decorative light pole, curbing, sidewalk) at the long-delayed Shell station/convenience market at the Route 128/Kent Place corner, authorizing the Supervisor to sign. The applicant pays for the work; the town will maintain the decorative improvements as it does elsewhere. Berra flagged an indemnity provision but counsel advised the work is fully insured/bonded with minimal town exposure and that DOT permit terms cannot be changed. Approved by vote.

cases.name: RFP for Operation of Community Park Athletic Facilities (Tennis/Turf Bubble), 205 Business Park Drive

timeline.summary: The board reviewed authorizing an RFP for a 10-year (plus 10-year option) license to operate the Community Park tennis/turf 'bubble' facilities (existing contract expires August 2024; proposed $250,000 minimum annual fee). Barbara DiGiacinto probed maintenance/parking/turf/tennis obligations (satisfied they fall on the operator) and joined Berra in pressing for an inflation hedge — 3% annual escalation 'or CPI, whichever is greater.' Hussain, Milim, and Rende preferred a clean flat 3% to attract bidders given the operator's large capital investment. Berra caught a 'three lowest bidders' typo (should be highest). DiGiacinto moved to amend to 3%-or-CPI-whichever-greater and otherwise approve; Hussain said 'nay' and declined to second, leaving the motion unresolved at the point the transcript ends.

cases.name: Public Comment — Downtown Parking Pay-in-Lieu Fee and Parking District

timeline.summary: Resident/developer Stefan urged the board to revive the 2018 comprehensive-plan recommendation (and Town Planner Adam Kaufman's proposed Chapter 355 amendment) allowing a $12,000-per-space 'pay-in-lieu' parking fee to fund municipal parking and incentivize shared parking districts, offering to be a 'seed investor.' He argued the town created the pay-in-lieu concept but never provided the parking facilities, and pushed for a work session. DiGiacinto agreed a work session is warranted and that the ~40-50-year-old parking legislation should be revisited. Rende and counsel (Roland) recounted the town's difficulty forming districts (contiguity, owner refusals) and endorsed signage/wayfinding to better use existing lots (e.g., Hergenhan, forthcoming Verizon lot). No action; work session to be considered.

cases.name: Recognition of Two Eagle Scouts

timeline.summary: The Supervisor recognized two local Scouts who attained the rank of Eagle Scout, presenting each a certificate of recognition and inviting them to describe their service projects (fern garden with bench/signage and improved learning deck/benches, both at Westmoreland Sanctuary). The board and families took photographs. A ceremonial item with no vote, praising the young men's accomplishment.

cases.name: Appointment of Brandon Hickey as Police Officer

timeline.summary: The Chief recommended appointing Brandon Hickey, a three-year NYC DEP police officer transferring in, to a budgeted police officer position effective March 2, 2024, after a full background investigation and panel interview. The board moved and approved the appointment by voice vote and swore him in on the spot. The Supervisor tied the hire to growing the force (now 31 officers) amid concern over local burglaries.

cases.name: Local Law Amending Town Code Chapter 114 — Application Processing / Tax Delinquency

timeline.summary: The board opened a public hearing on a local law amending Chapter 114 so that delinquency in real estate taxes becomes grounds to withhold processing of a property-improvement application. The board received the notice/affidavits and the short environmental assessment form but did not adopt the negative declaration or the law. Town Attorney Roland noted ~25 delinquent taxpayers had been sent letters under a newly authorized in-rem foreclosure and recommended adjourning the hearing to draw a larger audience. The hearing was adjourned to a date uncertain by voice vote.

cases.name: Proposal from James Turlish and Son — New Water System at North Castle Pool & Tennis Club

timeline.summary: The board approved, on an emergency basis, the proposal from James Turlish and Son for a new water system at the North Castle Pool and Tennis Club, to be paid from fund balance, and authorized the Supervisor to sign the agreement. Approved by voice vote. The Supervisor noted the work is needed to ensure the pool opens for the season.

cases.name: Probationary Appointment of Joseph Lee Bawardi — Groundsman

timeline.summary: The board approved the probationary appointment of Joseph Lee Bawardi as groundsman, effective March 4, by voice vote. Routine personnel action.

cases.name: Probationary Promotional Appointment of Paula Landy — Full-Time Library Clerk

timeline.summary: The board approved the probationary promotional appointment of Paula Landy to full-time library clerk, effective January 28, 2024, by voice vote. A council member welcomed her to the town. Routine personnel action.

cases.name: Communications Committee — Call for Volunteers

timeline.summary: The Town Clerk announced that the technology task force spearheaded by Councilman Hussain has been elevated into a formally established Communications Committee, now seeking roughly seven volunteers with backgrounds in communications, security, or internal development. Applications go through the town's volunteer boards page and are vetted by Councilman Hussain. No vote; an outreach/announcement item.

cases.name: Closing in Memory of Deceased Residents

timeline.summary: Following tradition, the board closed the meeting in memory of three residents: Andrew Caesar (Windmill Farms, ~60-year resident and early IBM family), John Michael 'Jack' Koza Jr., and former North White Plains resident Joseph Brad Finney. Councilwoman DiGiacinto, acting as town historian, offered remembrances; the board moved and approved closing in their memory by voice vote.

cases.name: Conservation Board Proposed Tree Code Amendments

timeline.summary: The Conservation Board (Jane Black, George Drapeau, Craig Benedict) presented proposed amendments to the town's tree-preservation code developed since 2022, including separating 'clearing' and 'thinning' definitions, switching from a calendar year to a rolling 12-month period, lowering the no-permit threshold from 10 trees to 3, removing the confusing landscape-buffer-zone provision, and setting a defined fine (proposed $2,000/tree) rather than an 'up to $1,000' floating amount. Town Planner Adam Kaufman said the existing law works well and the changes are reasonable but not strictly necessary. The board coalesced strongly around resident education (videos, mailers, newsletter inserts) over penalties, and agreed to refer the fine question to the town prosecutor, involve the building inspector, and bring a revised draft back for a public hearing, targeting the first April meeting. No vote taken.

cases.name: RPRC Review Fee for Master-Planned Single-Family Lots
cases.applicant: Town Planner / Town Engineer (Adam Kaufman, Keller)

timeline.summary: Town Planner Adam Kaufman recommended a reduced RPRC review fee of $300 per lot (down from ~$1,800) for individual lots within approved master site plans such as Eagle Ridge and Airport Campus, since the engineering and planning is largely done and the RPRC only checks consistency. Councilman Berra argued the fee should be somewhat higher (about $400 total) so the town is not shortchanged, while other members urged deference to the department head's judgment and against micromanaging. The board adopted Kaufman's $300 recommendation and directed the master fee schedule be updated accordingly. Supervisor Rende recused himself due to his IBM employment adjacent to Eagle Ridge; the motion passed with the remaining members in favor.

cases.name: Madonna Senior Housing — Water Main Extension Bond Release & 3-Year Maintenance Bond

timeline.summary: On the recommendation of the town engineer (John Kellard) and special counsel, the board authorized release of the water main extension performance bond for the Madonna senior housing project and establishment of a three-year maintenance bond. Release was made conditional on the Clerk's office first receiving the maintenance bond and the Town Attorney approving and signing it, with a copy furnished to board members. Members asked that going forward a draft maintenance bond be provided when such items are on the agenda. Approved on a motion and second, all in favor.

cases.name: Shoemaker Lane / Wampus Mill Subdivision — Roadway & Sewer Bond and Cul-de-Sac Repair
cases.applicant: Shoemaker Lane / Wampus Mill subdivision developer

timeline.summary: The item concerned releasing the public roadway and sewer main performance bond and establishing a three-year maintenance bond that would also guarantee milling and repaving the cul-de-sac to the highway superintendent's satisfaction by July 1. The road dedication package was found to be dated, with open questions about who guaranteed the repairs (the father versus the son) and whether the town had been plowing the road as an emergency measure. Special counsel Roland expressed concern about accepting a bond rather than having the work completed before dedication, calling it a hybrid maintenance/performance bond. The board tabled the item pending an updated package (title report, current taxes, maintenance bond draft) from staff.

cases.name: Wall Street Rides FAR — Charity Cycling Event (Oct 5, 2024)
cases.applicant: Wall Street Rides FAR (autism research charity)

timeline.summary: The board approved use of town roads and the pool parking lot for the 10th annual Wall Street Rides FAR charity cycling event for autism research on October 5, 2024. Approval was conditioned on no pavement markings other than chalk that washes off with rain (responding to resident Ed Woodyard's letter about lingering spray-paint arrows), with organizers encouraged to use signs instead, plus Town Attorney approval of indemnity/releases and satisfactory insurance. Organizers were to be told the pool parking lot might not be fully available if pool construction begins. Motion, second, all in favor.

cases.name: Velocity Ride to End Cancer — Charity Ride (Oct 6, 2024)
cases.applicant: Velocity Ride to End Cancer (Columbia University Irving Cancer Center)

timeline.summary: The board approved use of town roads for the Velocity Ride to End Cancer benefiting Columbia University's Irving Cancer Center on Sunday, October 6, 2024, back-to-back with the prior day's event. The same conditions as the Wall Street Rides FAR approval were applied (no paint / chalk only, signs preferred, police route review, Town Attorney sign-off, insurance). Motion, second, all in favor.

cases.name: Retirement Letter — Sharon Reiner (effective March 31)

timeline.summary: The board received the retirement letter of Sharon Reiner, effective March 31, praising her as a devoted employee (noting Sal in Water/Sewer will miss her). A procedural gap was caught by Councilman Hussain — a motion and second had been made but the vote never formally called — so the roll/voice vote was retaken to make it official. Rende noted his practice of sending a thank-you letter from the supervisor and full board to departing employees.

cases.name: Reappointment of Mel Orlana to the Architectural Review Board

timeline.summary: The board reappointed Mel Orlana to a vacated seat on the Architectural Review Board for a term expiring September 13, 2028, with Rende praising his building and construction background. Motion, second, all in favor.

cases.name: Appointment of David Affrack to the Housing Board

timeline.summary: The board appointed David Affrack to the Housing Board for a five-year term expiring March 13, 2029, on the recommendation of Housing Board member Ginny McGrown, noting his volunteer work helping residents with tax returns. Motion, second, all in favor.

cases.name: Resignation of Joe Monticelli from the Zoning Board of Appeals

timeline.summary: The board received Joe Monticelli's letter of resignation from the Zoning Board of Appeals, effective March 4, 2024, with Rende and DiGiacinto praising his long service (formerly on the Rec Board and years as ZBA chair). Motion, second, all in favor.

cases.name: Appointment of Edward Lashin to the Zoning Board of Appeals

timeline.summary: The board appointed Edward Lashin to the Zoning Board of Appeals for a term expiring December 31, 2029; Lashin had been interviewed January 7 (originally for Les Burkhammer's seat). Councilwoman DiGiacinto objected on process grounds — Monticelli's seat had only been open since March 4, and she wanted to give other interested residents the chance to apply and interview — and cast the lone 'no.' Hussain and others stressed the standard vetting/interview process had been followed. The measure carried on a roll-call vote: Berra aye, Hussain aye, DiGiacinto no, Rende aye (recorded as a split vote, DiGiacinto opposed).

cases.name: Appointment of Ray Rodriguez as Chairperson of the Zoning Board of Appeals

timeline.summary: The board appointed sitting ZBA member Ray Rodriguez as chairperson (at the pleasure of the board), with Rende noting Rodriguez has the full confidence and support of the ZBA. Motion, second, all in favor.

cases.name: Town Clerk Conference Request — NYS Town Clerks Association (Albany)

timeline.summary: The board approved Town Clerk Allison Simon's request to attend the New York State Town Clerks Association Conference in Albany, April 21-24, 2024, which she described as a learning and networking opportunity to enhance office skills. Rende emphasized the value of continuing education for all personnel. Motion, second, all in favor.

cases.name: Closings in Memoriam — Bill Canavan and Charity Lunder's Father

timeline.summary: The board closed with two remembrances: Bill Canavan, the town's hydrogeologist and founder/president of Hydro Environmental Solutions who worked closely on the Brynwood Summit project, who died suddenly at 59; and the father of Charity Lunder, who passed away at 103. DiGiacinto and Berra offered heartfelt tributes before the board adjourned.

cases.name: Town Sign Law Rewrite (Content-Neutral Update)

timeline.summary: Planner Adam Kaufman presented a draft rewrite of the town's sign law stripping content-based restrictions to conform with current case law, covering prohibited sign types (e.g., pole/pylon signs, murals), residential lot signage limits, right-of-way setbacks, and grandfathering of existing signs. The board raised questions about enforcement capacity (possibly needing a part-time code enforcement officer), uniform road-setback measurements, whether temporary/A-frame signs need permits, and a proposed community sign-location alternative to signs on private property. The board agreed to submit individual comments and have the town attorney review the draft before another work session.

cases.name: Board of Ethics Annual Update and Training Video

timeline.summary: Board of Ethics chair David Simons and member Brett Summers presented a new annual ethics-training video (shown to 11 of 13 boards/committees so far) and gave an annual update, including a 6-month recusal look-back rule, expanded disclosure requirements covering investment real estate, 19 of 25 disclosure forms returned so far, and a proposal to create a plain-language ethics guide booklet. Board members discussed adding compliance tracking to the boards/committees spreadsheet and clarified that recusal obligations extend to executive session.

cases.name: The Bristol at Armonk — EMS Condition Waiver / Site Plan Amendment Referral
cases.applicationType: waiver from application processing restriction law
cases.applicant: The Bristol at Armonk (E.V. Armonk LLC)

timeline.summary: The Bristol, an assisted-living facility, sought a waiver of the town's application-processing restriction law (triggered by a pending building-department summons/enforcement action) so it could go before the planning board to amend a 2012 site plan condition requiring an on-site EMT, which it says it can no longer legally staff under Department of Health rules. Board members pressed hard on why a decade-old compliance problem — non-emergency transport calls burdening the volunteer Armonk Fire Department/EMS — was only being addressed now that a summons had been issued, questioning the facility's overnight nursing coverage and the sincerity of its assurances. The board ultimately granted the waiver unanimously so the matter could proceed to the planning board, while directing that the planning board strongly urge the applicant to fund outside specialized legal counsel.

cases.name: North Castle Revolutionary War 250 Steering Committee — Formation, Mission Statement and Funding

timeline.summary: Following a work-session update from the 250th Anniversary Steering Committee co-chairs (including plans for a July 4, 2026 time capsule and restoration of historic markers at Miller Hill and Mount Misery, aided by a $50,000 county grant), the board formally established the North Castle Revolutionary War 250 Steering Committee, adopted its mission statement (amended to say 'understanding and appreciation'), appointed Councilmembers Milim and DiGiacinto as board liaisons, and allocated $40,000 for a commemorative video and historic marker restoration.

cases.name: 209 Bedford Banksville Road — Declaration of Restriction (FAR Transfer)
cases.applicant: Joseph and Celeste Claimant (property owners at 191/209 Bedford Banksville Road)

timeline.summary: A declaration of restriction tied to a planning board condition (de-restricting a roughly four-acre lot to permit an addition using transferred FAR from an adjoining lot) was tabled at Councilman Berra's request after he raised late concerns about missing indemnification language and an unclear condemnation-valuation clause. The supervisor asked that concerns be raised earlier in the future to give the applicant's attorney time to respond; Berra explained he had been ill and only saw the item in Friday's packet.

cases.name: Local Law to Amend Chapter 325 (Vehicle & Traffic) — Byron Brook Place No-Parking Zones and Banksville Road Stop Sign
cases.address: Byron Brook Place and Banksville Road, North Castle
cases.applicant: Police Chief Peter Simonson / Police Department

timeline.summary: Based on a memo from Police Chief Simonson, the proposed local law would create no-parking-anytime zones near the commercial buildings at Byron Brook Place (prompted by a since-departed telemarketing tenant's overflow parking) and add a stop sign with curb/curve reconfiguration on Banksville Road to calm traffic, similar to the School Street work in Coxsing. The board received the two memos and scheduled a public hearing for April 24, 2024. Officer Tom presented the field observations and temporary cone/signage trial. Members were broadly enthusiastic and asked mainly about unintended consequences for residents' overflow parking.

cases.name: Approval of 2023 Budget Transfers

timeline.summary: Previously deferred so the chair could examine it further, the 2023 budget transfers were brought back for approval. Berra said he was now comfortable after digging into it and consulting Councilman Hussain. The motion was made, seconded, and carried on a voice vote.

cases.name: Highway Equipment Purchases — Backhoe and 4-Ton Falcon RME Asphalt Hot Patcher

timeline.summary: Two highway purchases were approved by separate voice-vote motions: a backhoe (funded in the 2024 highway operating budget with roughly $20,000 of the excess paid from the highway fund balance) and a 4-ton Falcon RME asphalt hot patcher (paid from the CHIPS balance). General Foreman Jamie Norris was present; members had reviewed the materials and had no substantive objections.

cases.name: Film Permit — Netflix Productions 'Zero Day' at Townhouse Diner and North Castle Martial Arts
cases.address: 720 N. Broadway (Townhouse Diner) and 700 N. Broadway (North Castle Martial Arts)

timeline.summary: The board approved a film permit for Netflix to shoot the Robert De Niro political-thriller series 'Zero Day' on May 9, 2024, from roughly 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. Berra highlighted the excitement of a De Niro production filming in town. Attorney Roland confirmed he had resolved the earlier indemnification concern by substituting a modern indemnification agreement. The motion carried on a voice vote.

cases.name: Salary Increases for Certain Department-Head Non-Union Employees (Effective Jan 1, 2024)

timeline.summary: This item became the meeting's flashpoint. Councilwoman DiGiacinto moved to adjourn into an additional executive session, saying she had information not previously discussed; other members objected that the raises had already been vetted across three executive sessions over two months (one lasting three to four hours) and that her April 1 email hadn't identified new information. The board voted 4-0-1 (Berra abstaining) to hold the exec session at the meeting's end, met, and then reconvened. On the substantive vote to approve the raises, the motion carried 4-0 with DiGiacinto abstaining 'for the reasons I gave' (though she stated she supports the increases). A sharp exchange followed over whether the extra session was warranted and over meeting decorum/Robert's Rules.

cases.name: Receipt of Resignation of Anthony J. Futia (Water & Sewer Maintenance Worker) for Retirement

timeline.summary: The board received the retirement resignation of water and sewer maintenance worker Anthony J. Futia, effective April 30, 2024. Members thanked him for roughly 38 years of service, with Berra noting it would be the first time in memory that no Futia works in the water and sewer department. Motion to receive was made, seconded, and carried.

cases.name: Terminal Leave Payment for Peter Chardiello (Police Department)

timeline.summary: The board approved a terminal leave payment for Peter Chardiello of the Police Department on a voice vote, with members wishing him well.

cases.name: Conservation Board — Reappointment of Jane Black and Appointment of George Drapeau

timeline.summary: The board reappointed Jane Black (co-chair) and appointed George Drapeau to the Conservation Board, each for two-year terms expiring April 10, 2026, on separate voice votes. Berra, the board's liaison to the Conservation Board, praised the members' dedication and noted the board could use more volunteers.

cases.name: Consent Items — Warrant No. 7 Payments and Bluestone Lane Liquor License Renewal Notice
cases.applicant: Town Clerk / BL 575 Main NYLC (Bluestone Lane)

timeline.summary: The board approved the audit and payment of claims on Warrant No. 7 together with receipt of the New York State liquor license renewal notice for Bluestone Lane at 575 Main Street, Armonk, on a single motion. Some members briefly noted the town clerk report was missing from their tablets but were comfortable proceeding since it was posted online. A related terminal-leave and alcohol-permit notification were part of the clerk's items.

cases.name: Local Law amending Chapter 325 (Vehicles & Traffic) — Banksville Rd/Long Pond Rd stop sign and Byron Brook Place no-parking
cases.address: Banksville Road at Long Pond Road; Byron Brook Place, off Route 22
cases.applicant: Town Highway Department / Police (Lt. Tom Cormack, engineer Joe Tramelli, foreman Jamie Norris)

timeline.summary: Public hearing on a local law amending Chapter 325 to formalize a new four-way stop at the Banksville Road/Long Pond Road intersection (tightening turning radii to 40 ft and 25 ft, adjusting striping) and to add no-parking zones on Byron Brook Place near two office buildings off Route 22. Lt. Cormack and engineer Joe Tramelli presented the month-long temporary trial that drew positive resident feedback. A resident (Robert Sweeney) and neighbors spoke in support. The board opened and closed the hearing and adopted the law by unanimous voice vote, with the Highway Department to complete blacktop work within a few weeks after filing with the Department of State.

cases.name: Proposed dog park at North Castle Community Park
cases.address: North Castle (IBM) Community Park, between the platform tennis courts and the indoor sports center/new bathrooms
cases.applicant: Recreation & Parks Superintendent Matt Traynor / Park & Rec Advisory Board

timeline.summary: The board considered Superintendent Matt Traynor's memo requesting permission to pursue a dog park, a project recommended by the Park & Rec Advisory Board and ranked highly in a resident survey. Residents Molly and Juliette Meyer gave a detailed presentation on siting, safety signage, separate small/large-dog areas, and maintenance. The main debate was procedural: Councilwoman DiGiacinto urged a task force (vet, dog trainer, registration/tagging, insurance review) before proceeding, while Supervisor Rende and Councilman Milim opposed a task force as needless delay and favored a later work session instead. The board unanimously passed a motion directing Traynor to develop a preliminary site plan, logistics, and cost estimate in preparation for a work session.

cases.name: Recognition — Byram Hills Speech and Debate Team (NYS Forensic League Championship)

timeline.summary: The Supervisor recognized members of the Byram Hills Speech and Debate Team and their coach Thomas (Tom) Lustig/Andriello for their performance at the New York State Forensic League Championship, inviting the students to speak and take photos with the board. Students including Aidan Aldaya Lustig (state champion, original oratory) and Valentina Marino described their experiences. A ceremonial recognition with no formal vote.

cases.name: Public Safety — Vehicle Thefts and Police Response

timeline.summary: Multiple residents (Jen Clark of Banksville, James Chambers, and Joe Santulo of Smith Farm, whose car was stolen the prior night) urged the board to do more about a wave of brazen vehicle thefts, criticizing 'lock your cars' messaging and lack of visible patrols near the Connecticut border. The board discussed investing in license-plate readers and cameras (with WiFi-coverage cost hurdles), adding patrol officers (two new patrolmen hired), inter-municipal cooperation with Greenwich, and possible legislative remedies. The Supervisor, also a Banksville resident and past victim, committed to bringing a funded proposal to the full board; no vote was taken.

cases.name: Becky Kittredge Memorial Plaque (Gazebo)

timeline.summary: Resident Sue Miller followed up on a long-promised plaque honoring former council member Becky Kittredge for the town gazebo, noting it had been approved months earlier but not yet made or installed. The board recalled approving the plaque (changing wording to 'in honor of'). The Supervisor asked Councilwoman DiGiacinto, a close friend of Kittredge, to coordinate getting the plaque made and installed and to plan a small dedication ceremony. No formal vote.

cases.name: Petition to Amend RB Zoning for a Small Animal (Veterinary) Clinic at 150 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Petitioner (concierge small animal clinic); via Priscilla Whittington letter

timeline.summary: The board received a petition to amend the Roadside Business (RB) zoning district to permit veterinary use for a small 'concierge' animal clinic, along with letters from the petitioner and Planning Director Adam Kaufman. Town Planner Kaufman recounted that the town had prohibited vet use by code amendment in the early 2000s and raised concerns about the location given newly approved adjacent multifamily housing. Councilwoman DiGiacinto strongly opposed amending RB zoning, warning it could open the door to larger 24/7 conglomerate facilities; other members agreed an industrial district might be more appropriate. The board directed Kaufman to inform the applicant the petition was not favorably received and to research how comparable municipalities treat veterinary uses, with no formal vote.

cases.name: Farley Request to Acquire Town-Owned Land near 101 Old Hickory Way
cases.address: near 101 Old Hickory Way, Bedford (crossroad connecting Pine Ridge Road to Old Hickory Way)

timeline.summary: The board received an April 23, 2024 email from Stefana and Steve Farley regarding roughly 0.334 acres of town-owned property, with a question of whether they sought purchase or adverse possession. The board voted to receive the item and then referred it to Town Attorney Roland to review the file and neighboring property-owner letters and report back at the next meeting.

cases.name: Use of Roads and Parks — Jewish Board Cycle of Support Cycling Event (Sept 15, 2024)
cases.applicant: Jewish Board of Family and Children Services
