timeline.summary: The board considered and approved a request from the Jewish Board of Family and Children Services to use town roads and parks for a 'Cycle of Support' cycling event on Sunday, September 15, 2024. Councilwoman DiGiacinto reiterated the standard condition of no permanent road markings, requiring temporary directional lawn signs, which is now built into the police department application. Approved by motion and unanimous voice vote.

cases.name: Consent Judgment — ASQ LLC (Armonk Square) v. Assessor (Index 61748/2020)

timeline.summary: The board authorized the town attorney to execute a consent judgment in the tax certiorari matter ASQ LLC (Armonk Square) v. Assessor of the Town of North Castle, index 61748/2020. Town Attorney Roland explained the COVID-era equalization-rate decline had pushed the property's valuation out of sync; the settlement reduces the assessment to the appraised value going forward only, with all prior years discontinued at no reduction and current-year refunds waived. Adopted by motion and unanimous voice vote.

cases.name: Authorization of $40,000 for the North Castle Revolutionary War 250th Steering Committee
cases.applicant: North Castle Revolutionary War 250th Steering Committee

timeline.summary: The board acted to direct the previously committed $40,000 for the Revolutionary War 250th steering committee through the Parks and Recreation budget line, on Town Attorney Roland's advice that routing funds through a specific department eases state-auditor acceptance. The budget covers roughly $20,000 for a commemorative film/video and $20,000 for new and restored historic signage (including Mount Misery). Committee representative Ed described progress on signage restoration, the video script/filming, a logo, posters, and planned fall fundraising. The board approved instructing the town administrator to have finance make the appropriation by motion and unanimous voice vote.

cases.name: Probationary Promotion of Officer Stephen J. Vitolo to Detective
cases.applicant: North Castle Police Department (Chief Peter Simonson)

timeline.summary: Chief Peter Simonson requested board approval to promote Police Officer Stephen Vitolo, employed since 2015 and recently assigned to the Detective Division, to the budgeted position of Detective effective May 25, 2024. The chief cited Vitolo's investigative work (identifying a Romanian theft group), forensic and EMT training, and prior service awards. A motion was made and seconded and the board approved it unanimously by voice vote, followed by congratulations and photographs.

cases.name: Recognition of Exceptional Emergency Response — May 2 Route 22 Motorcycle Crash Rescue
cases.applicant: North Castle Police Department (Chief Peter Simonson)

timeline.summary: The chief recounted a May 2, 2024 incident in which a motorcyclist was ejected into the reservoir; Officer Bill Young, off-duty Westchester County Officer Mohammad Shandu, and two civilian Good Samaritans (Elijah Reeves and Steven Sikognagno) kept the victim's head above water and carried him up steep terrain, likely saving his life. The board recognized Officer Young and Officer Shandu (present) and thanked the Good Samaritans (who declined to attend). Every board member offered praise for the police force and the culture within the department; this was a recognition/commendation, not a vote.

cases.name: Vehicle Thefts, Police Staffing, License Plate Readers & Bail Reform Discussion
cases.applicant: North Castle Police Department (Chief Peter Simonson)

timeline.summary: At the supervisor's request the chief presented on a rash of larcenies from vehicles and stolen cars (50 in a decade locally, 40 with keys/fobs left inside; 216 countywide in Q1 2024), urging residents to lock cars and remove fobs. He detailed low staffing (31 officers vs. 44 in Bedford, 40 in New Castle), the department's two existing license plate readers, three more being installed (Nannyhagen/120, Rt 22/Banksville, Bedford-Banksville Rd), and a new state technology grant for additional readers and body cameras. Board members and the chief expressed strong frustration with 2020 bail-reform and raise-the-age laws, urging residents to lobby state legislators; no vote was taken. The board signaled support for funding more readers and increasing police staffing.

cases.name: Resident Request to Lower Speed Limit on North Greenwich Road (Route 433)
cases.address: North Greenwich Road / Route 433, Armonk (Nick's Pizza to CT border)

timeline.summary: Resident Dr. Salazar reported dangerous speeding on the 45 mph stretch of North Greenwich Road (Rt 433) near a special-needs center, with no sidewalks and children waiting for buses. Town Attorney Roland noted it is a state road, so the town can only request that the state lower the limit. The supervisor said he would have Town Administrator Kevin check with the chief on how a prior reduction (Rt 22/120 from 55 to 50) was achieved and advised the resident to write state representatives; treated as a referral/follow-up item, no vote.

cases.name: Summit Club (former Brynwood) — Convert Temporary to Permanent Special Use Permit
cases.applicant: Summit Club Partners, LLC (attorney Mark Weingarten, Del Bello Donnellan Weingarten Wise & Wiederkehr)

timeline.summary: The applicant sought to convert the golf club's temporary special use permit (last extended Dec 2023) to a permanent one, arguing it has completed SEQRA, rezoning, subdivision and the maintenance-facility detail the board requested, and needs a permanent permit to finance the approved 72-unit golf-course community. Neighbors (Garrett Kennedy of 2 Upland Lane, a letter from Bob Green read by Ed Woodyard, Jim Gavigan, Jill O'Dell) strongly opposed, citing early-morning machinery, noise/music events, light and litter, an increase from ~300 to 500 members, and proposed rentable cottages they likened to an Airbnb hotel. The board declined to close the hearing before a holiday weekend, discussed separating the financing-critical permanent elements from the temporary public-use element, and adjourned the hearing to a date certain of June 12 by unanimous voice vote.

cases.name: Summit Golf Club — Permanent Special Use Permit (Public Hearing)
cases.applicant: Del Bello, Donnellan, Weingarten, Weiss & Whitaker LLP (Summit Golf Club)

timeline.summary: Reconvened public hearing on a permanent SUP to operate the golf club, allow public use during residential construction, and govern members, cottages, camps, and events. Applicant offered concessions: cottages limited to members/guests (no Airbnb), 500 members kept consistent with the old Canyon Club, outdoor music cut off at 9 p.m. until an amenities building is built, compliance with the town noise ordinance, sunset of public golf at 12/31/29, and cottages capped at 20 bedrooms (10 cottages). Residents (Garrett Kennedy, Elon Keller, Andrew Lester, Alan Blum, Jim Gavigan) argued the SUP must separate the multi-year construction phase from post-construction, enforce the 25-foot landscape buffer, and not permanently codify 500 members/public golf that were never environmentally studied (study assumed ~350 golf members). After extended debate the board voted to close the public hearing with a 10-day written comment period and to hold a work session; members will submit comment points to planner Adam Kaufman within a week.

cases.name: 2023 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report & Audit Presentation

timeline.summary: The Bonadio Group (Michael Connolly, with partner Joe by video) presented the FY2023 audit, reporting an unmodified (clean) opinion consistent with prior years, no new GASB implementations, and no disagreements with management. The Town Justice Court agreed-upon-procedures report was still being finalized. Comptroller Abbas reported a strong fund balance (~$25.6M general/highway/library, ~$23M after committing ~$2.6M) and reminded the board that ARPA funds must be committed by year-end. Received as a presentation.

cases.name: Fund-Balance Transfer for Town Paving & Drainage Projects

timeline.summary: Authorization of a fund-balance transfer (~$1.2M) for three unbudgeted projects, chiefly a large Maple Avenue drainage/pipe-lining job plus additional paving (including the Windmill entrance and continuation of last year's lumberyard-area paving). Berra questioned whether much paving remained and asked for a detailed breakdown; Milim proposed authorizing now and getting the itemized breakdown at the next meeting. Approved on that basis, with staff to return with detail.

cases.name: Orchard Roll Road Subdivision — New Town Road Naming

timeline.summary: Recommendation of the Road Naming Committee for naming a new town road (with E-911 coordinator notification). Because the item arrived late and Saleem Hussain had not had time to review it with the committee, he moved to table it to a later meeting (June 26). Tabled.

cases.name: Wetland Mitigation & Construction Performance Bonds (Yip, CG East Lane/Turret, Whippoorwill Hills)
cases.address: 20 Green Valley Road; East Lane; 345 Main St / Log Cabin Way / Cider Mill, Armonk

timeline.summary: Routine bond actions on KSCJ Consulting recommendations: established a wetland mitigation bond and five-year monitoring bond for the Elaine Yip residential project (20 Green Valley Road); renewed construction performance and wetland mitigation bonds for CG East Lane LLC (Turret subdivision, East Lane); and released the landscape maintenance and two-year monitoring bonds for the Whippoorwill Hills HOA (345 Main Street) after confirmed plantings. All approved without controversy.

cases.name: Salt Domes Replacement/Repair — Emergency Authorization

timeline.summary: After discussion in executive session about structural issues with the salt dome(s), the board opted to proceed under an emergency authorization rather than a normal competitive bid. Approved conditionally on receiving a written letter from the Town Administrator/Highway detailing the work, cost, and the reasons the emergency justifies bypassing the bid process.

cases.name: Middle Patent Yard — Transfer Station Cleanup & Future Use (Discussion)
cases.address: Middle Patent Road (Water District No. 2 property, ~74 acres)

timeline.summary: Discussion, requested by DiGiacinto, of the cleanup and effective shutdown of the Middle Patent Yard as an informal transfer/compost station. Records showed the town paid ~$89,300 (2023) and ~$43,062 (2024) in dumping fees to remove accumulated material, plus ~8,000 cubic yards of highway millings and other prohibited material stored there. Rende and Milim argued the expanded use was never authorized (a 1990s-era resolution allows only leaf composting), posed environmental risk to a water source, and should end; DiGiacinto agreed cleanup was overdue but pressed for cost/impact data on lost yard-waste services before closing. A sharp exchange erupted between Milim and DiGiacinto over past positions. The board agreed to refer future use to the Conservation Board and Open Space Committee for a possible restoration/passive-recreation plan.

cases.name: Letter to Westchester County DA Miriam Rocca on Organized Auto Theft Rings
cases.applicant: Town Board (drafted by Councilman Milim, with Councilman Berra)

timeline.summary: Authorization for board members to sign a letter to Westchester County DA Miriam E. Rocca expressing grave concern over organized auto theft rings from Connecticut, citing high-speed chases (120+ mph), a rammed police car, and near-misses in downtown Armonk. The letter urges tougher prosecution, enhanced penalties, and resources, treating public-safety-impacting property crimes seriously (including bail and prosecutorial discretion for youthful vs. adult offenders). Adopted with minor edits (delete 'in particular,' pluralize 'communities,' accent on Berra's name).

cases.name: School, Camp, License & Wetland Bond Agreements (Consent Batch)
cases.address: Byram Hills schools; 14 Tall Woods Road, Armonk
cases.applicant: Byram Hills Central School District; NYS DEC; various

timeline.summary: Batch of routine authorizations for the Supervisor to sign: an MOU with Byram Hills for a School Resource Officer for 2024-25; summer camp use agreements/leases for Crittenden Middle School and Wampus Elementary (June-August 2024); an agreement with Kristen Youngers and Michelle Starr on a wetland mitigation bond at 14 Tall Woods Road; and an amendment to the NYS DEC license-issuing-agent agreement for hunting and fishing licenses. All approved without dissent.

cases.name: Memorial — Banksville Firefighter Preston Presley

timeline.summary: The board closed in memory of Preston Presley, a Banksville firefighter since 1971 and Banksville Community House coach, remembered as a genuine, community-minded person; condolences extended to the family and a letter to be sent. Meeting adjourned.

cases.name: Summit Club (formerly Brynwood) — Permanent Special Use Permit Work Session
cases.address: Route 22 / Upland Avenue, Armonk (Summit Club golf course)
cases.applicant: Summit Club / developer 'Jeff' (Metropolitan Golf Group), attorney Mark Weingarten

timeline.summary: Extended work session (no vote) to resolve outstanding conditions for the permanent special use permit covering the maintenance building, guest cottages and continued public golf-course use during construction of 73 residential units. The board reached near-consensus on most items: no-kitchen guest cottages limited to 20 bedrooms, a 9 PM amplified-music curfew until the amenities building is built (then the standard town noise ordinance, with events sited behind the building), public play ending October 2026 with yearly extensions, a 100-per-day day camp, deferred pickleball, water sampling per SEQRA findings, and Audubon certification applied for by April 1. The unresolved item was cottage ownership — the developer wants to pre-sell/lease units to members or passive investors placed in a management-company rental pool, while DiGiacinto and Berra worried about losing control; a no-public-posting restriction was floated as a compromise. Noise was the most contentious: Berra pushed for a stricter 'no distinctly audible noise beyond the property line' standard while the applicant and Milim argued that was legally unworkable and singled the club out. Formal action (Old Business B) was tabled for the town attorney and planner to codify the discussed terms into a resolution for a future meeting; the developer's late request to revive 88 (vs. 73) residential units was ruled out of scope.

cases.name: Levine Residential Project — Wetland Mitigation License Agreement & Bond, 11 Piping Brook Lane

timeline.summary: The board received the town engineer's (KSCG/J) recommendation to establish a wetland mitigation bond and a five-year monitoring/maintenance bond after an encroachment of roughly 23,680 sq ft into a conservation easement abutting the Levine property. It authorized the Supervisor to sign a license agreement (already signed by Levine and the abutting owner) allowing remediation work, with the Conservation Board having approved at least 2-for-1 mitigation. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Local Law to Prohibit Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)
cases.applicant: Town Board / Town Planner Adam Kaufman & Town Attorney Roland

timeline.summary: The board received a draft local law (with short EAF parts 1-3, a negative declaration and lead-agency intent) to strengthen the definition of 'public utility' so that battery energy storage systems cannot be claimed as public utilities and thus effectively prohibited, prompted by a dispute in neighboring Mount Kisco. The attorney flagged that a stronger version (modeled on the Town of Evans) should also define the different BESS levels. The board declared itself lead agency, referred the law to planning boards, and scheduled a July 24 public hearing. Extended discussion centered on fire risk (volunteer fire departments cannot safely fight BESS fires) versus renewable-energy benefits; the board consensus is that the risks currently outweigh the benefits.

cases.name: Road Naming — Israel Townsend Hill (Orchard Road Subdivision)

timeline.summary: The board considered the Road Naming Committee's first-choice recommendation to name a new road 'Israel Townsend Hill,' honoring a Quaker patriot buried on the property whose family were town founders. Hussain objected on principle to naming roads after individuals (citing unknown historical complexities and the risk of later reappraisal) and urged instead the committee's agreed second choice 'Townsend Farm Hill,' plus a referral to the Conservation Board and board guidance/liaison for future namings. Milim, Rende and Ed Woodyard resisted micromanaging the committee. Milim moved to adopt 'Israel Townsend Hill'; it passed 4-1 on a roll call with Hussain voting no. The board agreed to appoint Hussain as liaison to the Road Naming Committee.

cases.name: Offer to Purchase ~1 Acre Town-Owned Property Contiguous to 21 Windmill Road
cases.address: Lot 101.42-2-8, contiguous to 21 Windmill Road, Armonk

timeline.summary: The board accepted an offer (over $50,000, against ~$12,000 in back taxes) from the Bonistalls to purchase a landlocked ~1-acre town parcel acquired via in-rem foreclosure that the family had always believed they owned. The buyer will merge it into their residence lot and sign a covenant against future subdivision, avoiding a 'house behind a house' scenario; the Planning Board recommended the merger 5-0. Resolution adopted subject to permissive referendum. Berra supported this unique, sympathetic case but insisted the town develop a fair, transparent process (notifying residents/neighbors) for any future sales of town property.

cases.name: Westchester Joint Water Works Agreement — Water District No. 8 (Airport Campus Extension)
cases.applicant: Town / Westchester Joint Water Works (Town Attorney Roland, Superintendent Sal)

timeline.summary: The board approved and authorized the Supervisor to sign the Westchester Joint Water Works agreement creating Water District No. 8 (Airport Campus extension), described as the final piece securing a water supply for the airport campus property. Approved by voice vote; Supervisor thanked the attorney, Sal and others.

cases.name: Resignations and Committee Appointments

timeline.summary: The board received resignations from James Worthman (Highway Department, eff. June 25) and Alec Tobia (Police Department, eff. June 24) — with the Administrator confirming exit interviews are conducted — and made several appointments: Ed Woodyard and Nora Manueli to the Landmark Preservation Committee (three-year terms), and Elisa (surname uncertain), Doug Mancinelli and Kate Hall to the Open Space Committee. The Landmarks appointments were expedited to ensure a quorum could bless the wording of a memorial plaque for Becky (gazebo dedication targeted for an August summer concert). All approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Appointment of Police Officer Matthew Giannella
cases.applicant: North Castle Police Department (Chief Peter Simon)

timeline.summary: Chief of Police Peter Simon presented Matthew Giannella, a six-year NYPD transfer with EMT and field-training credentials, as a candidate for police officer effective July 13, 2024. Chief Simon detailed the background investigation and panel interview and recommended appointment in light of an upcoming retirement and a resignation. The board approved the appointment unanimously by voice vote and the Supervisor administered the oath of office.

cases.name: Westchester County Update — Deputy County Executive Ken Jenkins
cases.applicant: Westchester County (Deputy County Executive Ken Jenkins)

timeline.summary: Deputy County Executive Ken Jenkins, standing in for County Executive George Latimer, gave a mid-year update covering sales-tax stabilization, a new civil-service role easing NYPD transfers, airport flight-path concerns, free Bee-Line transit for the summer, and the Route 22 crosswalk in North White Plains. Board members asked about sales-tax impacts on town revenue and pressed for county help on the crosswalk, Health Department pool-permit delays, and roadside invasive-species trimming on county roads. No action taken; the exchange was informational and cooperative.

cases.name: Special Use Permit — Breezemont Day Camp (HZBR LLC)
cases.address: Breezemont Day Camp, Armonk (Cox Avenue / Rose Hill area)

timeline.summary: The board opened and held a public hearing on Breezemont Day Camp's application for a special use permit to operate a summer day camp, made permissible under a recently adopted local law allowing day camps as a special use in residential districts. Town Planner Adam Kaufman explained the planning board gave a positive recommendation, with the applicant to update plans for required 15-foot perimeter screening and parking, and to limit the PA system/bullhorn to emergencies only (no amplified music). No public spoke in opposition; board members praised the camp and its historic-building preservation. The hearing was closed with adoption of the resolution deferred until updated plans are submitted, targeting the July 24 meeting.

cases.name: Temporary and Permanent Special Use Permits — Summit Golf Club (formerly Brynwood)
cases.address: Summit Golf Club (formerly Brynwood), off Evergreen

timeline.summary: The board considered separate resolutions for a temporary special use permit (allowing public use of the golf course during residential construction, plus a proposed maintenance building) and a permanent special use permit for the Summit Golf Club. Debate centered on the town noise ordinance (Chapter 210): Councilman Milim analyzed the code and concluded it already suffices with the added 9 PM restriction, while Councilman Berra wanted a stricter 'not distinctly audible beyond the property line' standard (matching the town planner's original staff position) and a 350-member cap, calling the project speculative. Residents on Evergreen (via attorney Garrett) asked that no amplified sound exceed the property boundary. Amendments were added, including no valet parking on public streets and broader material-storage language. Both resolutions passed 3-1 (DiGiacinto aye, Milim aye, Berra no, Rende yes; Hussain absent), the permanent one adopted with conditions including a pending zoning variance.

cases.name: 2024 Standard Workday and Reporting Resolution (NYS Retirement System)

timeline.summary: The board adopted the annual standard workday and reporting resolution required by the New York State and Local Retirement System for elected and appointed officials not on hourly payroll, who must certify hours worked (via a three-month sample, recertified each four-year term) to participate. The Clerk explained the mechanics and it passed by voice vote. Members joked about the roughly $11.85/hour effective stipend.

cases.name: NYS DEC Water Quality Improvement Grant Application — Salt Storage Domes
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (Administrator Kevin Hay; grant writers)

timeline.summary: The board took two actions on a NYS Consolidated Funding Application / Water Quality Improvement Program grant to help fund demolition of the failing existing salt storage dome, installation of a new 72-foot-diameter dome, and re-roofing/repair of the second dome, at 75% grant with a 25% town match. It authorized the Supervisor and Town Attorney to sign the grant application and adopted a resolution of support, both by voice vote. Administrator Hay and the Supervisor clarified for a resident that one dome is in jeopardy of collapse and has been shut down.

cases.name: Purchase of 2024 Chevrolet Pickup Truck for Highway General Foreman
cases.applicant: Highway Department (General Foreman Jamie Norris); Sourcewell contract

timeline.summary: The board considered purchasing a 2024 Chevrolet pickup (via Sourcewell contract, from general fund balance) for Highway General Foreman Jamie Norris, whose current Ford Explorer would move into the shared fleet to replace a 20-plus-year-old vehicle no longer roadworthy. Councilman Berra objected that the unbudgeted purchase was a hefty expense, preferred a smaller/hybrid replacement, and wanted two weeks to explore alternatives; DiGiacinto, Milim, and Rende argued a pickup better fits a working foreman's duties and a fleet vehicle is needed regardless. After debate Berra withdrew his tabling request, and the motion carried on a roll call (DiGiacinto aye, Milim aye, Berra aye, Rende yes).

cases.name: Assignment of Legal-Services Retainer — Stevens Barone Riley & Lewis to Abrams Fensterman LLP

timeline.summary: The board considered authorizing the Supervisor to sign an assignment of the legal-services retainer from Town Attorney Roland Barone's firm to Abrams Fensterman LLP (effective Sept 1-Dec 31, 2024), as Barone merges his practice into the larger firm to create a long-term exit strategy while continuing to serve the town. Councilwoman DiGiacinto abstained, reading a prepared statement demanding full disclosure of Supervisor Rende's monetary and legal relationship with Abrams Fensterman and raising transparency and future-fee questions. Rende disclosed he has no monetary relationship but was represented by firm partner Bob Spolzino (whom he has known 30+ years) in his post-election absentee-ballot case, and stressed the merger was Barone's decision affecting all his municipal clients. Milim and Berra defended the process and criticized DiGiacinto for not raising concerns in executive session; the motion passed with DiGiacinto abstaining.

cases.name: Personnel Appointments, Resignation, and Liaison Assignment

timeline.summary: The board unanimously approved probationary appointments of Alex Cornev and Jeffrey Osciello as Highway Department road maintainers (eff. July 15) and Kaylee Castillo as an hourly library page (eff. July 11), accepted with regret the resignation of library custodian Felix Barrios (eff. Aug 2), and appointed Councilman Saleem Hussain (absent) as liaison to the Road Naming Committee, a role he had volunteered for. All passed by voice vote.

cases.name: Administrator Update — Route 128 Paving and Water/Sewer Generator RFP

timeline.summary: Administrator Kevin Hay reported that NYS DOT paving of Route 128 remains on schedule to begin at the end of July, with the town coordinating equipment staging, and that the Water and Sewer Department has an RFP out for annual servicing of emergency generators, due back at month's end for board adoption. Informational only.

cases.name: Supervisor's Disclosure Statement — Abrams Fensterman Campaign Contributions / Ethics

timeline.summary: Rende opened by reading an email/statement disclosing that, contrary to his answers at the July 10 meeting, he had received $1,000 campaign contributions each from Abrams Fensterman LLP, attorney Robert Spolzino and attorney Albert Pirro, after having voted to assign the town's legal-services retainer to Abrams Fensterman. He asserted he had satisfied the ethics code's after-the-fact disclosure requirement and that the Ethics Board chair (Brett Summers) was satisfied. DiGiacinto, who had abstained on the underlying vote, accused him of a possible ethics violation, of citing executive-session discussion, and of orchestrating the timing to silence her; a lengthy, hostile exchange revisited the matter at the end of the meeting. Milim and Berra defended Rende, criticizing DiGiacinto for 'playing politics on camera.' No vote; resident Ed Loberman also questioned the Ethics Board timeline (meeting set for Aug 5).

cases.name: Work Session — Community Preservation Plan / Fund (Open Space Committee, Conservation Board, Westchester Land Trust)

timeline.summary: The Open Space Committee (chair Carrie Kzak), Conservation Board (Adam Barnett) and Westchester Land Trust (VP Janelle Robbins) presented land-preservation tools, focusing on a community preservation plan and an associated fund financed by a small real-estate transfer tax on home sales above the county median. They cited North Castle's 2004 open-space bond and the recent 63-acre Erico acquisition, and requested board permission to work with town professional staff (planner, attorney, assessor, clerk) to gather data and run a resident survey. The board gave informal consensus/directive (no formal vote) to let the committees proceed with staff, with survey wording to be reviewed by Adam Kaufman, counsel and the board before release. Town planner Adam Kaufman flagged state-mandated plan requirements, TDR study, five-year updates and cost/benefit considerations.

cases.name: Probationary Appointment of Matthew Greevey — Police Officer
cases.applicant: North Castle Police Department (Chief Pete Simonson)

timeline.summary: Chief of Police Pete Simonson presented Matthew Greevey, a nearly nine-year NYPD officer (28th Precinct, Central Harlem) with prior Manhattan DA and National Guard experience, for a probationary police officer appointment effective July 27, 2024, tied to an upcoming retirement/transfer. The board unanimously approved the motion and Rende administered the oath of office, with a swearing-in and family photos. Sentiment was warm and celebratory.

cases.name: Q2 2024 Finance Report and ARPA Fund Commitment
cases.applicant: Director of Finance (Abbas, via Town Administrator Kevin Hay)

timeline.summary: The board received the Director of Finance's July 11 memo on second-quarter 2024 revenues, expenses, budget reports and bank reconciliation (presented by Kevin Hay in the comptroller's absence). Discussion centered on roughly $1.2 million in American Rescue Plan (ARPA) funds that must be committed/spent on eligible water-and-sewer infrastructure; Milim corrected the deadline to Dec 31, 2026 (not 2025). Rende and Milim stressed urgency to designate projects and 'not mess this up.'

cases.name: New Water Source, Water District 4 — DOH Approval and Authorization to Bid Construction

timeline.summary: Water & Sewer superintendent Sal reported that, after roughly eight and a half years of work (since 2016), the county Department of Health approved a new ~350-gpm well water source in Water District 4 and authorized going to bid for a prefabricated pump house, storage tank, booster/well pumps and DOH-required treatment, at an estimated ~$1.5 million. The board received the memo and adopted a motion approving the new source and authorizing the bid (hoped out to bid by late fall). Members tied the project to potentially committing ARPA funds, given water/sewer eligibility.

cases.name: Request to Purchase Town-Owned Property at 533-535 Main Street, Armonk (Frank Madonna Sr.)

timeline.summary: The board received a letter from Frank Madonna Sr. seeking to buy the ~0.06-acre town-owned former oil-depot parcel (acquired via in-rem foreclosure, ~$353K spent on tank cleanup), evidently to relocate two AFFH affordable units from the Byram condominium project there. A majority of the board expressed no interest in rezoning the tight, CB-Armonk-zoned parcel to residential or moving the affordable units off-site; Berra and Milim opposed on principle (AFFH integration and 'moral hazard' of bailing out a developer's economics), while DiGiacinto was more open/empathetic to the developer's post-COVID financial hardship. No action beyond receiving the letter; the board left the parcel's for-sale status essentially unchanged and discussed possible future parking uses.

cases.name: Resolution Supporting Renewal of Westchester County Airport Terminal Use Agreements
cases.applicant: Intermunicipal Airport Master Plan Task Force

timeline.summary: The board received the Airport Master Plan Task Force's July 10 request and adopted a resolution recommending Westchester County renew and reaffirm, with updates, the terminal use agreements of the commercial airlines operating at Westchester County Airport. Members praised town representatives Larry Ruozzi and Michael Pollack, noted the airport would not expand and that commercial flights are only ~15% of airport traffic, and adopted the resolution as the task force's document.

cases.name: Authorization of Leave of Absence — Employee No. 003937

timeline.summary: The board authorized a leave-of-absence request for employee number 003937, a Unit 2 contract requirement that the board authorize the extent of the leave. Routine; questions were answered offline and the motion carried unanimously.

cases.name: Tree-Hazard Safety on State Routes 128 and 22 — Letter to State Officials

timeline.summary: Prompted by a fatal accident (resident Kathy Tuziani killed April 4 when a tree fell on her car on Route 128) and a recent large branch fall near the same site that damaged power lines and caused a fire, the board discussed tree-hazard safety. Rende read a letter he was sending to Senator Mayer, Assemblyman Burdick and DOT officials urging proactive state tree assessment and trimming along Routes 128 and 22, and directed the highway foreman to trim aggressively with additional funds if needed. DiGiacinto conveyed the Tuziani family's plea for urgency. Kevin Hay noted state DOT paving on Route 128 begins around July 28.

cases.name: Probationary Appointment of Christopher Costa to Police Sergeant

timeline.summary: The Police Chief requested promotion of Officer Christopher Costa, a nine-year veteran, field training officer and EMT, to the budgeted, vacant patrol sergeant position effective August 17. The vacancy arose from Sergeant Sabatella's transfer to detectives following Detective Sergeant Finoteri's retirement. Board members offered congratulatory remarks praising Costa's finance background and record, and the probationary promotion was adopted by voice vote. Costa introduced his family, who were seated in the audience.

cases.name: Dedication of Armonk Gazebo to Becky Kidrich

timeline.summary: The Supervisor announced completion of a long-delayed dedication of the gazebo to former deputy supervisor and board member Becky Kidrich, prompted originally by resident Sue Miller. A plaque was made and mounted to a stone taken from Kidrich's former garden, with help from the Landmark Preservation Board, Parks & Rec Board, Highway Department, and the Supervisor's confidential secretary Josephine Egan. The unveiling was scheduled for the final outdoor gazebo concert on Saturday. This was an announcement, not a vote.

cases.name: Board of Ethics Statement Regarding Supervisor's Disclosure

timeline.summary: During public comment, Board of Ethics chair Brett Summers read a statement, authorized by the full Ethics Board at its August 5 meeting, correcting Supervisor Rende's July 24 work-session assertion that the Ethics Board had found he satisfied full disclosure requirements under Section 276. Summers stated he had only provided informal guidance on July 12 and could not speak for the board absent a formal meeting. No board action was taken; the item was informational/critical public comment.

cases.name: Local Law Amending Definition of Public Utility to Address Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)

timeline.summary: Following a public hearing closed in July, the board adopted a corrected local law amending the definition of 'public utility' to make clear that a battery energy storage system (BESS) is excluded and cannot claim public-utility status as a zoning loophole; only Level 1 and Level 2 systems are covered, with Level 3, Tesla chargers, solar, and cars excluded. The board adopted a negative SEQRA declaration and then the local law by voice vote. Members framed it as a temporary stopgap pending safety-technology maturation and discussed proactively identifying appropriate zones (avoiding sensitive environmental areas and areas without public water). The Town Attorney noted the state could still preempt via an override law.

cases.name: Basis of Design Report — Water Storage Tank, Booster Station, and Interconnection of Water Districts 8 and 4
cases.applicant: Water & Sewer Dept (Sal Misisti); D&B Engineers & Architects

timeline.summary: The board received (by voice vote) a July 2024 basis-of-design report evaluating interconnection of Water District 8 (New King Street / Airport Campus, sourced from Westchester Joint Water Works) with Water District 4 to secure an additional water source for downtown Armonk. Engineer Andrew Grundy presented the history and options; the selected approach eliminates the previously proposed 1-million-gallon Cooney Hill tank (saving ~40% of cost) in favor of drawing WJWW water on demand via a booster station on an Airport Campus parcel to be dedicated to the town. Members discussed grant pursuit, coordination timing with Airport Campus, rehabilitating the Miller Circle tank, and future extension toward Water District 2 and the high school. A member briefly moved to recuse over IBM being a District 4 customer but withdrew after the Town Attorney advised there was no special benefit to IBM.

cases.name: Armonk Close (former Lumberyard) — Sanitary Sewer Main Dedication and Maintenance Bonds — 154 Bedford Road

timeline.summary: The board acted on the town engineer's recommendations to accept dedication of the sanitary sewer main extension into Sewer District No. 2 and to establish related maintenance bonds for the Armonk Close project. Because the applicant had submitted only electronic drafts, the Town Clerk lacked original ink documents; the board approved the acceptances and bonds contingent on receipt of original documents satisfactory to the Town Attorney, to avoid delaying the building's certificate of occupancy. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Local Law Amending Chapter 336 (Water) — Hydrant Fees and Final Water Meter Reading Fee

timeline.summary: The board received a memo, short environmental assessment form, and lead-agency declaration for proposed local laws to collect hydrant fees in Water Districts 1, 2, 4, 5, and 8 via quarterly customer water bills, and a final water meter reading fee in all districts. Items one through four were approved by voice vote and a public hearing was scheduled for September 11, 2024. The Supervisor noted the change lets fire districts avoid budgeting for hydrant costs.

cases.name: IBM Community Park Turf Field Improvements — Floodplain Mitigation Approval

timeline.summary: The board considered a memo requesting approval to use a portion of the Water/Sewer superintendent's adjacent property to mitigate 100-year floodplain storage lost by adding up to 3 inches of fill and a short retaining wall behind the outfields of Fields 1 and 2 (a step toward possible artificial turf, which has not yet gone to bid). The plan was developed with NYSDEC. Councilwoman DiGiacinto sought to table and refer it to the Conservation Board, objecting that costs were unknown and the floodplain is environmentally sensitive; Councilman Milim countered that approval carries no cost and characterized the referral as an unnecessary delay tactic, leading to a sharp exchange. The approval passed 4-1 on a roll call, with DiGiacinto opposed.

cases.name: Hidden Oak Subdivision (Kevin McKenna) — Recommendation on Bond Amounts

timeline.summary: The board considered KSCJ/Kellard recommendations for construction performance bond amounts for the subdivision road, water main extension, and stormwater drainage system. Because no actual bonds had been drafted or reviewed by counsel, the board declined to establish the bonds and only received Kellard's recommended amounts, opting for a two-step process with the actual bonds to return on a future agenda. Received by voice vote.

cases.name: Purchase of Salt Spreader from Sourcewell Contract

timeline.summary: The board approved a request to purchase a slide-in salt spreader (with brine tanks) via Sourcewell contract, paid from the highway fund balance, repurposing a truck chassis whose dump body was damaged rather than discarding the truck. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Extension of Construction Performance Bond — Subdivision, 7 Pine Ridge Road

timeline.summary: On the town engineer's recommendation, the board approved a seven-year extension of a construction performance bond. A member had worried inflation over seven years would leave the original amount inadequate, but confirmed with JMC and Kellard that most construction is complete, so the existing bond is sufficient; a future bond reduction was anticipated. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Rosenthal Residence — Wetland Mitigation and Monitoring Bonds — 10 Creamer Road

timeline.summary: On the town engineer's recommendation, the board approved establishment of a wetland mitigation bond and a five-year monitoring/maintenance bond. The Town Attorney had seen a draft and confirmed no contingency was needed. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Armonk Cider and Donut Festival, Jamie's 5K Run, and Byram Hills Carnival — September 22, 2024
cases.applicant: Armonk Chamber of Commerce and Byram Hills Preschool Association

timeline.summary: The board approved the annual festival, 5K run, and preschool carnival for September 22. Discussion focused on road markings after a past event used non-removable paint; the board reaffirmed only non-permanent directional signage may be used and directed the Town Administrator to permanently update the permit form accordingly. Approved by voice vote with that modification.

cases.name: Alcohol Permit — Burke Neurological Institute Retreat at Lombardi Park
cases.address: Lombardi Park Pavilion and Clark Field

timeline.summary: The board approved an alcohol permit for a staff retreat on September 5, 6, and 12, subject to updated indemnity and release language matching corrections made on other recent permits to better protect the town. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Donation to Recreation and Parks Department from Byram Hills Preschool Association

timeline.summary: The board accepted, with appreciation, a donation to the Recreation and Parks Department. Approved by voice vote with no debate.

cases.name: Special Event Permit — Jewish Board of Family and Children Services Cycling Fundraiser at Congregation B'nai Israel
cases.applicant: Jewish Board of Family and Children Services

timeline.summary: As a late addition, the board received a special event permit application for a September 15 cycling fundraiser relocating its base to Congregation B'nai Israel (tents, breakfast/lunch, vendors) because of construction at Purchase College. The board received the application and scheduled a public hearing for September 11, 2024, pending fire, police, and town planner review. Councilman Milim recused himself as a member of the congregation.

cases.name: Annual Emergency Generator Service — Peak Power Systems (Water & Sewer)

timeline.summary: The board approved a proposal from Peak Power Systems for annual emergency generator service of 15 units in the Water and Sewer Department and authorized the Supervisor to sign. Treated as straightforward; approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Indoor Sports Facility Operation Agreement — CDC Development (Tech Track Sports Center)
cases.applicant: CDC Development Program Properties Inc. (Tech Track Sports Center)

timeline.summary: The board approved a proposal for continued operation of the indoor sports facility by CDC Development (Tech Track Sports Center) for another year and authorized the Supervisor to sign. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Probationary Appointment of Jake Terenzi — Maintenance Mechanic

timeline.summary: The board approved the probationary appointment of Jake Terenzi as maintenance mechanic effective August 15, 2024. The Supervisor praised Terenzi's trade skills, especially fence work that has saved the town outside-contractor costs, in support of the new maintenance department. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Probationary Appointment of Jim Loewenburg — Parks Groundsman

timeline.summary: The board approved the probationary appointment of Jim Loewenburg as parks groundsman in the Parks and Recreation Department effective September 3, 2024, by voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Annual $500 Stipend for Deputy Supervisor Jose Berra

timeline.summary: The board approved a $500 annual stipend for Deputy Supervisor Jose Berra, retroactive to January 1, correcting a reorganization oversight; the Supervisor noted past deputy-supervisor stipends ran much higher and that Berra himself asked only for $500. Councilwoman DiGiacinto explained her history of voting for and against such stipends and endorsed the modest amount as a fitting token of appreciation. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Court Office Personnel Attendance at NYS Magistrates Court Clerks Conference

timeline.summary: The board approved attendance by court office personnel (Nancy and Elizabeth) at the New York State Association of Magistrates Court Clerks conference, a budgeted expense. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Jewish Board Cycle for Support — Charity Ride Special Event Permit
cases.address: Congregation B'nai Israel, 2 Banksville Road, Armonk
cases.applicant: Jewish Board of Family and Children's Services (JBFCS)

timeline.summary: The board held a public hearing and approved a special event permit for JBFCS's annual 'Cycle for Support' charity ride (roughly 335 riders raising close to $1 million for children's mental health programs) on September 15, 2024, after event organizers described extensive coordination with the Armonk Fire Department and police, staggered rider waves, and shuttle/parking arrangements with the school district. No board or public objections were raised.

cases.name: Local Law Amending Water Code — Hydrant Fee and Final Meter Reading Fee Collection

timeline.summary: The board held a public hearing and adopted a local law amending Chapter 336 (Water) to let the town collect fire hydrant fees directly on quarterly water bills in Water Districts 1, 2, 4, 5 and 8, instead of billing fire districts (which then re-levied residents) — streamlining administration as new hydrants are added. A companion provision authorized a $50 final-meter-reading fee to recoup costs from the roughly 65-70 annual final reads done for home sales. Estimated added quarterly cost to a typical water customer is about $5.35.

cases.name: ARPA Fund Allocation Planning

timeline.summary: The board discussed how to obligate roughly $1.2 million in remaining COVID-era ARPA funds by year-end (to be spent by 2026), reviewing candidate projects including the downtown well development, the Verizon lot parking project, a highway vacuum truck, salt domes, dog park/turf fields, and North Castle library building safety upgrades. Town Administrator Kevin was asked to compile a project list, possibly designating multiple candidate projects for flexibility, ahead of the next meeting.

cases.name: Highway Department Relocation Feasibility Study (Architect Contract)

timeline.summary: The board debated and approved, over Councilwoman DiGiacinto's dissent, a contract with an architecture/planning firm (roughly $225/hour) to study relocating the highway department, including examining an unspecified alternative site discussed in executive session as well as the current yard. DiGiacinto argued the town should first gather highway foreman Jamie Norris's specific facility needs and questioned relying on a 17-year-old 2007 feasibility study before engaging a costly consultant, favoring an on-site landscaping alternative to screen the current yard from Route 22/128; Supervisor Rende countered that the decade-long delay, PESH complaints, and equipment-safety issues meant the town could not wait for 'perfect information,' leading to a sharp personal exchange between the two over past votes (turf fields, floodplain mitigation).

cases.name: Catalis Assessment Software Subscription Agreement

timeline.summary: The board approved an annual subscription, maintenance and support agreement with Catalis (formerly GAR/CAI) for new assessment software, after a board member asked the town administrator to more rigorously vet new municipal software purchases against Association of Towns resources and peer-municipality experience going forward, citing past payroll-software issues.

cases.name: Proposed Dog Park at IBM Community Park
cases.address: IBM Community Park, 205 Business Park Drive, Armonk
cases.applicant: Recreation & Parks Department (Matt Traynor) / residents Molly Weinrock & Juliet

timeline.summary: A work session on creating a roughly 105-by-90-foot fenced dog park at IBM Community Park, championed by Rec Superintendent Matt Traynor and residents Molly and Juliet Weinrock. The board debated rules, permits, fees, vaccinations, and a hold-harmless agreement, with the consensus favoring a streamlined single process run through the Town Clerk with no separate fee and no separate permit. Next steps: firm cost numbers, possible ARPA funding, a check with Town Planner Adam Kaufman on wetlands/buffer, and a later public hearing to codify rules and amend the dog code. No vote was taken.

cases.name: Police Appointments — Officers James Lucas & Reynaldo Pena; Promotion of Anthony Sabatella to Detective Sergeant

timeline.summary: Chief Simonson presented James Lucas (veteran NYC DEP police officer) and Reynaldo Pena (former NYPD/Danbury officer) for appointment as police officers, and Sergeant Anthony Sabatella for promotion to Detective Sergeant, all effective September 28, 2024. All three were approved unanimously (motions made and seconded, 'all in favor — aye') and the two officers were sworn in. The board noted the department is now at its budgeted officer strength for the first time in years.

cases.name: Order Calling Public Hearing — Summit Club Sewer District & Sewage Works Corporation

timeline.summary: The board adopted an order calling a public hearing for October 9, 2024 on the petition, map and plan to form the Summit Club Sewage Works Corporation and establish the Summit Club sewer district. Town Attorney Roland Barone explained the district would 'sit on a shelf' until needed and that the order required a roll-call vote under the Transportation Corporations Law, tied to the applicant's financing and imminent plant construction. Roll call passed 4-0 (Milim, DiGiacinto, Berra, Rende aye; Hussain absent).

cases.name: Proposed Amendment to Code Sec. 275-15.1 — Subdivision Notice / Address-Change and Mailing Reforms
cases.applicant: Town Board / Town Planner Adam Kaufman

timeline.summary: Discussion of amending the code so subdivision public-notice mailings alert neighbors that a subdivision could trigger an address change, prompted by resident Matt Sorrell whose address was changed (April Road / Whippoorwill) without his prior knowledge after a neighbor's subdivision. The board declined to reverse the change or use alphanumeric (A/B) addresses, deferring to Police Chief Simonson and county 911 on public-safety grounds. Councilman Berra also proposed switching notices to trackable certified mail, requiring a copy of the addressed envelope as proof, and widening the notification radius. The board voted unanimously to schedule a public hearing on the amended law for its first November meeting.

cases.name: Resolution — Non-Enforcement Grace Period on Address-Change Mailbox Requirement (Sorrell)

timeline.summary: To relieve the Sorrell family from the code's daily fine for not updating their changed mailbox address, the board adopted a resolution (unanimous voice vote) suspending enforcement until July 1, 2025, letting the school year end before the change takes effect. The neighbor whose subdivision caused the change is to be notified and given an additional grace period. Town Attorney Barone will draft the resolution with the specific names/addresses.

cases.name: Acceptance of $20,000 Armonk Lions Club Donation — Wampus Brook North Bridge Replacement & Fence
cases.address: Wampus Brook Park / Hunter Field, Armonk

timeline.summary: The board accepted a $20,000 Armonk Lions Club donation toward the Wampus Brook North bridge replacement and a fence along the Wampus Brook Park/Hunter Field border, approving the conditions in the donation letter (including a commemorative plaque). The donation offsets part of the ~$56,000 bridge cost and funds fence material, with removable panels for the Folderol festival; town labor is to be used. DiGiacinto raised process questions about whether the fence sits on town or school property and possible union concerns, which counsel addressed. Adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: Waiver of Permit Fees — Congregation B'nai Israel October 7th Memorial Vigil

timeline.summary: The board approved waiving permit fees for a memorial vigil for the victims of October 7th at the Wampus Brook Park gazebo, consistent with past practice of waiving such fees. Approved by unanimous voice vote.

cases.name: License Agreement — 4 Trip Lane (Right-of-Way Driveway Gate and Stone Masonry Piers)

timeline.summary: The board approved a single license agreement (for both spouses, Anna and David) covering the right-of-way area by the driveway entrance gate and stone masonry piers at 4 Trip Lane. A duplicate agreement mistakenly on the agenda was excluded. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Town Administrator / Council Updates — Route 128 Paving, Salt Domes, Route 22 DOT Meeting

timeline.summary: Closing updates: Route 128 paving is essentially complete (final checklist items remaining) and salt-dome construction is expected to begin the first week of October. Supervisor Rende noted a late-September/early-October DOT meeting on lower Route 22, with attendance limited to avoid an Open Meetings Law quorum; other members were invited to submit written comments. The board also flagged a property-maintenance/mowing issue and offered condolences to Kevin Hay on the loss of his brother.

cases.name: Summit Club Sewage Works Corporation & Standby Summit Club Sewer District

timeline.summary: Public hearing on the petition, map/plan/report to form the Summit Club Sewage Works Corporation and establish a standby Summit Club Sewer District serving the approved residential golf-course community, whose privately owned sewage plant must be structured under NY Transportation Corporations Law so the town can take over only in the event of a default. After extensive questioning driven by the town's water/sewer superintendent and clarifications from town counsel and the applicant's engineer, the board closed the hearing and, by roll-call votes recorded 4-0 (Milim, Hussain, DiGiacinto, Rende aye), consented to form the Sewage Works Corporation and adopted the resolution establishing the standby district. The board agreed to increase the operation-and-maintenance bond term from at least five years to at least ten years. The stock escrow, O&M, and easement agreements were held for redline revisions to be presented at the next meeting.

cases.name: Tabled matter(s) pending map/plan/report redline revisions

timeline.summary: Following the minutes, the board tabled a matter (and its associated items) after discussion with the town attorney and Councilman Berra pending redline changes to the documents, with Councilman Hussain abstaining. A related item (referred to as Item B) requiring changes to a map/plan/report was likewise tabled by motion. Counsel indicated the revisions would be worked out at a Monday meeting already scheduled.

cases.name: Local Law amending Chapter 146 (Dogs) — dog park rules and regulations

timeline.summary: The board considered receipt of a local law adding dog-park rules and regulations to Chapter 146 and scheduled a public hearing for November 20, 2024. Councilwoman DiGiacinto disclosed via a letter that the project's lead proponent, Molly Meyer, is a non-resident (Mount Pleasant), arguing transparency required acknowledging the board was acting on a non-resident's request; other members strongly pushed back, calling residency irrelevant to a community benefit and defending the project. Members cited the 2022 Parks & Recreation survey (dog park the second-most-requested project) and a low estimated cost (~$25,000-$30,000 per Rec Superintendent Matt Traynor). The exchange grew heated over whether DiGiacinto's letter implied wrongdoing; the board ultimately agreed to receive the law, schedule the hearing, and send a message welcoming Meyer and her daughter's continued involvement.

cases.name: Wetland mitigation bond, monitoring bond & cash bond agreement — Guadalupe Real Estate residence, 41 Mead Road
cases.applicant: Marcella Yeps & Nicholas Quadros / Guadalupe Real Estate NY, LLC

timeline.summary: On the town engineer's (KSCJ Consulting) recommendation, the board approved establishment of a wetland mitigation bond and a five-year monitoring and maintenance bond for the residence at 41 Mead Road, then separately approved the related cash bond agreement (item G1). The agreement had been submitted late and was not properly posted on the agenda; the Supervisor used the occasion to reiterate the rule that agenda items be finalized at the Wednesday agenda meeting to avoid last-minute errors. Both approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Wetland mitigation bond & five-year monitoring bond — Fort Trip Lane residence

timeline.summary: On the town engineer's (KSCJ Consulting) recommendation, the board approved establishment of a wetland mitigation bond and a five-year monitoring and maintenance bond for the residence project at Fort Trip Lane. Approved by voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Retroactive filming permit — Miracle-Gro commercial

timeline.summary: The board granted retroactive approval of a filming permit for World War 7 to film a Miracle-Gro commercial on October 8, 2024. Because the location is on a narrow road, the police reviewed and approved traffic arrangements before the expedited shoot; the full $3,000 fee (including the $1,000 application fee) was confirmed paid. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Friends of Frosty — Frosty Day parade & tree lighting road/park use
cases.address: Wampus Brook Park / Wampus Brook Park South

timeline.summary: The board approved the Friends of Frosty's request to use town roads and Wampus Brook Park (and Park South) for the annual Frosty Day parade and holiday tree lighting on Sunday, December 1, 2024. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Alcohol permit — Katonah Classic Stage opening-night reception
cases.address: Whippoorwill Hall, 19 East Whippoorwill Road, Armonk

timeline.summary: The board approved an alcohol permit for Katonah Classic Stage to hold a reception on the opening night of its play at Whippoorwill Hall on October 25, 2024. Members praised the theater as a community asset that helps drive the local economy, noting strong ticket sales. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: License agreement — Saglimbini, 2 Trip Lane right-of-way encroachment

timeline.summary: The board approved a license agreement with Martha Saglimbini regarding the right-of-way area at 2 Trip Lane for driveway entrance gates and stone masonry piers, and authorized the Supervisor to sign; it is identical to an agreement previously approved for 4 Trip Lane. The Supervisor urged residents to check with the planning department before erecting improvements that may fall within an easement. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Resignations — library clerk and Board of Assessment Review member

timeline.summary: The board accepted the resignation of Cheryl Cheramella as library clerk at the North Castle Public Library (effective October 2, 2024) and the resignation of Stuart Breezeblatt from the Board of Assessment Review (effective September 30, 2024). Both accepted by voice vote.

cases.name: 2025 Tentative Town Budget

timeline.summary: The board received the tentative 2025 town budget and scheduled its public hearing for November 20, 2024.

cases.name: John A. Lombardi Park Water District Extension
cases.applicationType: map, plan and report / water district extension
cases.lastStatus: received; public hearing anticipated December 2024 or January 2025

trajectory.status: received; public hearing anticipated December 2024 or January 2025

timeline.status: received; public hearing anticipated December 2024 or January 2025
timeline.summary: The board received an updated map, plan and report for extending the water district to Lombardi Park, which was redesigned to run the service line up School Street (passing seven residences) rather than across Byron Hills' property, after Byron Hills had already granted an easement for the original routing. The board directed staff to send an informational letter to the affected seven residents, explaining they will owe future debt-service costs regardless of whether they connect, ahead of scheduling a public hearing once health department plan approval is received.

cases.name: Town Pool Filter Media Replacement
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (Recreation and Parks)

timeline.summary: The board approved Superintendent Matt Trainor's request to replace the town pool's sand/gravel filter media (never previously changed) via Nuclear Swimming Pool Service LLC, using a fund-balance transfer, to avoid a Department-of-Health-recommended delay risk to next season's pool opening; a board member asked staff to arrange a town roll-off container and proper disposal for the estimated 20-30 yards of removed material.

cases.name: Eagle Ridge (North Castle Drive) — Easements and Community Benefits Agreement Compliance
cases.address: North Castle Drive, Armonk (former IBM property)
cases.applicant: Mad Madonna Armonk LLC / IBM (International Business Machines Corporation)

timeline.summary: The board approved a package of agreements for the Eagle Ridge residential subdivision on the former IBM North Castle Drive property: an easement dedication for Road A, a utility easement for a new water main, and an access/utility agreement between the developer, IBM and the town, plus received a declaration of covenants and restrictions ensuring at least 60% of housing units include four primary bedrooms (satisfying condition 10 of the master site plan resolution). The developer's representative confirmed no property transfers triggering the project's Community Benefits Agreement (CBA) payment obligation had yet occurred. The board also discussed coordinating snow-plowing logistics between the town highway department, IBM, and the future homeowners' association, and was told 2025 is the target for breaking ground.

cases.name: Local Law amending Code Section 275-15.11 — subdivision public-hearing notice (potential address changes)

timeline.summary: A public hearing was opened on a local law adding language to subdivision public-notice requirements advising that a subdivision may result in future address changes in the surrounding neighborhood, prompted by a resident upset over a forced renumbering (21/23 Whippoorwill Road). The Town Planner explained the added sentence; Councilman Berra argued the notice should be broader (more affected owners, more specificity about contiguous addresses, an informal police referral, and a move away from certificates of mailing to trackable certified mail). The planner and board explained a general notice at the start of the process can only say so much. The board closed the hearing, adopted the negative declaration, and adopted the local law, all by voice vote.

cases.name: North Castle Historical Society — Mount Misery marker wording
cases.applicant: North Castle Historical Society (Tom Rice et al.)

timeline.summary: The Historical Society presented proposed language for a new metal marker at Mount Misery (funding previously approved; sign to cost under $3,500 from an Ohio vendor). The text recounts two historical accounts of the name's origin, including one describing Huguenots slaughtering Native Americans. Councilman Hussain raised concern the killing language could feel 'assaulting' to Native American readers and suggested framing it as differing historical accounts rather than a 'disagreement'; Councilman Milim echoed the 'differing accounts' wording. The board voted to approve the wording with the suggested edits, to be redistributed to the board.

cases.name: Byram (Armonk) unit-owner petition — possible relocation of AFFH units
cases.address: Byram, Route 128 / Old Mount Kisco Road, Armonk

timeline.summary: The board formally received a petition from market-rate condo owners at the 16-unit Byram (2 AFFH units) asking the town to allow the two affordable units to be relocated off-site, triggered by a certificate-of-occupancy compliance issue and concern that planned HOA amenities would raise common charges. An extended policy debate followed on AFFH affordability rules, the risk of developer 'gaming,' one-off exceptions versus amending the local law to require a 1.5:1 or 2:1 replacement ratio, on-site embedding versus clustering, and small-complex divisiveness. The board received the petition (administrative) and, over Berra's objection, four members agreed to schedule a future work session; no substantive decision was made.

cases.name: Order calling public hearing (Dec 11, 2024) — Water District No. 4 School Street extension

timeline.summary: The board adopted an order calling a public hearing on December 11, 2024 to consider extending Water District No. 4, to be known as the School Street extension. Because it is an order requiring a district action, it was adopted by roll call, 5-0 (Berra, Milim, DiGiacinto, Hussain, Rende all aye).

cases.name: Authorization to open bank account — North Castle 250th anniversary committee
cases.applicant: North Castle 250th steering committee / Finance Director

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Director of Finance to open a dedicated JP Morgan Chase account for the North Castle Revolutionary War 250th anniversary committee to receive and record donations (to be named 'North Castle 250th'). The finance office will control the account and issue tax-deductible donation receipts; the committee anticipates donations and commemorative-item sales. A similar approach was used for the 1976 bicentennial. Adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: Kent Place parking lot (former Verizon property) improvements — bid award to Tony Casale Inc.
cases.address: Kent Place / Kent Street, Armonk (former Verizon property)

timeline.summary: The board awarded the Kent Place parking-lot (former Verizon property) improvement bid to Tony Casale Inc. and authorized the supervisor to sign. Members discussed dedicating a portion of roughly $1.2 million in ARPA funds (which must be committed by year-end) to this project plus equipment purchases such as a senior bus and a plow/dump truck, with a separate ARPA-allocation resolution to be prepared before the next meeting. Councilwoman DiGiacinto recused herself due to her family's ownership of commercial property on the west side of Main Street. Adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: 2025 agreement with Verity Electric — traffic signal and flashing beacon maintenance
cases.address: Bedford Road & Maple Avenue; four flashing beacons on Route 22

timeline.summary: The board authorized the supervisor to sign the 2025 agreement with Verity Electric for maintenance of the Bedford Road/Maple Avenue traffic signal and four Route 22 flashing beacon assemblies. The administrator noted Verity has done this work for the town for about 20 years and there are few providers. Supervisor Rende disclosed, for the record, that the Verity principal donated to his election campaign, and later praised Verity for donating labor and materials after the town's eagle statue was vandalized. Adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: Sewer District No. 2 sludge-hauling agreement extension — Spectra Serve Inc. (2025)

timeline.summary: The board approved extending the Sewer District No. 2 sludge-hauling agreement with Spectra Serve Inc. for the 2025 fiscal year. Treated as self-explanatory; adopted by voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: PBA successor contract — stipulation agreement (Jan 1, 2024 – Dec 31, 2027)

timeline.summary: The board authorized the supervisor to sign a stipulation agreement between the North Castle PBA and the town for a successor contract covering January 1, 2024 through December 31, 2027. Adopted by voice vote without discussion.

cases.name: Personnel items — Ficaris appointment, Libertari vacation carryover, Stevens resignation
cases.applicant: Town departments (Building Maintenance, Highway, Water & Sewer)

timeline.summary: The board approved the probationary appointment of Austin Ficaris to maintenance mechanic in the Building Maintenance Department effective November 14, 2024; approved a request by Rocco Libertari (Highway Department) to carry over 2024 vacation days; and received the letter of resignation of Anthony Stevens (Water and Sewer Department) effective October 15, 2024. All handled by voice vote.

cases.name: Receipt of North Castle Fire District No. 1 (North White Plains) 2025 budget
cases.applicant: North Castle Fire District No. 1 (North White Plains)

timeline.summary: Pulled from the consent agenda (item C), the board received the North Castle Fire District No. 1 adopted 2025 budget (~$700,000+). Supervisor Rende detailed his concerns: the district first sent a two-page 'summary,' a zero fund-balance line despite past unremitted hydrant fees, a certification referencing 'estimates,' and a response that the full budget must be FOILed. He contrasted it with Armonk's detailed submission and cited the state comptroller's accounting manual. Milim shared the concern that being told to FOIL implied a withheld document; the Town Attorney said any worksheets are FOIL-exempt and recommended asking the state comptroller to review sufficiency. DiGiacinto was uncomfortable airing it publicly and defended the volunteer firefighters. The board received the budget 'as presented' (a mandatory administrative appendage to the town budget) by voice vote, with further discussion to follow.

cases.name: 2025 Town and Special District Preliminary Budgets

timeline.summary: Finance Director Abbas Sura presented a roughly $42.6M total 2025 budget (3.2% higher than 2024), with the general fund about 65% and highway about 21%, funded partly by ~$4M of fund balance and a total tax levy near $24.2M. The budget delivers a 0% tax increase — the fourth consecutive year — and stays about $158K under the NYS tax cap. The board opened the public hearing but deliberately kept it open, adjourning to its December meeting for adoption. Extensive board discussion covered budgeting 'to actual,' a smooth 'glide path' toward moderate future increases, the ~$25M fund balance, AAA bond rating, ARPA funds (~$1.1-1.2M), and upcoming capital projects (turf fields, pool, 333 Main, library).

cases.name: Local Law — Amend Chapter 146 (Dogs) to Add Dog Park Rules and Regulations
cases.address: Community Park (near town floodplain), North Castle
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (Recreation & Parks; drafted with resident Molly Meyer)

timeline.summary: Public hearing and adoption of a local law codifying North Castle dog park rules and regulations (Chapter 146). Residents Molly and Juliet Meyer presented supportive research; the board added a wording change to the hold-harmless/indemnification agreement (narrowing the gross-negligence carve-out) at Councilman Berra's suggestion. Debate centered on Councilwoman DiGiacinto's requests — a permit/application form capturing dog-license numbers, initially restricting use to North Castle residents, and clearer enforcement/contact info — which the majority viewed as unnecessarily burdensome versus a practical honor-system approach plus a posted contact number. The board closed the hearing, adopted the negative declaration, and adopted the local law by voice vote; the Town Attorney confirmed no roll call was required. DiGiacinto voted yes despite her stated reservations.

cases.name: Release of Guarantee Bond — Santucci Construction, 25 Orchard Drive

timeline.summary: The board received a recommendation from KSCJ Consulting Engineers and released a guarantee bond from Santucci Construction for 25 Orchard Drive. Motion made and seconded, no questions, adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: 2025 NYS Association of Towns Membership and Voting Delegate Designation

timeline.summary: The board approved 2025 membership in the New York State Association of Towns and designated the Supervisor as the town's voting delegate at the February annual meeting. Members asked the Supervisor to report back informally on the votes; staff and members were encouraged to attend sessions of interest. Adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: Engineering Services Agreement — WSP USA, Long Pond Dam Safety Certification

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to execute a professional engineering services agreement with WSP USA for coordination of P&G forms for the dam safety annual certification and review/update of the emergency action plan for Long Pond Dam, as required by NYS DEC. Councilman Jose Berra recused himself (a party had spoken to him in his prior capacity as a lawyer before he joined the board). Adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: Agreements — Clove Road Park Baseball Fields (Survey and Engineering)
cases.applicant: TC Merits Land Surveyors; KSCJ / Kellard Consulting

timeline.summary: Two related items for Clove Road Park baseball field renovation. The board authorized the Supervisor to sign the TC Merits topographic survey agreement (adopted). The second item — a ~$62,200 Kellard/KSCJ engineering agreement — was tabled after the Parks & Rec Advisory Board and Councilman Milim objected that its scope covered a potential seven-figure drainage project the board is unlikely to pursue; the board will get the survey first, then scale back Kellard's scope for a biddable field-releveling project (est. ~$100K-300K). Rec Superintendent Matt Traynor and Kensico Little League volunteer Bob provided background; drainage/flooding at the low-lying field was debated.

cases.name: Term Adjustment — Angelina Colombo, Assessment Review Board

timeline.summary: The board corrected the five-year term date of Angelina Colombo on the Assessment Review Board to now expire September 30, 2026, fixing prior incorrect information (confirmed with the Town Attorney and Town Clerk). Adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: Board of Ethics 2024 Recommendations to Amend the Code of Ethics

timeline.summary: Board of Ethics Chair Brett Summers presented five reform recommendations: barring town board members, department heads and consultants from holding office/voting positions in political parties; requiring recusal (not just disclosure) when aggregate campaign contributions exceed $500; making failure to file campaign-finance disclosures a code violation; a new mirror disclosure obligation on applicants; and barring members of land-use boards from appearing on behalf of third parties before town boards. The board broadly supported the package but debated the constitutionality of the political-party-membership ban, whether the applicant-disclosure rule should also cover town contractors, how applicants would be educated, and the effective date. No vote was taken; the board directed liaison Berra to work with the Ethics Board, receive a revised law at the Feb 12 meeting, and schedule a public hearing.

cases.name: 2025 Organizational/Reorganization Agenda — Designations, Policies, Appointments

timeline.summary: The board adopted its annual reorganization items by voice vote: designating depositories (adding new bank PPAC/PCSB alongside JP Morgan Chase and others), payment/ACH authorizations, appointment of Jose Berra as Deputy Supervisor, liaison and committee appointments, legal-notice policy (Journal News and Examiner), the second-and-fourth-Wednesday 7:30 PM meeting schedule, 70-cents-per-mile reimbursement, the 2025 master fee schedule, and various financial and workplace policies. All passed unanimously; a clerical date error (January 12, 2023) on several pages was noted for correction. DiGiacinto voted for the workplace-violence and sexual-harassment policies while stating they have flaws that Administrator Kevin is drafting improvements for.

cases.name: 2025 Legal Services Agreement with Abrams Fensterman LLP

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign the 2025 legal-services agreement with Abrams Fensterman LLP, the firm to which Town Attorney Roland moved in 2024. Supervisor Rende disclosed, for public knowledge, that several members of the firm made campaign contributions to his 2023 campaign. The board praised the move as beneficial (retaining Roland's expertise plus a full firm behind him) and adopted the agreement, along with separate 2025 agreements for justice-court counsel (Patrick Bliss), labor counsel (Bond Schoeneck & King), engineering/stormwater services (KSCJ Consulting), ambulance and fire-protection districts, and financial advisory services (Capital Markets Advisors).

cases.name: Establishment of Water District No. 9

timeline.summary: The board received the WASP Engineering Group report and environmental assessment form for proposed Water District No. 9 and adopted an order calling a public hearing for February 12, 2025 (roll call 5-0). Counsel Roland and Water/Sewer Superintendent Sal explained that the district cannot be finalized until Westchester Joint Water Works confirms served parcels and WASP prepares an amended as-built report (fewer hydrants and uncompleted meter chambers than originally reported, because the funded work ran out of money). Superintendent Sal flagged the need to verify that installed hydrants are active for fire protection and that a New York City water agreement is in progress.

cases.name: Resolution Urging the State to Pause the Central Arraignment Plan

timeline.summary: The board adopted a resolution urging the New York State court system to pause a centralized (White Plains) arraignment plan, subject to minor text corrections to be sent by Milim. Supervisor Rende argued the plan imposes heavy costs and manpower burdens (two officers per prisoner transfer), pulling police off the road, and criticized it as another erosion of local authority. Former Justice 'Sue' spoke against it on justice-administration grounds (loss of one-on-one interaction with defendants). The resolution passed by voice vote.

cases.name: Resolution Supporting Hudson River Valley Greenway Trail Grant — Wampus Brook Park Greenway Trail
cases.address: Wampus Brook Park / 128 Main Street, Armonk
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (Town Planner Adam Kaufman)

timeline.summary: The board adopted a resolution supporting a 50% Hudson River Valley Greenway trail grant to build an 8-foot multi-use path (with boardwalk over wetlands) from Wampus Brook Park toward the pool and ultimately the Sands Mill development, reviving a 2007/2008 Kellard-designed plan. Planner Kaufman explained the grant is due at month's end and adoption is non-binding but needed to proceed; cost estimates are pending. Members were enthusiastic, framing it as safer connectivity for children and a highly rated park-and-rec priority, though DiGiacinto reiterated her call for a townwide capital-improvement plan. The resolution passed by voice vote.

cases.name: Salary Increases for Department-Head / Non-Union Employees (Merit-Based)

timeline.summary: The board approved merit-based salary increases for department-head and non-union employees. The item passed, but Councilwoman DiGiacinto — while voting for the raises — objected to the methodology, arguing there was no matrix and employees were never told the expectations, and urged a better process next year.
