After lengthy debate about fairness, publicity, and whether granting it could 'taint' or delay the process, the board voted to grant the extension, publicize it widely (website, press, bulletin board, supervisor update), and inform anyone who submits on Sept. 22 that additional time is available. The item became a proxy for a broader fight over how open the RFEI process had been. Passed unanimously.

cases.name: 333 Site / Eminent Domain and Municipal Facilities Direction

timeline.summary: In response to resident questions, the Supervisor explained the town is not currently moving forward on 333 and has not taken the next step on eminent domain, because the community wanted alternatives explored. He recounted how a resident-plus-professional committee was considered but abandoned over cost and composition concerns, leading instead to the free RFEI approach. He stressed that any ultimate direction would go to a voter referendum. No action taken.

cases.name: Daughters of Liberty Legacy Letter — Historic Designation of Two Mount Misery Parcels; Referral to Landmark Preservation Committee
cases.applicant: Cynthia Abbott Coffee, Daughters of Liberty Legacy

timeline.summary: The board received a letter from Cynthia Abbott Coffee requesting historical designation of two town parcels on Mount Misery and referred the matter to the Landmark Preservation Committee (LPC). Members confirmed the LPC referral was included and noted the requester may later make a presentation. Received and referred unanimously.

cases.name: Payment Requisition #1 to Populito Construction — Water District 4 New Well Building Site Work

timeline.summary: The board approved payment requisition #1 to Populito Construction for site work at the Water District 4 new well building; the Supervisor noted the work is progressing well. Discussion with Water/Sewer superintendent 'Sal' pivoted to repurposing a town-owned 3,000-gallon fuel tank (from the old tennis-bubble mechanicals at Community Park) for a water-facility generator rather than leaving it unused. Approved.

cases.name: Receipt of Letter from Patricia Ann Colombo (dated August 10, 2025)

timeline.summary: The board voted to receive a letter from Patricia Ann Colombo dated Aug. 10, 2025, with no substantive discussion. Received.

cases.name: Film Permit — Patch Bay Presence Productions LLC, 15 Middle Patent Road

timeline.summary: The board approved a film permit for Patch Bay Presence Productions LLC to shoot a feature film at 15 Middle Patent Road on Sept. 30–Oct. 1, 2025. Members confirmed the PDF was reviewed and off-site parking arranged; police (Tom McCormick) coordinated staging at the Summit Club as before, with the production described as considerate neighbors previously. Approved.

cases.name: Autism Science Foundation Rides Fair Charity Cycling Event — Town Road & Pool Parking Lot Use
cases.address: Town road and pool parking lot

timeline.summary: The board approved a request from the Autism Science Foundation to use a town road and the pool parking lot for a charity cycling 'rides fair' for autism research on Oct. 4, 2025. The application was amended to bar road spray-paint marking (signs only, to be removed after), and the same group ran it smoothly last year with two applicant-paid police officers. Approved.

cases.name: Authorization to Sign Agreement with ClearGov for New Budget Software

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign an agreement with ClearGov for new budget software, discovered by the Supervisor, Town Administrator Kevin, and Comptroller Abbas at professional conferences. Members praised it as a transparency tool that presents the budget with graphs and pie charts for the public, with a possible capital-planning add-on for five- and ten-year planning. Enthusiastically approved.

cases.name: Stipulation of Agreement with CSEA Unit 2 — Add Water Treatment Operator 2A Position

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign a stipulation of agreement with CSEA Unit 2 adding the Water Treatment Operator 2A position to the collective bargaining agreement. Approved with little discussion.

cases.name: Westchester Joint Water Works — Water District 9 Corey Heights Water Supply Improvements (Water Supply Agreement & Bill of Sale)

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign two agreements for Water District 9 Corey Heights improvements — a water supply agreement and a bill of sale/assumption of obligations transferring the public water mains. Superintendent Sal flagged that Section 5 (page 4), covering NYC DEP per-capita charges and a needed population determination, must be clarified with NYC before it is finalized. The board approved the water supply agreement subject to clarification to the town attorney's satisfaction in consultation with Sal, and separately approved the bill of sale. Two connections are active; the other nine await DEC. Adopted with conditions.

cases.name: Highway Garage Roof Replacement — ELQ Industries via White Plains Job Order Contracting Program
cases.applicant: ELQ Industries (via Gordian / City of White Plains job order contracting)

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign an agreement with ELQ Industries, via the White Plains job order contracting program, to replace the leaking highway garage roof, to be paid from fund balance since maintenance lines are insufficient. Members lamented the near-$200,000 cost, noting prior estimates of ~$150K and ~$170K in past years were never acted on, on a building 'not even worth saving,' but agreed the holes endanger workers and equipment. The ~10-day job should finish before winter closes the garage. Approved with the fund-balance funding notation.

cases.name: Stipend for Danielle D. Tomas, Senior Office Assistant, Building Department

timeline.summary: The board authorized a stipend for Danielle D. Tomas, senior office assistant in the Building Department, effective Sept. 11, 2025, with members noting she is 'doing the job of two people.' Approved.

cases.name: Resignations/Retirements — Virginia Garcia and Jane Purser (North Castle Public Library)

timeline.summary: The board accepted, with regret and good wishes, a retirement resignation from library assistant Virginia Garcia (effective Sept. 12, 2025) and a resignation from library hourly clerk Jane Purser (effective Aug. 9, 2025). Both accepted.

cases.name: Conference Travel Authorizations — Assessor and Highway Personnel

timeline.summary: The board approved two travel authorizations: Town Assessor Georgeanne Richardson to attend the NYS Assessors Association Fall Conference in Lake George, Oct. 6–9, with a town vehicle; and Highway General Foreman Jamie Norris to attend the League of Municipalities Conference in Atlantic City, Nov. 18–20, with lead mechanic Matthew Harrisch and a town vehicle. Both approved. A consensus agenda was also approved.

cases.name: Proposed Ethics Code Amendments — Agenda Scheduling and Distribution Dispute
cases.applicant: Ethics Board / Town Board Ethics Liaison

timeline.summary: During liaison updates, Councilman Berra (ethics liaison) pressed to distribute special counsel Bob Spolzino's revised ethics-code documents and DiGiacinto's comments and to put receipt of the revised law on the next agenda so a public hearing could be scheduled. The Supervisor said the confidential materials would be distributed the next day but that the item would go on the agenda only after the board deliberates it in executive session, and accused Berra of overreaching as liaison and injecting personal views into the ethics board's work. The exchange escalated into a heated, personal argument involving Rende, Berra, and DiGiacinto over agenda-setting authority (two members may request an item in writing; the Supervisor otherwise sets the agenda), staff use, and prior email blasts. No action taken.

cases.name: Con Edison Proposed 2026 Rate Hikes — Resident Advocacy Appeal

timeline.summary: In her liaison update, Councilwoman DiGiacinto urged residents to email State Senator Shelley Mayer and Assemblyman Chris Burdick (both of whom attended her North White Plains gathering) opposing Con Edison's proposed 2026 delivery rate hikes and to have them forward concerns to the Governor and Public Service Commission. The Supervisor confirmed the town had put out messaging. No action taken.

cases.name: North Castle Public Library Summer Programs Update and Fall Programming

timeline.summary: Councilman Hussain shared a screen presentation of the library's summer statistics — over 30,000 total checkouts including 20,000+ books, 2,800+ audio, 8,000+ ebooks, 310 programs, ~9,000 youth attendees, and ~6,000 books read — and promoted fall programming (meditation, art history, knitting, cooking demos) and the Armonk outdoor art show whose proceeds fund library programs. Celebratory discussion, no action.

cases.name: Supervisor Update — Parks, Turf Field, Dog Park, Water Projects, and Sidewalk Planning

timeline.summary: The Supervisor reported progress across many projects: the turf field, the nearly complete dog park (targeting an early-October ribbon cutting), Clove Road field work, the Quarry Heights playground (with an engineer reviewing drainage from an impervious pad), the swimming pool improvements, School Street and the Water 8-to-4 connection waterline, Quarry Heights water expansion, and cleanup of the Sands Mills historic site. He also asked staff to phase long-deferred sidewalk improvements (a 2005 plan) rather than shelving them as too costly. DiGiacinto pushed to prioritize sidewalks across all three hamlets, noting North White Plains residents walk to the train and stores, not just for exercise. Discussion only.

cases.name: Open Space Committee Work Session — Digital Natural Resources Inventory (NRI) Map
cases.applicant: Open Space Committee (Carrie Kasak, chair) with Westchester County GIS (Anna Geraldo Gomez)

timeline.summary: Open Space Committee chair Carrie Kasak, Town Planner Adam Kaufman, and Westchester County GIS staff presented a web-based Natural Resources Inventory map layering wetlands, forests, slopes, tax parcels, zoning, and other data for every parcel in town, provided free by the county (saving the town thousands). It was described as phase one of a plan leading to a Mianus River Gorge conservation-scoring algorithm and a possible Community Preservation Fund referendum (real-estate transfer tax) via the Trust for Public Land. The tool will be posted publicly and is intended for all boards (Planning, ZBA, Conservation, Town Board). No vote; work session/discussion only.

cases.name: Recognition of Police Department State Re-Accreditation

timeline.summary: Supervisor Rende reported the police department passed its five-year state accreditation review 'with flying colors,' with retired-chief assessors reviewing 112 processes and conducting unannounced ride-alongs and one-on-one interviews. He recognized Chief Simonson, Lt. Huffnagel, Sgts. Joel Thomas and Chris Costa, and the whole department. Board members echoed pride and noted the voluntary process aids public safety and possibly insurance costs. No formal action.

cases.name: Welcome of Fall High-School Interns / Town Internship Program
cases.applicant: Town internship program (spearheaded by Josephine Egan)

timeline.summary: The board welcomed two new high-school interns, Arnhem Das and Jack McNulty, in the town's newly formed rotating internship program (crediting Josephine Egan and the town clerk/administrator offices). Both interns spoke about their interest in local government. Board members encouraged them to ask questions and even criticize the board. No formal action.

cases.name: Clove Field / Community Park Field Improvement Update

timeline.summary: Supervisor Rende updated on the Clove Field project: a next-day meeting with Highway, Parks, and staff (Jamie, Kevin, Matt, Joe Chamele) to set a firm start date, likely early the following week, beginning with drainage rerouting. Topsoil saved from Community Park is stockpiled for relocation to Clove Road, and work is coordinated with contractor Matt DeRosa's turf schedule to finish before winter sod season. Discussion only, including a resident/attendee who asked about timing.

cases.name: Ethics Board Proposed Ethics-Code Amendments (Resident Request for Action)

timeline.summary: During public comment, resident Susan Scheimer (who helped draft the current code) urged the board to act on ethics-code amendments the Ethics Board proposed on January 8, asking that a new public hearing be noticed if that is what it takes to move forward. Supervisor Rende responded that the proposed changes would be discussed with counsel in that evening's executive session and that a new public hearing could likely be set by October 8. No formal action taken in public session.

cases.name: Receipt of Letter from Francesca and Frederick Azada (received Sept 4, 2025)

timeline.summary: The board voted to receive a letter dated/received September 4, 2025 from Francesca and Frederick Azada, submitted as property owners. Brief clarifying discussion on the name/status; motion made, seconded, and carried by voice vote. Routine receipt.

cases.name: Petition Opposing Basketball 'Court' at Quarry Heights Park
cases.address: Quarry Heights Park, North White Plains

timeline.summary: The board formally received a resident petition opposing construction of a basketball court at Quarry Heights Park. Members pushed back on the petition's accuracy, stressing the plan is a small permanent hoop and pad (not a full court, no parking lot), replacing a portable hoop that neighbors the Candreas installed years ago; the chief reported zero complaints about the existing portable hoop. The board voted to receive the petition (motion, second, voice vote) while signaling intent to proceed with the improvement, using pervious asphalt and stockpiled topsoil, and to consider refurbishing the playground in the 2026 budget. Members emphasized keeping kids off the road for safety.

cases.name: Retroactive Special-Event Permit — Spectrum Painting/JB Auto Body Charity Car Show
cases.applicant: Spectrum Painting / JB Auto Body Works

timeline.summary: The board granted retroactive approval of a special-event permit for a charity car show held Sunday, September 28 at 135 Bedford Road, benefiting a women's-cancer foundation. Approved by motion, second, and voice vote, with a request that organizers apply in advance next year. The discussion prompted a plan to revise the local law (with Town Planner Adam Kaufman) to let the board refer routine recurring special-event permits to professional staff rather than hold public hearings, targeting a November meeting.

cases.name: Community Park Artificial-Turf Change Order No. 1 (Shaw Sports Turf) — Sports Lines & Eagle Logo

timeline.summary: The board received a KSCJ Consulting memo and considered Shaw Sports Turf change order no. 1 on the Community Park artificial-turf project, covering added sports-line striping (for two micro soccer fields and a practice football field) and an optional North Castle Eagle logo; a negotiated reduction (3% on striping, 6% with the logo) was secured via Joe Chamele and Matt DeRosa. The board split the vote into two motions. The line package (~$29,677) passed unanimously (5-0). The Eagle logo (~$45,406 before reduction) passed by roll call 3 aye (Milim, Hussain, and presiding Supervisor Rende) to 1 no (DiGiacinto) with 1 abstention (Berra). DiGiacinto criticized the change-order process and the logo cost as cosmetic; supporters argued change orders are normal and the branding adds value.

cases.name: Tie the Town Pink Campaign — Pink Ribbons Benefiting Soul Riders (Barn Hills)

timeline.summary: The board approved the Barn Hills 'Tie the Town Pink' campaign to place pink ribbons around town (Main Street, Town Hall pillars and staircase railings) benefiting Soul Riders, a nonprofit supporting people impacted by cancer. Discussion focused on not rigidly capping the number at nine; the board approved it as proposed, allowing additional reasonable locations. Motion, second, and voice vote.

cases.name: KSCJ Proposal — Water District 4 Extension (Byram Hills HS, Brentwood/Summit) and Supplement to Water District 2 (Windmill)

timeline.summary: The board approved a KSCJ engineering-services proposal to study extending Water District 4 to Byram Hills High School and the proposed Brentwood/Summit community, and to supplement Water District 2 (Windmill) supply, authorizing the supervisor to sign. Water/Sewer Superintendent 'Sal' explained the engineering, elevations, hydraulics, pump-station needs, easements, added fire hydrants, and how selling water to Summit and Windmill creates efficiencies and backup supply while addressing stressed wells and PFAS at the high school. Members noted costs are recovered through district bonds paid by users. Approved by motion, second, and voice vote.

cases.name: Purchase of Radios for Parks & Recreation (Metrocom Wireless, via County Contract)

timeline.summary: The board approved purchasing radios for Parks & Recreation trucks and home bases from Metrocom Wireless through the Westchester County contract. Members noted this puts Highway, Police, and Parks on the same radio system, important for snow emergencies, bad-weather coordination, and school-district bus transportation. Motion, second, and unanimous voice vote.

cases.name: Stipulation Agreement — Town of North Castle, CSEA, and Employee No. 3420

timeline.summary: The board authorized the supervisor to sign a stipulation agreement between the Town of North Castle, the CSEA, and employee number 3420. Approved by motion, second, and voice vote with no substantive discussion in public session.

cases.name: Excelsior Housing Group — Request to Extend RFEI Submission Deadline

timeline.summary: Supervisor Rende raised a same-day letter from Excelsior Housing Group LLC, an interested RFEI respondent, requesting the submission deadline (currently extended to about October 20) be pushed to December 1. Rather than add it as a last-minute item, the board agreed to take it up at the October 8 meeting, with Rende suggesting a possible compromise November date. No action taken; deferred.

cases.name: Local Law to Amend Chapter 127 — Short-Term Rental Regulations

timeline.summary: A work session on a draft local law creating a registration/regulation scheme for short-term rentals, prompted by a severe problem property on Washington Avenue in North White Plains. The board reached rough consensus to keep a primary-residence requirement, retain (over Hussain's and Rende's objection) an owner-must-be-present requirement, reduce the waiting period from four years/two years to two years on the CO and one year of residency, and add quiet-hours provisions. No vote was taken; the planner and building inspector will revise the draft, compile an inventory of existing rentals, and bring it back before scheduling a public hearing.

cases.name: Resolution Supporting Intermunicipal Airport Master Plan Task Force Recommendations
cases.applicant: Airport Master Plan Task Force (rep. Michael Pollock, w/ Larry Ruisi)

timeline.summary: A resolution joining seven municipalities in support of task force recommendations to the county on Westchester County Airport, covering the terminal use agreement (240-passenger/half-hour limit), FBOs, noise, traffic, and environmental concerns. Task force representative Michael Pollock presented and answered extensive questions about the ~80/20 private-vs-commercial traffic split and legal constraints. Adopted 4-1 by roll call, with Milim voting no because he wanted the resolution to push for a larger commercial-carrier share over time. Rende commended Milim for voting his conviction rather than abstaining.

cases.name: Extension of Town Hall Project RFEI Deadline (Excelsior Housing Group request)
cases.address: 45/15 Bedford Road & town hall parcel, Armonk
cases.applicant: Excelsior Housing Group, LLC (via letter from Patrick Normyle)

timeline.summary: Consideration of a letter requesting extension of the deadline to submit an RFEI (Request for Expression of Interest) on the town hall project to Dec 1. After a long and heated debate over the RFEI process itself, the board voted 4-1 to extend the deadline for all respondents to November 10 (aligning with the Nov 12 board meeting). Berra voted no, wanting the process concluded sooner while Milim is still on the board and believing respondents had ample time. The item produced a sharp Rende-DiGiacinto confrontation over whether the RFEI is a political/misleading exercise, with Milim also criticizing DiGiacinto's public messaging as divisive.

cases.name: Sidewalks, Trails & Pedestrian Crosswalk Safety (Parks Board follow-up)
cases.address: Main Street/Rt 128, School Street, Wampus Brook Park (Armonk); Nethermont/Virginia Road (North White Plains)

timeline.summary: During public comment a Parks Board member followed up on ~2.5-year-old survey recommendations for sidewalk/trail extensions in Armonk and an unsafe CVS-area crosswalk on state Route 128. Rende described reviving a shelved comprehensive sidewalk plan and pursuing a staged, grant-and-bond funding approach, noting a prior grant application was denied. The board discussed prioritizing safety segments and coordinating with NYSDOT on the crosswalk and a possible signal; no formal action was taken.

cases.name: Local Law to Amend Chapter 263 Special Events — Remove Public Hearing Requirement

timeline.summary: The board received a proposed local law updating Chapter 263 (special events) to remove the public hearing requirement and scheduled a public hearing on it for October 22, 2025. Received and public hearing set by voice vote.

cases.name: Code of Ethics Amendments — Close Public Hearing & Schedule Work Session

timeline.summary: The board acted on the public hearing opened April 9, 2025 regarding proposed Code of Ethics amendments and set a joint work session with the Ethics Board for the first November meeting (November 12), when the drafting counsel is available. A clean revised draft incorporating minor word changes will be circulated to Ethics Board members by end of week, with the aim of setting a public hearing date after the work session.

cases.name: Revised Town Workplace Violence Policy

timeline.summary: The board adopted a revised workplace violence prevention policy after discussion, prompted by DiGiacinto, over whether it covers elected officials. The Town Administrator and special counsel clarified that under state statute the policy covers municipal employees but not town board members/officers (who are public officers, not employees), whereas the sexual harassment policy covers everyone. A proposed parallel-language tweak was set aside to avoid tabling; adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: Revised Town Sexual Harassment Policy

timeline.summary: The board adopted the revised sexual harassment policy by voice vote. Staff confirmed that, unlike the workplace violence policy, this policy covers all elected officials, appointees, and consultants under state and federal law.

cases.name: Policy for Use of Municipal Vehicles for Highway Emergency Personnel

timeline.summary: The board adopted a policy governing take-home/emergency use of municipal vehicles by highway emergency personnel. Adopted by roll call with all five members voting aye. DiGiacinto supported it but asked that the recurring cost be considered in the context of the upcoming budget.

cases.name: Change Order #2 — IBM Community Park Turf / Clove Road Baseball Field Reconstruction (Shaw Sports Turf)
cases.address: Clove Road ballfields; IBM Community Park

timeline.summary: The board received a letter and approved Change Order #2 to the Shaw Sports Turf agreement to reconstruct the natural-grass Clove Road baseball fields (drainage, regrading, re-cut infields) alongside the IBM Community Park artificial turf project, authorizing the supervisor to sign. Doing the work through the existing co-op contract and reusing stockpiled tested topsoil saved substantial money versus a new bid. DiGiacinto made the motion and thanked longtime advocate Bob Kandrea; received and authorization approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Aquaworks Contract Termination & Emergency Contractor Authorization
cases.applicant: Town Board (docs prepared by Town Attorney Roland's office) / Aquaworks

timeline.summary: Add-on items: the board adopted a resolution declaring an emergency condition and authorizing termination of an existing contract, approved the contract termination agreement, authorized the supervisor to sign, and approved the Aquaworks bid proposal to serve as emergency contractor to complete the project. Added on, received, and all items adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: Conservation Board Memo — Major Andre Site Improvements

timeline.summary: The board received a memo from the Conservation Board asking to be consulted on projects like the Major Andre site improvements. Rende explained he had responded that referral was not required because the donor-funded work (invasive-plant and dead-tree removal, grass planting) made no substantive change to the wetland/watercourse and, per the planning department, needed no Conservation Board review. Received by voice vote; discussion only.

cases.name: Alcohol Permits & Community Event Approvals
cases.address: Whippoorwill Hall, 19 East Whippoorwill Road; Wampus Brook Park; North Castle Public Library, Armonk
cases.applicant: Katonah Classic Stage; Friends of Frosty; 250th Revolutionary War Committee

timeline.summary: The board approved a group of routine permits/event requests by voice vote: an alcohol permit for Katonah Classic Stage receptions at Whippoorwill Hall (Oct 14-Nov 2), use of town roads and Wampus Brook Park for the annual Frosty Day parade and tree lighting (Nov 30), and an alcohol permit for the 250th Revolutionary War Committee opening-night exhibit reception (Oct 20). Rende encouraged residents to attend the Oct 20 exhibit at the Armonk library branch.

cases.name: Appointments & Personnel — Planning Board Appointment and Police Training

timeline.summary: The board approved sending Police Officer Matthew Janelli to the NYS Highway Safety Symposium in Oswego (Oct 14-17), appointed Thomas Crespi to the Planning Board for a term ending December 31, 2025, and approved the consensus agenda. All approved by voice vote; DiGiacinto welcomed the Crespi appointment.

cases.name: Sidewalk & Trail Improvements — Armonk and North White Plains Hamlets (Work Session)
cases.applicant: Town Planner Adam Kaufman / Recreation & Parks Advisory Board

timeline.summary: Adam Kaufman presented a long-planned multi-phase vision for pedestrian connectivity: filling sidewalk gaps on North Broadway with a mid-block crossing, a Virginia Road sidewalk, and multi-use paths connecting schools and neighborhoods in the Armonk hamlet. The board learned the Greenway grant for the School Street-to-Sands Mill path was denied a second time, prompting discussion of self-funding via a bond given the town's AAA rating. Consensus was to close the work session and direct staff/engineers to redesign a comprehensive, lower-cost sidewalk plan serving BOTH hamlets (substituting cheaper trails/gravel paths and a Route 128 sidewalk for expensive boardwalk options), then bring back cost estimates. No formal vote to spend money was taken; the board also weighed the plan against other big-ticket projects (town hall, highway garage).

cases.name: Local Law Amending Chapter 263 (Special Events) — Remove Public Hearing Requirement

timeline.summary: The board opened and held a public hearing on a local law to remove the public-hearing requirement for special-event permits, replacing it with a staff referral while keeping safety protocols and the 250-ft neighbor-notification requirement. Staff explained the change reduces burden on applicants (e.g., Troy's Nursery Easter event, corporate car shows) and aligns special-event permits with the town's event-permit process. The board received the required documents (public notice, affidavits, negative declaration, EAF Parts 1-2), closed the hearing, adopted the negative declaration, and adopted the local law, all by voice vote (aye). Matt Milim probed whether notice should exceed 250 ft and use town envelopes/certificates of mailing, but the board opted to keep the existing 250-ft standard.

cases.name: Payment Application No. 2 — Papito Construction (Water District #4 Well Site Work)

timeline.summary: The board approved payment application No. 2 to Papito Construction for site work on the Water District #4 well project. Described as 'pretty straightforward'; Water/Sewer superintendent Sal was available for questions but none were raised. Passed by voice vote (aye).

cases.name: Resolution Authorizing NY Statewide Investment in More Swimming (NY Swims) Grant

timeline.summary: The board adopted a resolution authorizing participation in the New York Statewide Investment in More Swimming (NY Swims) grant program. Passed by voice vote (aye) with no substantive discussion.

cases.name: Proposal from Cartographic Associates (CAI) — Tax Map Maintenance for 2026 Data

timeline.summary: The board approved a proposal from Cartographic Associates, Inc. for tax-map maintenance processing data recorded in 2026, and authorized the Supervisor to sign the agreement. A member began raising roof-warranty questions before realizing they had jumped ahead to a later item; the tax-map item itself passed by voice vote (aye).

cases.name: Hergenhan Recreation Center Roof Replacement — ELQ Industries via Gordian Cooperative

timeline.summary: The board approved an ELQ Industries proposal (through the Gordian state-bid cooperative) to replace the leaking Hergenhan Recreation Center roof at about $194,000, paid from fund balance. Extensive discussion centered on a 20-year shingle warranty and the flat-roof/shingle junction that had failed; one member wanted the cost of stepping up to 25/30-year shingles and asked that the Town Attorney review the manufacturer's warranty. Staff explained the steep pitch makes higher-rated shingles unnecessary and that the cooperative bid limits material choices. The motion passed with one abstention (the member seeking more warranty/cost information); Supervisor Rende voted yes, glad to 'finally get the roof fixed' after years of leaks.

cases.name: Temporary Political Signs / Sign Law Enforcement & Revision (Discussion)

timeline.summary: Prompted by resident and former highway employee Mike Giaccio, the board discussed the proliferation of temporary political signs and inconsistent enforcement of the existing sign code. Members broadly agreed the situation is 'out of control' and that the sign law is ambiguous and should be revised, recalling prior unsuccessful work sessions. Rende favored requiring each candidate to register a responsible contact with the Clerk so violating signs can be flagged for removal rather than having town staff pull them; Barbara urged candidate self-restraint on timing and quantity and prompt post-election cleanup; Matt stressed that rewriting the ambiguous law is necessary to enable fair, non-selective enforcement. No formal action taken.

cases.name: Driveway / Highway Bond Permit Process Simplification (Discussion)

timeline.summary: During liaison/updates, Barbara DiGiacinto raised that residents doing driveway work can face two separate permits (building department plus a highway bond when work touches the curb cut/right-of-way). Rende noted the town had already met with the building and highway departments and posted clarifying notes on the website, and explained the highway bond is required only when work affects the curb cut in the right-of-way. Barbara asked to check whether the process can be further simplified to a single permit. No action taken.

cases.name: Receipt of Proposed 2026 Town Budget

timeline.summary: The board formally voted to officially receive the proposed 2026 town budget as presented, satisfying the state-law requirement to receive the budget by November 10. The motion to receive passed by voice vote (all in favor). The Supervisor praised staff (Abbas, Kevin, and Matt's analysis) for the work product. Receipt is a procedural step; substantive review was deferred to the scheduled public hearing.

cases.name: Set Public Hearing on 2026 Budget for November 19

timeline.summary: The board adopted a motion to set the public hearing to review the proposed 2026 budget for November 19. The motion was made, seconded, and passed by voice vote (all in favor). Members indicated they intend to scrutinize the budget line items carefully at that hearing before adoption.

cases.name: 2026 Budget Tax-Cap Override and 4.81% Tax Increase Discussion

timeline.summary: Receipt of the budget prompted a lengthy, at times heated debate over the proposed 4.81% property tax increase, which would override the state's 2% tax cap for the first time in town history. Councilman Milim asked the Comptroller to explain how the tax cap works; Abbas explained it is a state-calculated levy limit (lower of 2% or inflation) with no penalty for exceeding it, effectively an alert to the public. The Supervisor, Milim, and Berra argued the cap is arbitrary/a 'red herring' given roughly 4-4.5% cost inflation (healthcare ~8%, retirement) on ~$37M of spending against only ~$22M of property-tax revenue, and that years of flat taxes had meant deferred maintenance (town hall, Hogan, pool, fields), an oversized fund balance, and budgeting for unfilled police/other positions. DiGiacinto and Berra voiced concern about breaking the cap and about development's impact on schools, and DiGiacinto requested the Budget & Finance Committee review the budget before the next meeting. The exchange grew adversarial, with Rende accusing DiGiacinto of politicizing the tax-cap issue for electoral advantage and she countering that receiving the budget at a special meeting without disclosing the cap override was itself political. No vote; discussion only, deferred to the November 19 hearing. Meeting adjourned as the Supervisor had to leave.

cases.name: Conservation Easement & Declaration of Covenants — 130 Old Mount Kisco Road, Armonk
cases.applicant: Jennifer Chiarella (owner); atty. Aaron Warner, Zarin & Steinmetz

timeline.summary: Consideration of a grant of conservation easement and declaration of covenants tied to a planning-board-approved three-lot conservation subdivision, plus authorization for the Supervisor to sign and record the documents. Counsel and applicant Frank Madonna appeared; the board discussed that the conserved 1.8-acre lot (with steep slopes) could otherwise have been built on. Approved on a voice vote.

cases.name: Marinovic Project, 101 Hickory Way — Wetland Bonds & Address Change

timeline.summary: Two-part receipt of town engineer recommendations: (1) establish a wetland mitigation bond and a five-year monitoring/maintenance bond, and (2) assign a new street address from 101 Old Hickory Way to 9 Crossroad with referral to the E-911 coordinator. Members flagged that the bond should reference the changed address; the board directed the Town Attorney to review the bond language ('formerly known as'). Both parts approved on voice votes.

cases.name: Goldman Project, 15 Stony Brook Place — Wetland Monitoring

timeline.summary: Receipt of a town engineer recommendation to establish a five-year wetland monitoring and maintenance requirement for the Goldman project. Approved on a voice vote.

cases.name: Payment Application #3 — Papatito Construction, Water District #4 New Well

timeline.summary: Authorization of payment application number three to Papatito Construction for site work on the Water District #4 new well project. Rende clarified the town is advancing the money as a loan to the water district, which will issue a bond once work is complete. Approved on a voice vote.

cases.name: Local Law to Override the Tax Levy Limit (GML §3-C) & Set Public Hearing

timeline.summary: Consideration of a local law to override the state 2% tax levy limit and to schedule a public hearing for December 10, 2025 (the last December meeting, before the year-end budget adoption deadline). The board stressed this was a safety-net/ministerial step that does not itself commit the town to exceeding the cap; the proposed 2026 budget carries a 4.81% increase driven largely by contractual salaries and healthcare. A heated exchange occurred between Milim and DiGiacinto over whether more budget cuts were possible. Adopted 4-1 by roll call, with DiGiacinto opposed.

cases.name: Revised Compensation and Benefit Manual

timeline.summary: Adoption of the revised Town of North Castle Compensation and Benefit Manual, effective January 1, 2025. Motion made and seconded, approved on a voice vote.

cases.name: Approval of Holiday Displays (Creche and Star & Crescent)
cases.address: Wampus Brook Park, Armonk; Miller Park, North White Plains

timeline.summary: Approval of requests for holiday displays: a minor nativity creche and a Star and Crescent, at both Wampus Brook Park in Armonk and Miller Park in North White Plains. Approved on a voice vote.

cases.name: Library Solutions LLC Agreements — Website/Calendar and Branding/Logo
cases.applicant: North Castle Public Library / Library Solutions LLC

timeline.summary: Authorization for the Supervisor to sign two agreements with Library Solutions (Library Market) for the North Castle Public Library: (1) a new website and calendar configuration, and (2) branding/logo work. The library declined to migrate to the town's Civic Plus platform in favor of a library-specialized vendor; board members probed cost (design vs. ongoing fees), the need for a new logo, ADA/branding rationale, and whether increased demand could raise Westchester Library System costs. Library board member Annie Gala and director Catherine presented; the project uses already-budgeted funds. Both agreements approved on separate voice votes.

cases.name: CSEA Stipulations — New Bargaining-Unit Positions

timeline.summary: Two stipulations of agreement with CSEA: Unit 1 to add the position of assistant automotive mechanic, and Unit 2 to add the position of recreation supervisor for senior citizens, to the respective collective bargaining agreements. Both authorized for the Supervisor's signature and approved on voice votes.

cases.name: Kent Street Parking Lot (Former Verizon Property) — Change Orders 10 & 11
cases.address: Kent Street parking lot (former Verizon property), Armonk

timeline.summary: Approval of two change orders with Tony Casale Inc. for the Kent Street parking lot improvements: change order #10 for landscape upgrades to parking-lot islands (adopted on a voice vote) and change order #11 for an asphalt paving extension (~$30,000). Change order #11 drew objection that a competitive bid could cost far less (~$10,000) and was arguably premature given a possible future parking district; it passed by roll call with Berra abstaining. DiGiacinto recused herself from both items citing a potential advantage to a family owning property on the west side of Main Street.

cases.name: BCN Telecom — IP Voice / Telecommunications Services Agreement

timeline.summary: Authorization for the Supervisor to sign a subscriber service agreement for IP voice/telecommunications service with BCN Telecom to replace ~10+-year-old, failing phone infrastructure and add faster internet and call-transfer capability. Net added cost cited at about $1,637/month after dropping Optimum/Verizon lines. DiGiacinto said she lacked the comparative analysis she would have wanted but ultimately supported it. Approved on a voice vote.

cases.name: Workers' Compensation Coverage Renewal (Comp Alliance 2026-2027)
cases.applicant: NYS Municipal Workers Compensation Alliance (Comp Alliance)

timeline.summary: Authorization for the Supervisor to sign a renewal agreement with the New York State Municipal Workers Compensation Alliance (Comp Alliance) for workers' compensation coverage for 2026 and 2027. Approved on a voice vote.

cases.name: Accudata Workforce Solutions — Payroll Software Agreement

timeline.summary: Authorization for the Supervisor to sign an agreement with Accudata Workforce Solutions for payroll software, a major upgrade adding electronic time clocks/swipes. Finance Director Abbas and Councilman Berra negotiated a last-minute reduction of the annual fee by $2,821 with no first-year increase and capped modest annual upcharges, saving roughly $4,000/year. Approved on a voice vote.

cases.name: Receipt of RFEI Responses (Town Hall / Architectural Services)
cases.applicant: GF55 (via Keith B. Rosenthal / Citizens of North Castle); Ferrari Companies, Croco Architecture PLLC & Torti Gallas Partners

timeline.summary: Added to the agenda and formally received the two RFEI responses submitted by the November 10 deadline, so they become public documents posted to the town-hall landing page. The board plans to give both responders a public presentation opportunity, likely at the Whippoorwill Hall theater in the first week of December; a third potential responder granted an extension did not submit. Received on voice votes.

cases.name: Probationary Highway Department Appointments

timeline.summary: Three probationary appointments in the Highway Department, all effective November 13, 2025: Christian Rossi (road maintainer), Anthony Dela Cruz Solazano (assistant mechanic), and Robert Pattanero (motor equipment operator). Rende noted all three positions were discussed and budgeted in the 2026 budget work sessions. Each approved on a voice vote.

cases.name: Work Session — Route 22 Bridge Replacement over Armonk Road Connector
cases.address: Route 22 over Armonk Road connector, North White Plains
cases.applicant: Westchester County Department of Public Works / HVA Engineers (design consultant)

timeline.summary: County DPW and HVA Engineers presented the design for replacing the structurally deficient, county-owned Route 22 bridge, backed by over $12 million in federal funds within a roughly $17.5 million project. The preferred alternative slides a precast concrete arch beneath the existing structure to minimize traffic impact, eliminates the accident-prone stop sign by converting the ramp into a free-flow merge lane, and reuses the original stone facade. The board and residents raised safety, bicycle/pedestrian access, fire-truck clearance, environmental (Kensico Reservoir/DEP wetlands), and communication questions; construction is targeted for spring 2027. No vote was taken; the board committed to send a formal letter of concerns urging the county/state not to delay broader Route 22 improvements.

cases.name: Final Resolution to Establish Water District No. 9

timeline.summary: The board adopted the final resolution establishing Water District Number Nine. The measure passed on a roll-call vote 4-0 (Berra aye, DiGiacinto aye, Hussain aye, Rende aye; Milim absent), and two certified copies were requested.

cases.name: Police Memo and Public Hearing Scheduling — Chapter 325 Vehicle & Traffic Amendments (Crossroad)
cases.address: Crossroad North, between Route 128 and Old Mount Kisco Road, Armonk
cases.applicant: Police Chief Peter Simonson / Town Board

timeline.summary: The board received Police Chief Peter Simonson's memo recommending amendments to town code Chapter 325 to designate Crossroad North as one-way westbound because the steep grade at Old Mount Kisco Road causes vehicles to bottom out and creates a sight-distance hazard. After the chief explained that Crossroad South already serves the alternate movement and rebuilding the grade would be too costly, the board voted to receive the memo and to schedule a public hearing for December 10 to draft the local law.

cases.name: Settlement — Andrew Verboy v. Town of North Castle

timeline.summary: The board approved a settlement in the matter of Andrew Verboy v. Town of North Castle by motion, second, and voice vote. Supervisor Rende afterward asked counsel whether the vote could be revisited off-camera; counsel advised it was the insurer's decision and unlikely given minors were involved and were supervised by town employees.

cases.name: 2026 Agreement with Verde Electric Maintenance Corp — Traffic Signal Maintenance
cases.address: Bedford Road & Maple Avenue; four flashing beacons on Route 22, Armonk

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign a 2026 agreement with Verde Electric Maintenance Corporation for traffic-signal maintenance at the Bedford Road/Maple Avenue intersection and four flashing-beacon assemblies on Route 22 in Armonk. The motion passed by voice vote after Supervisor Rende disclosed that principals of Verde Electric had made contributions to his past campaigns.

cases.name: Resignation for Retirement — Police Chief Peter Simonson

timeline.summary: The board accepted Police Chief Peter Simonson's letter of resignation for retirement after 36 years, effective end of 2026. Board members expressed extensive appreciation for his professionalism, leadership, and outside utility contacts; the motion was made 'with deep regret and appreciation' and passed 'regrettably' by voice vote.

cases.name: Proposed Code of Ethics Amendments and Public Hearing Scheduling

timeline.summary: A late-added item to receive proposed Code of Ethics amendments (drafted with special counsel Bob Spolzino and the Board of Ethics) and schedule a December 10 public hearing triggered a heated dispute. DiGiacinto objected that she received a revised draft only at 4:27 p.m. and accused Berra of overreaching by directing the attorney's edits; Rende said the law 'stinks,' was drafted for the wrong reasons, and that incoming member Sonny Vataj should weigh in. After agreeing to delete one disputed provision, the motion (Berra/Hussain in favor) failed on a 2-2 roll call (Berra aye, Hussain aye, DiGiacinto no, Rende no; Milim absent), a tie constituting denial.

cases.name: RFEI Presentations — Municipal Facilities Redevelopment (Town Hall / Police / Court / Highway)
cases.address: Town Hall & Highway Department site, Bedford Road, Armonk
cases.applicant: RFEI responders: Ferrari Companies (Michael Ferrari, with Torti Gallas & Croco architecture) and Keith Rosenthal / 'Citizens of North Castle'

timeline.summary: The board convened a special meeting to receive two responses to its RFEI for modernizing the town's municipal facilities. Ferrari presented a comprehensive ~$70M vision acquiring the Mariani (45 Bedford Rd) and 215 Business Park Drive properties, relocating highway/bus operations, and adding extensive parkland, fields, an amphitheater, and ~40 residential units at 333 Main St; Rosenthal presented a ~$40-45M plan confined to the existing town-owned site with phased, interconnected buildings and a village green. Both plans notably contained NO commercial development of town land, addressing prior resident fears. The board stressed these are conceptual ideas, not proposals, and that any final plan would go to a full town-wide referendum (they committed to a full vote rather than relying on permissive referendum). No vote or decision was taken; the board signaled more meetings and likely a steering/expert committee to develop concrete A/B or single-bond options with real cost estimates.

cases.name: Proclamations Honoring Retiring Police Chief Peter Simonson
cases.applicant: Town Board / County Legislator Margaret Kunzio / Senator Shelley Mayer

timeline.summary: County Legislator Margaret Kunzio presented a Westchester County proclamation declaring December 11 'Chief Peter Simonson Day,' Senator Shelley Mayer sent a state proclamation, and Supervisor Rende read a town proclamation recognizing Simonson's 35 years of service (1990-2025), including his rise through the ranks to chief in 2014. Every board member spoke at length in tribute to his leadership, mentorship, and community impact. Members of the public, including former secretary Mindy Berard reading a statement from former Supervisor Michael Schillero, also offered praise. Purely ceremonial and universally supportive.

cases.name: Certificate of Recognition for Departing Councilman Matt Milim

timeline.summary: The board presented a certificate of recognition to Councilman Matt Milim, whose four-year term was ending (this being his last meeting), thanking him for his service and specifically for resurrecting the Armonk Lions Club and the Folderol festival. Each colleague spoke warmly about his intelligence, independence, and willingness to embrace debate and dissent. Supervisor Rende and Chief Simonson noted their close working relationships. Ceremonial and universally supportive; incoming councilman Sonny Vataj was acknowledged as his successor.

cases.name: Provisional Appointment of Mary Madsen — Animal Warden/Parking Enforcement Officer

timeline.summary: Police Chief Simonson recommended the provisional appointment of Mary Madsen as Animal Warden/Parking Enforcement Officer, filling a vacancy left by Angel Morales's January 2025 retirement. He detailed her 11+ years as a dog control officer and veterinary background and a completed background investigation. The board voted unanimously to appoint her effective January 5, 2026, and Rende then swore her in with family present.

cases.name: Appointment of Reagan Huffnagel as Interim Police Chief

timeline.summary: The board appointed Reagan Huffnagel to interim Police Chief effective January 1, 2026, to succeed the retiring Chief Simonson. The motion passed unanimously by voice vote with congratulations from the board. (The meeting had opened with an executive session interviewing three candidates from the police chief list.)

cases.name: Local Law Amending Chapter 325 — Crossroad North One-Way and Prohibited Left Turn
cases.address: Crossroad North between State Route 128 and Old Mount Kisco Road, Armonk
cases.applicant: North Castle Police Department / Highway Department

timeline.summary: A public hearing was held on a local law amending Chapter 325 to make Crossroad North one-way westbound and to prohibit left turns onto Old Mount Kisco Road, after Highway General Foreman Jamie Norris flagged that vehicles were bottoming out on the steep grade. Lt. Tom McCormick presented site photos, including a September 25 incident where a vehicle got hung up and needed a tow. The board closed the hearing and adopted the law unanimously, combining both changes into one local law.

cases.name: Local Law to Override the Tax Levy Limit (Tax Cap)

timeline.summary: A public hearing was held on a local law to override the tax levy limit established in General Municipal Law 3-c. Resident correspondence was received into the record. The board framed the override as unavoidable given ~8% healthcare and retirement inflation on a budget dominated by employee costs. It was adopted 4-1 on a roll call vote (Milim, Berra, Hussain, Rende in favor; DiGiacinto opposed), the first time in the town's history the cap has been overridden.

cases.name: Adoption of the 2026 Town and Special Districts Preliminary Budget

timeline.summary: After a lengthy public hearing, the board adopted the 2026 budget (total appropriation just under $44M, town-portion tax increase 4.81%) on a 4-1 roll call vote (Milim, Berra, Hussain, Rende yes; DiGiacinto no). Comptroller Abbas and Milim defended a multi-year 'glide path' to structurally balance revenues with expenses and wean the town off drawing on a fund balance that had ballooned to ~$25M. DiGiacinto objected that the board rejected her requests for 8-10% departmental cuts, a hiring freeze, and review of long-vacant positions, noting the county had trimmed its increase to ~3%. Berra voted yes 'with regret,' pressing on declining interest income, condo taxation, overtime, and missing quarterly reports.

cases.name: Proposed Local Law to Permit Level 3 (Fast) EV Charging Stations
cases.applicant: Town Planner / prompted by IBM application

timeline.summary: Town Planner Adam Kaufman presented a proposed amendment to Section 355-4 to permit Level 3 fast EV charging (currently limited to Levels 1-2, capped at 20% of parking), prompted by an IBM application at its gated corporate campus. Councilman Hussain recused himself because he works at IBM. The board received the related documents (items 1-5) and debated how to avoid parking/congestion problems, converging on Milim's idea that EV spaces not count toward off-street parking minimums, restricting the exclusion to Level 3, and adding EV charging as a minor site-plan category. No vote on the law; Kaufman will redraft for the January 14 meeting to then set a public hearing.

cases.name: Sidewalk Improvement Bond Release and Escrow — 873 North Broadway

timeline.summary: On a memo from KSCJ Consulting, the board released the NYS sidewalk improvement bond held for four years from the prior owner (873 Holding Company LLC) and established a new escrow agreement with the new owner (873 LLC) for the improvements to be completed by June 2026, authorizing the supervisor to sign. Members briefly discussed making the release contingent on the new escrow; staff advised the documents would handle it simultaneously and the new owner cannot get a building permit without escrowing. Both items passed unanimously by voice vote.

cases.name: Payment Application #4 — Papatio Construction, Water District #4 New Well

timeline.summary: The board approved payment application #4 from Papatio Construction Company Inc. for site work performed at the Water District #4 new well project. Passed unanimously by voice vote with no questions.

cases.name: Chabad Hanukkah Menorah Lighting at Wampus Park Gazebo
cases.applicant: Chabad of Armonk, Chappaqua and Pleasantville

timeline.summary: The board approved a request from the Chabad of Armonk, Chappaqua and Pleasantville to hold its annual Hanukkah menorah lighting ceremony at the Wampus Park gazebo on December 16. Passed unanimously by voice vote.

cases.name: Aqua Works Change Orders — Lombardi Park Water District Extension

timeline.summary: The board approved three change orders on the John A. Lombardi Park water district extension. Change Order #1 (concrete removal/disposal at $130/cubic yard, verified by the engineer) and #2 (air release valve chamber) passed unanimously. Change Order #3 — an added ~$115,000+ to demolish an old, asbestos-containing, oil-heated building and reroute the water connection so the town stops heating it — passed 4-1 (Milim, Hussain, Berra, Rende yes; DiGiacinto no). DiGiacinto and Berra objected that a building demolition should have been a bid item and an agenda item, not a change order, and complained information arrived late; Milim, Hussain, and Rende defended it as an efficient, money-saving addition to the same contract.

cases.name: Sewer District #2 Bid Awards — Sludge Hauling and Methanol Supply
cases.applicant: Wind River Environmental LLC / Solvents and Petroleum Service Inc.

timeline.summary: The board awarded two 2026 fiscal-year Sewer District #2 contracts, sludge hauling to Wind River Environmental LLC and methanol supply to Solvents and Petroleum Service Inc., and authorized the supervisor to sign both agreements. Both passed unanimously by voice vote.

cases.name: Receipt of Retirement/Resignation — Lisa Larson, Parks & Recreation

timeline.summary: The board received, with regret, a letter of resignation for retirement from Lisa Larson, Senior Office Assistant in Parks and Recreation, effective January 23. Passed unanimously by voice vote; Rende thanked her for the advance notice.

cases.name: 2026 Reorganization — Oaths of Office and Deputy Supervisor Appointment

timeline.summary: New Councilman Sonny Vataj was sworn in (a second, ceremonial oath by a visiting justice), and re-elected Supervisor Joseph Rende and Councilwoman Barbara DiGiacinto were recognized (DiGiacinto already re-sworn by the Town Clerk). Each gave brief remarks thanking residents. The board then appointed Saleem Hussain as Deputy Town Supervisor on a unanimous voice vote, with a member remarking it was 'a great choice.'

cases.name: Organizational Agenda — Depositories, Officer/Secretary Appointments, Annual Policies, Fee Schedule and Salaries

timeline.summary: The board adopted the bulk annual reorganization items on unanimous voice votes: designating depositories, authorizing ACH/wire/facsimile payment authority, and reappointing statutory officers and board secretaries (Town Clerk Allison Simon as Records Management/Access Officer, Registrar, and Board of Elections liaison; Deputy Clerk Maria Scharf; Director of Finance Abbas; Assessor Georgeanne Richardson; Confidential Secretary Josephine Egan; historians, ZBA/Planning/ARB secretaries; fire inspectors including new hire Henry Sieno; engineer KSCJ; town counsel Abrams Fensterman). It also readopted town policies (procurement, investment, workplace-violence, sexual-harassment, IT-usage, videoconferencing, vehicle), the 2026 master fee schedule, meeting schedule (2nd/4th Wednesdays 7:30pm), 72.5 cents/mile mileage, the 2026 salary installment schedule, code-of-ethics posting, and charge-card/advance-payment authorizations.

cases.name: Annual Service, Legal and Fire/Ambulance Agreements for 2026
cases.applicant: Various vendors/districts (KSCJ Consulting, Abrams Fensterman, Patrick Bliss Esq., labor counsel, Valhalla/North White Plains Ambulance, Banksville and Armonk fire districts)

timeline.summary: As part of reorganization, the board authorized the Supervisor to execute the recurring 2026 professional and public-safety agreements on unanimous voice votes: legal services (Abrams Fensterman; Patrick Bliss for Justice Court; labor counsel), KSCJ Consulting for engineering, wetlands, and MS4 stormwater-management/IDDE services, and fire-protection and emergency-ambulance agreements for the ambulance district and Banksville/Armonk fire districts. These are routine annual renewals with no controversy.

cases.name: Long Pond Park District Agreement for 2026 (Member Recusal)
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle / Long Pond Park District

timeline.summary: The board considered the 2026 agreement between the town and the North Castle Long Pond Park District. One council member announced a recusal on this item; the board confirmed no roll-call vote was required despite the recusal and passed it on a voice vote of the remaining members. The recusing member was referred to in the ASR as 'councilman Vera.'

cases.name: Payment Application No. 1 — Aquaworx (School Street Water Main Extension)

timeline.summary: The board approved Payment Application No. 1 to Aquaworx for the School Street water main extension on a voice vote, after superintendent Sal reported the completed work had passed pressure testing and bacteriological sampling and was submitted to the Health Department for approval to energize the main, with service connections to follow (including Lombardy Park). Rende raised the idea of eventually offering Anthony Court residents (5-6 homes) the chance to extend the main and join the district, noting service tees were already provided for future extension, and stressed sequencing paving work to avoid reopening roads.

cases.name: Water District 4 New Well/Control Building — EFI Payment App No. 2 and WSP USA Amendment No. 2

timeline.summary: The board approved Payment Application No. 2 to Engineered Fluid Incorporated (EFI) for the Water District 4 new well building and control (work ~90% complete; contract pays 65% at this stage with a final payment on completion; building delivered in two parts including a ~70,000-lb structure). It also approved WSP USA Amendment No. 2 for engineering/construction services, but conditioned it: the town attorney flagged that WSP re-attached its standard terms and conditions rather than the more favorable originally negotiated terms, so Sal will obtain a revised amendment referencing the original agreement's terms, subject to the town attorney's approval, before signing. Members expressed interest in touring the site.

cases.name: Recreation & Parks Equipment Purchases — Ventrac and Wacker Neuson Wheel Loader

timeline.summary: The board approved Superintendent Matt Traynor's requests to purchase a new Ventrac machine and a Wacker Neuson wheel loader (via Sourcewell contract), both funded from the 2026 operational budget, on voice votes. Rende noted staff identified an unused piece of equipment to be sold at auction to offset the cost, choosing auction over a vendor trade-in for greater value.

cases.name: Filming Permit, Mount Pleasant Easement Letter, and Miscellaneous Agreements
cases.address: Townhouse Diner, North White Plains; 44 Custis Avenue
cases.applicant: Patch Bay Productions LLC; Town of Mount Pleasant; Westchester County; WeatherWorks; CompDoc; SPCA

timeline.summary: The board handled a cluster of routine items on voice votes: retroactive approval of a Patch Bay Productions filming permit ('An Unaccustomed Earth' at the Townhouse Diner, Jan 9, 2026); receipt of a letter from Mount Pleasant's supervisor on expanding a permanent easement at 44 Custis Avenue for police communication equipment on the Custis water tower; the WeatherWorks 2026 renewal; a DOT/FMCSA drug-and-alcohol consortium compliance agreement (2026-2027); a five-year Westchester County IMA for snow/ice removal on county roads (Oct 2025-Sep 2030, at the higher reimbursement rate); a CompDoc summer-camp registration software agreement; a Westchester County RICI criminal-records/police-blotter storage IMA (Mar 2026-Jul 2029); and the 2026 SPCA agreement.

cases.name: In Memoriam — Heidi Slater, Wilfred Mincken, Tony Cecia

timeline.summary: The board closed with condolences to the families of Heidi Slater (longtime resident active in the Armonk Methodist Church), Wilfred Mincken (decades-long Armonk resident), and Tony Cecia, whom DiGiacinto described as 'the glue' of the American Legion. Rende and DiGiacinto shared personal reflections on Cecia, and another member recalled his son's eulogy advice to 'laugh' and 'cry' daily and noted that political differences never prevented friendship. The board then adjourned.

cases.name: Probationary Appointment of Reagan Hufnagle as Police Chief

timeline.summary: The board approved the probationary appointment of Reagan Hufnagle to Chief of Police effective January 29, 2026, moved up on the agenda so he could be sworn in. Supervisor Rende administered the oath after a brief search for the Bible. Motion made and seconded, all in favor (5-0). Chief Hufnagle thanked the board and administration and praised the department.

cases.name: Separation Agreement with Police Chief Peter Simonson

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign the separation agreement with outgoing Police Chief Peter Simonson. Motion made and seconded, all in favor (5-0). Passed without substantive discussion.

cases.name: Commendation of Personnel for Snowstorm Response

timeline.summary: Supervisor Rende commended the highway department, police, parks and public-safety personnel for their handling of a difficult weekend storm, thanking residents for heeding safety warnings and staying off the roads, and crediting Town Administrator Kevin Hay's advance department-head planning meeting. No formal action taken. Councilwoman DiGiacinto added praise for first responders.

cases.name: Revolutionary War 250th History Moment — Miller Hill Park
cases.address: Miller Hill, Route 22, North White Plains
cases.applicant: North Castle Revolutionary War 250th Committee / Historical Committee

timeline.summary: Jed Schisler, a junior at Byram Hills High School, delivered a monthly 'history moment' presentation on Miller Hill Park in North White Plains and its Revolutionary War significance. The board thanked the student and the Historical Committee for keeping the series going. Informational; no action taken.

cases.name: Local Law to Amend EV Charging Station Definition (Permit Level-Three Charging)

timeline.summary: Public hearing on a local law to amend the definition of electric vehicle charging station in section 355-4 of the town code to permit level-three charging. Councilman Saleem Hussain recused himself (employed by IBM, which prompted the item). The core debate was whether level-three spaces should count toward the minimum off-street parking requirement; DiGiacinto and Rende argued they should count (like level one and two), while Berra preferred keeping the exclusion. The board agreed by consensus to remove the exclusion sentence, closed this hearing, directed the Town Planner to revise the language, and scheduled a new public hearing for February 11, 2026.

cases.name: Local Law to Regulate Short-Term Rentals of Homes
cases.applicant: Town (Town Planner Adam Kaufman; special counsel Bob Spolzino)

timeline.summary: Extended public hearing on a proposed local law regulating short-term rentals and referral to the town and county planning boards. The board worked through disputed policy provisions: it kept the waiting-period requirement in provision C (two years after initial CO for new construction, one year after acquiring title otherwise), kept the quiet-hours provision K, and by majority voted to remove provision E (requiring the owner to stay overnight during a rental) as overly restrictive, with DiGiacinto dissenting. Special counsel Spolzino was directed to draft an expedited revocation procedure (likely a building-inspector hearing officer with quick timeframes) to give the law 'teeth' while surviving judicial scrutiny. The board closed the hearing rather than adopt the draft as written, directing a redraft and a new public hearing to be set (targeting February 25, 2026).

cases.name: Open Space Committee Recommendation — John Fava Nature Preserve
cases.applicant: Open Space Committee / Westchester Land Trust

timeline.summary: The board received the Open Space Committee's recommendation to create the John Fava Nature Preserve (previously the Children's Land Preserve) on Byram Lake Road, Armonk. Councilman Berra moved to receive and praised Fava's decades of conservation work; Rende and DiGiacinto supported naming the preserve for Fava. Councilman Hussain objected to the naming approach, arguing preserves should be named for the principles they represent with an honoree recognized on a plaque instead, and asked to discuss alternatives with Open Space chair Kerry Kasak. The board received the recommendation and deferred a formal resolution pending that conversation.

cases.name: Revised Purchase Order / Procurement Policy

timeline.summary: Consideration of the revised town purchase order and procurement policy was tabled to allow Town Attorney Roland more time to review and to gather board questions. Councilman Berra requested a work session to hash out the policy, which Rende agreed to try to schedule for the February 11 meeting. Motion to table made and seconded, all in favor.

cases.name: Provisional Appointment of Kenny Keneally — Appraisal Technician

timeline.summary: The board approved the provisional appointment of Kenny Keneally as appraisal technician in the Assessor's Department, effective January 29, 2026. DiGiacinto congratulated him, noting he had been doing two jobs. Motion made and all in favor.

cases.name: Travel Authorization — Director of Finance Abbas (2026 NYS GFOA Conference)

timeline.summary: The board approved Director of Finance Abbas attending the 2026 New York State GFOA Conference, April 15-17, 2026. DiGiacinto complimented Abbas for checking every box of the procurement/travel submission requirements. Motion made and all in favor.

cases.name: Reappointment of Tom Crispy to the Planning Board

timeline.summary: The board reappointed Tom Crispy to the Planning Board for a five-year term expiring January 30, 2031, with congratulations. Motion made and seconded, all in favor.

cases.name: Committee Resignations — Christine Eggleton (Landmark Preservation) and Alyssa (Open Space)

timeline.summary: The board accepted, with regret, the resignation of Christine Eggleton from the Landmark Preservation Committee and the resignation of a member (Alyssa) from the Open Space Committee. Both motions made, seconded, and passed. Members expressed regret at losing them.

cases.name: Closing in Memory of Maria Palacio

timeline.summary: The board closed the meeting in memory of Maria Palacio, a nearly 60-year Armonk resident who worked for the North Castle Recreation Department serving seniors, extending condolences to her family. Councilwoman DiGiacinto delivered the memoriam and also thanked sanitation workers for double garbage pickup amid the snow. Motion to close made and all in favor.

cases.name: Revised Town Procurement Policy

timeline.summary: In a work session the board reviewed a completely rewritten town procurement policy drafted by Comptroller Abbas using auditor/state-comptroller guidance and peer Westchester municipal policies. The board went page-by-page through Councilman Jose Berra's extensive written comments, sorting them into town-attorney/administrator edits (handled by Kevin), legal questions (for Town Attorney Roland), substantive changes, and error corrections. Numerous wording refinements were agreed (e.g., prices confidential 'prior to award,' grant purchases planned when the grant 'is approved,' softening bid-specification language, adding 'or other entity' to non-collusion language, credit-card purchase limits set at $25,000 with Sam's/Home Depot capped at $2,000 each). No vote was taken; Abbas will produce a redraft in a distinct color for review by Berra, Kevin, and Roland, targeting placement on the agenda for a formal vote at an upcoming meeting.

cases.name: Rare Disease Day Recognition Request
cases.applicant: Susan Cardillo (Star Spangled Carousel) and Reese Geller

timeline.summary: During public comment, resident Susan Cardillo and Byram Hills junior Reese Geller presented on Rare Disease Day (Feb. 28), describing FOXP1 syndrome and asking the town to allow awareness banners, to publicize a fundraiser via town email/newsletter, and to offer any additional guidance. Supervisor Rende responded supportively, offering to feature it in the daily supervisor's update, share it on town social media and community pages, and connect the effort with the Chamber of Commerce, inviting Cardillo to come to the office to coordinate. No formal action was required.

cases.name: Local Law Amending EV Charging Station Definition (Level 3 Charging)

timeline.summary: The board held a public hearing on a local law amending the definition of 'electric vehicle charging station' in Town Code section 355-4 to permit Level 3 (fast) charging and to exclude Level 3 stations from off-street parking calculations. The request originated with IBM, so Councilman Hussain recused himself. No members of the public spoke and the town planner had nothing to add. The board adopted the negative declaration and then the local law by voice vote; Supervisor Rende said he was 'very satisfied' with the law.

cases.name: Resolution Creating the John Fava Nature Preserve

timeline.summary: The board considered naming a 63-acre town-owned parcel on Byram Lake Road the 'John Fava Nature Preserve' to honor Fava's decades of environmental stewardship (35 years with Westchester County Parks and 40 years on the North Castle Conservation Board). Open Space Committee chair Carrie Kasak spoke in favor, and resident Susan Miller spoke strongly for it while sharply criticizing Councilman Hussain's prior hesitation. Hussain delivered an extended screen-shared explanation of his philosophical view that the town should name land for its natural features and recognize people durably (plaques, archives, expandable recognition) with clearer precedent-setting standards, but he ultimately voted in favor. The resolution passed by voice vote; DiGiacinto and Berra strongly supported honoring Fava directly while respecting differing views.

cases.name: Short-Term Rental Local Law — Referral and Public Hearing Scheduling

timeline.summary: The board received a proposed local law to create regulations governing the short-term rental of homes, referred it to the town and county planning boards, and scheduled a public hearing for February 25, 2026. A new procedure (worked out with the Town Clerk and special counsel Bob Spolzino) will allow certain changes during a public hearing without requiring a second hearing, via added posting language. Councilman Berra supported enacting it to end resident hardships while cautioning it may be too restrictive and could be revisited; Rende noted he would still favor republishing for substantial changes, especially where litigation risk exists.

cases.name: Payment Requisition No. 1 — Shaw Integrated & Turf Solutions (Artificial Turf Field)
cases.applicant: Shaw Integrated and Turf Solutions Incorporated

timeline.summary: The board approved payment requisition No. 1 from Shaw Integrated and Turf Solutions Incorporated for the artificial turf field improvements. There was noticeable initial hesitation among members to make the motion, which Supervisor Rende remarked on, though it ultimately passed by voice vote.

cases.name: Change Order No. 4 — Shaw Integrated Turf Solutions (Irrigation at Clove Road Fields)
cases.address: Clove Road Little League and Babe Ruth League baseball fields
cases.applicant: Shaw Integrated Turf Solutions Incorporated (per KSCJ Consulting memo)

timeline.summary: The board received a memo from KSCJ Consulting and approved Shaw Integrated Turf Solutions' Change Order No. 4 for installing an irrigation system at the Clove Road Little League and Babe Ruth League baseball fields, part of the Community Post park artificial turf project, and authorized the supervisor to sign the proposal. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: NYS Association of Towns Membership and Voting Delegate Designation

timeline.summary: The board approved 2026 membership in the New York State Association of Towns and designated Supervisor Joseph A. Rende as the town's voting delegate at the February annual meeting. A member asked how the delegate's votes could be viewed; Rende agreed to share how he votes and noted the legislative agenda and outcomes are available via the association. Approved by voice vote after brief discussion.

cases.name: Change Order No. 4 — Aqua Works (Lombardi Park / School Street Water Main Extension)
cases.applicant: Aqua Works Incorporated (per KSCJ Consulting memo)

timeline.summary: The board received a KSCJ Consulting memo and approved Aqua Works Incorporated's Change Order No. 4 for the Lombardi Park / School Street water main extension, covering additional asbestos removal related to the Lombardi Park building demolition. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Formation of the Town Hall Advisory Committee
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (Alan Blum, committee lead)

timeline.summary: The board approved forming a Town Hall Advisory Committee and adopted its mission statement and committee structure to plan for the town's inadequate town hall, highway, and water department facilities. Volunteer lead Alan Blum described an independent, non-political, expertise-driven committee that will gather needs-based data and keep the community informed, with a short window for additional volunteers. Discussion clarified that Town Planner Adam Kaufman would serve as a resource rather than a formal liaison, preserving the committee's independence; Hussain asked about accepting volunteers and Berra and Rende stressed letting the group work independently. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Resignation of Angela Colombo from the Board of Assessment Review

timeline.summary: The board accepted, with thanks and appreciation, the letter of resignation from Angela Colombo from the Board of Assessment Review, effective January 6, 2026. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Appointment of Denise Lombardi to the Board of Assessment Review

timeline.summary: The board appointed Denise Lombardi to the Board of Assessment Review for a term ending September 30, 2026. DiGiacinto praised her as a well-qualified, licensed appraiser familiar with the assessor's office. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Town Purchase Order and Procurement Policy
cases.applicant: Town Administrator Kevin (with Comptroller Abbas and Town Attorney Roland)

timeline.summary: The board considered adoption of a revised purchase-order and procurement policy that staff had updated per prior work-session direction. Berra raised a late wording tweak on grant-related purchases that he said Roland found meritorious, but DiGiacinto challenged why that input was not circulated to the full board beforehand; Berra then withdrew the suggestion as non-substantive. The policy was adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: Special Use Permit — Virgin Mary & St. Damiana Coptic Orthodox Church (ADA access) + Schedule Public Hearing
cases.applicant: Virgin Mary and St. Damiana Coptic Orthodox Church

timeline.summary: The board acted on the church's request for a special use permit to support an ADA-compliant accessible-access sidewalk improvement for elderly parishioners, along with referral to the town and county planning boards. Adam Kaufman explained the church has operated for decades without an existing special use permit, which the Planning Board needs on record to approve the site plan. The board voted to receive the application and to schedule a public hearing for March 25, 2026 (moved from an initial March 11 suggestion to allow proper notice).

cases.name: Payment Application No. 6 — Papito Construction (Water District No. 4 well project)

timeline.summary: The board approved payment application number six from Papito Construction for site work performed on the Water District No. 4 new well project. Approved by voice vote with no substantive discussion (Vataj moved, DiGiacinto seconded).

cases.name: Agreement with Northeast Westchester Special Recreation for 2026

timeline.summary: The board authorized the supervisor to sign the 2026 agreement with Northeast Westchester Special Recreation. Adopted by voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Salary Increases for Department Head / Non-Union Employees (effective Jan 1, 2026)

timeline.summary: The board considered salary increases for department-head and non-union employees retroactive to January 1, 2026. DiGiacinto voted no and requested a roll call, objecting not to the raises themselves but to the methodology used to determine them, which she said differs from comparable municipalities; discussion was limited because details were set in executive session. The resolution was adopted 4-1 (Berra aye, Vataj aye, DiGiacinto no, Hussain aye, Rende yes).

cases.name: Appointments to the Town Hall Advisory Committee

timeline.summary: The board appointed Alan Blum, Diana Barrera, George Dropo, Howard Fisher, Susan Geffen, and Rich Rosen to the town hall advisory committee, an initial list with more names to follow. After discussion led by Berra, the board changed Town Planner Adam Kaufman from a committee member to a non-member advisor/resource, to preserve the committee's perceived independence and public trust. Adopted as modified by voice vote.

cases.name: Alcohol Permit — Katona Classic Stage Reception at Whippoorwill Hall

timeline.summary: The board approved an alcoholic-beverage permit for a Katona Classic Stage reception at Whippoorwill Hall on March 14 and 28, 2026, by voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Alcohol Permit — Atlantic Westchester Company Picnic at Lombardy Park
