Note: 'Sonny Vataj' does NOT appear as a board member (he joins in 2026); a 'Bissell Vitage' named in the closing-in-memory list is a resident (brother of the Armonk fire captain), not the councilman, and was not attributed. Guest County Executive Ken Jenkins is an elected official, not town staff. Some voice-vote-only procedural items had no individual attribution.

meetings.meetingSummary: The Town Board reconvened from an executive session (advice of counsel on a contract matter) and opened with a presentation by high-school intern Jenny Hsu, who read her prize-worthy essay on North Castle's Revolutionary War history. The board held and closed a public hearing granting Mianus River Gorge a special-use permit for a scientific research center, handled a long slate of miscellaneous items, agreements, and appointments, and authorized a first amendment to the Toll Brothers water contribution agreement that will finally bring Westchester Joint Water Works supply into town. Much of the meeting was consumed by contentious debate over the highway facility, the town-hall RFEI process (and a councilmember email criticized as a political scare tactic), and two personnel/labor policies that were ultimately tabled for a clean redraft. The evening closed with a memorial for longtime resident Harry Tompkins.
meetings.durationNote: Reconvened into public session from executive session (advice of counsel, contract). Full board present (Rende, DiGiacinto, Hussain, Milim, Berra); no absences noted.

cases.name: High School Intern Presentation — Jenny Hsu 250th Anniversary Essay
cases.applicant: Town Clerk's Office / North Castle High School Internship Program
cases.summary: Intern Jenny Hsu, working through the Town Clerk's office, read an original essay on North Castle's role in the American Revolution written for the NY Association of Towns' 250th-anniversary documentary project. Board members praised the essay warmly and the Supervisor asked her to return to read it during the town's 2026 celebration and to place a copy in the town time capsule. Ceremonial item with no vote.
cases.publicComment: Intern Jenny Hsu read her essay; Judge Susan Scheimer spoke in support of adding it to the time capsule. Uniformly warm, celebratory tone.

memberPositions.evidence: Graded the essay 'an A plus plus plus' and praised its style and language as beautiful.
Praised the intern program, asked her to read the essay at the 250th celebration and place it in the time capsule.
Tied the intern's civic effort to his own daughter's essay award, expressing hope for young people in government.

cases.name: Ethics Code Amendments — Resumption of Public Hearing
cases.summary: The Ethics Board chair asked, during public comment, to resume the ethics-code public hearing (commenced April 9) on September 24. The board discussed that special counsel Bob Spolzino delivered his opinion May 28 but no board member has yet submitted written comments to counsel; the Supervisor and members set August 27 as the deadline for member comments. Counsel (Roland) advised that if substantive changes are made the existing hearing must be closed and a new hearing re-noticed and republished. No formal vote; targeted for the September 24 meeting.
cases.publicComment: The Ethics Board chair spoke, requesting a firm date to resume the hearing; cooperative but pressing for progress.

memberPositions.evidence: Committed to putting the item on the exec-session and reopening the hearing once counsel's response is in; accepted the Sept 24 target.
Clarified the comment deadline was August 13 vs September and agreed to get her comments done, before the extended Aug 27 date.

cases.name: Mianus River Gorge — Special Use Permit for Scientific Research Center
cases.applicant: Mianus River Gorge Inc. (Rod Christie, Executive Director)
cases.summary: The board opened and closed a public hearing on a special-use permit letting Mianus River Gorge, in operation since 1953, formalize/expand its scientific research center on ~960-1,200 protected acres in a residential zone. No neighbors spoke in favor or opposition. The board adopted a negative SEQRA declaration and the resolution granting the permit; site-plan approval to follow at the Planning Board. Motions carried unanimously by voice vote.
cases.publicComment: Applicant Rod Christie spoke; no neighbors or members of the public objected.

memberPositions.evidence: Called the organization wonderful and said the town is proud to have Mianus River Gorge; thanked them for preserving a magnificent spot.

Had no problem with the application but flagged that the two-persons-per-acre standard could theoretically permit 1,800+ people and mused about tightening special-use-permit requirements in future cases; satisfied given no comparable large parcels exist.

cases.name: Approval of Town Board Minutes — July 23, 2025
cases.summary: The board approved the town board minutes from July 23, 2025 by unanimous voice vote. Routine.

cases.name: United Hardware & Convenience — Special Use Permit for Outdoor Propane Sales
cases.summary: The board voted to receive United Hardware's special-use-permit application to sell/exchange small propane tanks from a caged container, refer it to the county planning board, and schedule a public hearing for September 10, 2025. Town Planner Adam Kaufman noted the applicant has not yet completed all required documents and staff are following up. Motion carried.

memberPositions.evidence: Living on that side of town, called it a great local resource, praised the store and welcomed convenient propane exchange.

cases.name: Letter from Board of Fire Commissioners — North Castle South Fire District No. 1
cases.applicant: Board of Fire Commissioners, North Castle South Fire District No. 1
cases.summary: The board received an August 4 letter in which the fire district refused to sign an agreement, cited aging Water District 1 infrastructure, and stated it would not use newly installed hydrants at Quarry Heights without flow-test data. The Supervisor and members expressed strong concern that a fire district would publicly commit in writing not to use available hydrants; the Supervisor plans to meet with the commissioners to understand the dispute. Received; no vote beyond acceptance.

memberPositions.evidence: Called it a big concern that the district would put in a public document that it would refuse to use hydrants; pledged to meet the commissioners to get to the bottom of the disagreement.
Fully agreed, said she doesn't understand the refusal to sign or to use hydrants; one can want the aging Water District 1 infrastructure fixed and still expect a fire department to use hydrants.

cases.name: Dog Park Expenses — Authorization to Use Fund Balance
cases.summary: The board approved a memo from the Director of Finance authorizing use of fund balance to pay dog-park expenses, covering fencing, a two-sided dog water fountain, signage, and a water line. The project was built largely in-house by highway and maintenance staff, saving money. Motion carried; grand opening/ribbon-cutting anticipated in weeks.

memberPositions.evidence: Publicly thanked highway and maintenance staff for building the dog park in-house, saving money and building staff pride.

cases.name: Highway Department Equipment & Vehicle Purchase (Budgeted + CHIPS Funds)
cases.summary: The board approved a memo from Highway General Foreman Jamie Norris authorizing purchase of equipment and vehicles using budgeted and CHIPS reimbursement funds. Members praised the detailed memo; the Supervisor and a member discussed claiming CHIPS money promptly since the state holds it without interest, and noted long lead times on equipment. Motion carried by voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Complimented Jamie Norris on a detailed memo she had no questions about and was happy to make the motion.
Praised the foreman's push to maximize auction/trade-in value and urged claiming CHIPS money as soon as legitimate rather than leaving it in the state's coffers earning no interest.
Explained CHIPS mechanics and, though a little concerned about the level of equipment spending this year, agreed it made sense given long delivery times.

cases.name: Highway Facility, Town Hall Project & RFEI — Policy Discussion
cases.summary: A prolonged, heated discussion branched off the equipment purchase into the town's deferred highway facility and town-hall projects and the town-hall RFEI (request for expressions of interest). One faction pushed to resolve the highway facility quickly, arguing the current yard is a poor gateway to the historic downtown and that a Butler-building band-aid would waste money; another member wanted to keep the highway yard in place and screen it with landscaping and objected to the RFEI's timing, transparency, and an implication that the board wants residential development. The Supervisor forcefully defended the RFEI as merely fact-finding and accused a member's town-wide email of being a political scare tactic. No decision or vote; the matter remains unresolved with a work session planned.

memberPositions.evidence: Insisted the town needs a full highway 'facility' (not a garage) and that town hall/court conditions are unsafe; defended the RFEI as non-binding fact-finding and sharply criticized a member's email as false, politically motivated scare tactics.

Objected to the RFEI's timing and lack of transparency (document not public until after the vote), defended her email as quoting the RFEI, and argued the highway yard should stay put and be screened with landscaping.

Expressed strong urgency to resolve the highway facility and town hall quickly and floated a phased approach; said keeping the highway yard as the town's entrance makes no sense and that being in government has been a challenge given the slow pace.
Framed as someone who could move quickly on the highway yard, seen as an achievable near-term project; engaged pragmatically on getting it done.

cases.name: Alcohol Permit — State of Play Productions at Whippoorwill Hall
cases.summary: The board approved an alcohol-permit application for receptions following theatrical performances at Whippoorwill Hall September 4-7, 2025. The Supervisor asked Administrator Kevin to verify the new group's track record in other communities. Motion carried by voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Approved but asked staff to confirm the new group's clean record and past performance in other communities.

cases.name: Revised Workplace Violence Policy
cases.summary: The board initially adopted the revised workplace violence policy with an added 'reasonable person' standard, then rescinded that vote so both this and the sexual-harassment policy could be handled together. It was tabled to a September 10 executive session with labor counsel to produce a clean redraft, targeting a September 24 vote. Councilmember Berra had multiple drafting concerns; other members deferred to labor counsel.

memberPositions.evidence: Advocated adding a 'reasonable person' standard to both policies and proposed adopting only labor counsel's accepted changes plus that standard.
Expressed full faith in labor counsel's work and pushed to move forward rather than delay, ultimately agreeing to rescind and table for a clean version.
Raised concerns that courts' reasonableness standard should be incorporated and that disciplinary determinations rest with the town board; pressed for changes.

cases.name: Revised Sexual Harassment Policy
cases.summary: The board debated the revised sexual-harassment policy at length. Councilmember Berra had submitted markups (e.g., substituting 'town board' for 'supervisor,' and adding a right to counsel for the accused), some accepted and some rejected by labor counsel on legal grounds (Civil Service Law §75). Other members (DiGiacinto, Hussain, Milim) were comfortable deferring to labor counsel's expertise but agreed no clean consolidated document existed. On counsel Roland's advice the item was tabled to a September 10 exec session for a clean redraft and a September 24 vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Author of the markups; argued for 'town board' over 'supervisor,' for a right to counsel for the accused, and felt labor counsel misunderstood several of his points.
Deferred to labor counsel, saying she didn't want to keep adding attorney fees to nitpick a phrase and was fine with the policy as written.
Said he saw the comments and counsel's answers and was fine with counsel's responses.
Said the board doesn't always have to take a hired expert's advice and it's the board's decision to own; respected Berra's disagreement but was okay with the policy and proposed a compromise motion.
Trusted labor counsel's legal-based responses and grew frustrated with what he saw as a pattern of last-minute member comments, but agreed to table for a clean version.

cases.name: Consent Judgment & Tax Refund — Stonewall LLC (2019-2023)
cases.summary: The board received a consent judgment and authorized payment of a tax refund to Stonewall LLC for the 2019-2023 tax years. Motion carried by voice vote. Routine tax-certiorari settlement.

cases.name: Prison Transportation Agreement — Westchester County Dept. of Correction (2025-2026)
cases.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign the 2025-2026 prison transportation agreement with the Westchester County Department of Correction. Town Attorney Roland confirmed it is identical to prior years' agreements. Motion carried.

cases.name: Trust for Public Land — Conservation Finance Feasibility & Technical Assistance
cases.applicant: Trust for Public Land / Open Space Committee
cases.summary: The board approved three related actions with the Trust for Public Land: authorizing a letter requesting technical advice on funding sources for land conservation and open space, receiving TPL's conservation finance feasibility proposal (dated Aug 5, 2025) with referral to the town attorneys, and authorizing the Supervisor to sign the TPL professional services agreement subject to attorney approval. Each carried by voice vote. Praise was given to Planner Adam Kaufman and Carey Kazak / the Open Space Committee for their work.
cases.publicComment: An Open Space Committee member raised a brief clarifying question; supportive tone.

memberPositions.evidence: Expressed strong appreciation for Adam Kaufman, Carey Kazak, and the Open Space Committee's hard work, stressing that conserving open space is what makes the town special.

cases.name: Police Mutual Aid & Rapid Response Plan — Westchester County IMA (2025-2030)
cases.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign an intermunicipal mutual-aid and rapid-response plan for the police departments of Westchester County for the period July 31, 2025 to July 30, 2030. Motion carried by voice vote.

cases.name: First Amendment — Water Contribution & Capital Expenditure Agreement (Toll Brothers / Water District 4)
cases.applicant: Toll Brothers (Airport Campus assignee) / Water District 4
cases.summary: The board authorized a first amendment to the water contribution and capital expenditure agreement under which Toll Brothers extends water from Westchester Joint Water Works via a new line, tank, and pump house, ultimately allowing Water District 4 to draw on an inexhaustible public supply. Toll's contribution rises to nearly $3M as its share of work escalates to just under $5M while the town's Water District 4 portion drops, netting the town roughly $200,000 positive with a 50/50 cost-share above $5M. Counsel Roland explained the terms; motion carried. The Supervisor hailed the long-sought reliable water source as a major community benefit.

memberPositions.evidence: Called it a rare opportunity to finally get clean, inexhaustible public water into town after decades of failed test wells; framed the development project as a great community benefit.
Made the motion to authorize the amendment.
Supported the outcome but was surprised the Toll portion grew more expensive and objected to being forced to approve same-day; urged pressing harder on details in future agreements.

cases.name: Long Pond Park Advisory Committee — Reappointments & Appointment
cases.summary: The board reappointed Stephen Berman and Susan Scheimer and appointed John Wolf to the Long Pond Park Advisory Committee, each for three-year terms ending August 13, 2028. Supervisor Rende recused himself from the Berman vote (stating he need not file a written explanation under the ethics code). Members praised the appointees' commitment and thanked Kevin Hay for his work preserving Long Pond. Motions carried.

memberPositions.evidence: Praised all three interviewees as committed and sincere, delighted to have people willing to give time to preserving Long Pond.
Noted Long Pond is one of many places saved thanks to the town board and residents, thanking Kevin Hay.

cases.name: Resignation — Judy Kitt from Open Space Committee
cases.summary: The board accepted, with regret, Judy Kitt's letter of resignation from the Open Space Committee effective July 22, 2025, noting she had been a good member. Motion carried.

cases.name: Stipulation Agreements with Employees No. 2884 and No. 3244
cases.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign two employee stipulation agreements (Nos. 2884 and 3244). Councilmember Berra had submitted last-minute drafting comments that the Supervisor and DiGiacinto criticized as an unhelpful recurring pattern; other members were comfortable with the agreements as written. Each passed 4-0 with Berra abstaining (citing drafting/exposure concerns, not the substantive terms): DiGiacinto aye, Hussain aye, Milim aye, Rende aye, Berra abstain.

memberPositions.evidence: Abstained on both agreements, citing drafting concerns about how the agreements would work and potential exposure to the town, though not objecting to the substantive terms.
Voted aye and expressed frustration with Berra's last-minute comments, saying if he wants to be counsel he should step down as a council member; trusted labor counsel.
Voted aye and called the last-minute drafting comments a recurring pattern (referencing the 5G legislation experience).
Voted aye; said he read Berra's comments but found them not material enough to matter and was fine with the agreement as written.
Voted aye, agreeing with Milim that Berra is a fully elected member entitled to raise comments but that the agreement was fine as it stands.

cases.name: Recreation Facilities Update — Turf Field, Pool Upgrades, Clove Road Field
cases.summary: During administrator and liaison updates the board discussed the turf-field project (fence installed, utility markout done, site survey next), planned pool upgrades (deck removal, releveling/repairing the good-condition stainless gutters, resurfacing, hillside retaining/invasive removal, future locker-room work) to be bid and done over winter, and in-house improvements at Clove Road Field using reused topsoil and better drainage. Members discussed shade structures/pergolas and a possible donation line on pool permits, and noted the county's July 3 fireworks parking may end once the fields are improved. Informational, no vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Detailed the phased pool plan and in-house Clove Road field work, framing it as proactive maintenance that saves money.
Suggested planning pergolas/shady areas when redoing the pool deck and a voluntary capital-improvement donation line on pool permits.

cases.name: Water Conservation Advisory — Summer Drought
cases.summary: In a liaison update a member urged residents, on well or municipal water, to conserve amid a dry July/August, noting Sal reported some water bills spiking from ~$80 to over $1,000 from lawn watering and pool filling, with usage running 3-4x normal (charges rising steeply with volume). Informational.

memberPositions.evidence: Relayed her conversation with Sal about the lack of rain and urged residents to conserve water and turn off automatic sprinklers.

cases.name: Closing Memorial — Harry Tompkins
cases.summary: The Supervisor closed the meeting with a memorial tribute to longtime resident Harry Tompkins, an Eagle Scout who attended American Legion, Memorial Day, and Veterans Day ceremonies, praising his integrity and quiet patriotism. The board offered condolences to his family before adjourning.

memberPositions.evidence: Delivered a heartfelt tribute to Harry Tompkins' values, integrity, and service.

themes.note: Highway facility, town-hall RFEI, pool/turf, and Toll water infrastructure dominated the meeting, with the highway/town-hall debate sharply contested.
RFEI transparency/timing and policy-redraft process drove much of the conflict between the Supervisor and Councilmembers DiGiacinto and Berra.
Landmark Toll/WJWW water agreement plus fire-hydrant dispute and a drought conservation advisory.
Long Pond appointments, a resignation, two employee stipulations (Berra abstaining), and two tabled labor policies.
Workplace-violence and sexual-harassment policy redrafts, tax-refund consent judgment, and reliance on labor counsel.
Dog park completed in-house, pool upgrades, turf and Clove Road fields, Long Pond stewardship.
Mianus River Gorge and United Hardware special-use permits handled smoothly.
Fire district's hydrant/agreement refusal drew concern; police mutual-aid and prison-transport agreements approved.
Intern essay presentation, Armonk community events, and Harry Tompkins memorial.
Police mutual aid, prison transportation, and Trust for Public Land engagement.
Trust for Public Land open-space conservation finance and Long Pond preservation.
CHIPS-funded highway purchases, dog-park fund balance, and a tax-certiorari refund.

staffInput.summary: Introduced the intern program and Jenny Hsu's essay; delivered community announcements (Armonk Has Heart art show, summer concerts, mobile passport unit, blood drive, Labor Day hours); read the Mianus public-hearing correspondence into the record.

Advised that substantive ethics-code changes would require closing and re-noticing the public hearing; explained the Toll/Water District 4 amendment terms; confirmed the prison-transport agreement matched prior years; recommended tabling both labor policies for a clean redraft rather than adopting from margin notes.

Reported on the turf-field project (fence, utility markout, upcoming site survey), dog-park progress, and pool upgrade planning; asked to verify the State of Play group's track record and to circulate a final workplace-violence policy.
Submitted the finance memo authorizing use of fund balance for dog-park expenses (rendered in the ASR as 'Basura').

Town Planner; addressed that the Mianus special-use permit is administrative and case-by-case with Planning Board site-plan review, noted United Hardware still owes application documents (staff following up), and was praised for open-space conservation work.

Water/Sewer superintendent; provided background on the fire district's hydrant demands and flow-test history (hydrants activated in January, seven months before the district's letter), and reported drought-driven spikes in water usage/bills.
Highway general foreman; submitted a detailed memo justifying equipment/vehicle purchases with budgeted and CHIPS funds, and led in-house work on the dog park and Clove Road field drainage.
Special counsel; delivered the May 28 ethics opinion referenced during the public-comment discussion on resuming the ethics-code hearing (not present).

meetings.attributionNote: Raw ASR with no speaker labels. The Supervisor's presiding voice (Joseph Rende, rendered as 'Grundy/Rendezvous/Endy') and roll-call votes were reliable anchors: the two stipulation-agreement roll calls explicitly named DiGiacinto, Hussain, Milim, and Berra (Berra abstaining). Jose Berra was further identifiable as the author of the policy markups ('J1'/'Jose that struck'). Full board present (Rende, DiGiacinto, Hussain, Milim, Berra); Berra attributed as this is a 2025 meeting. Ambiguity remains in the extended highway-facility/RFEI cross-talk, where the 'move quickly / highway yard makes no sense' voice is attributed to Berra at medium confidence (could be Milim), and in ceremonial cross-talk over the intern presentation. Name manglings normalized: Digacinto/Digacento=DiGiacinto, Hussein=Hussain, Millam/Millen=Milim, Barra/Bera=Berra. Staff names garbled: 'Basura'=Abbas (Comptroller); Judge Scheimer/Baldino and 'Craig' (labor counsel) referenced.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Town Board opened after an executive session and handled a heavy agenda dominated by the town's municipal-facilities effort: it granted a requested extension (to Oct. 20) of the RFEI for the town hall project and discussed the stalled 333 site and the eminent-domain question. Routine miscellaneous receipts, referrals, permits, water-district agreements, a costly emergency highway-garage roof replacement, new budget software (ClearGov), and several personnel actions were approved. The meeting was marked by two sharp, prolonged disputes: one over the transparency of the RFEI process, and one during liaison updates over moving the proposed ethics-code amendments to the agenda, which exposed deep friction among Supervisor Rende, Councilwoman DiGiacinto, and Councilman Berra.
meetings.durationNote: Quorum present. Councilman Milim participated remotely ("from far away"). Councilman Berra stepped out briefly for a personal matter and returned. Meeting opened at 5:30 with a prior executive session for board/committee interviews and contract matters.

cases.name: Extension of RFEI (Request for Expression of Interest) for the Town Hall Project
cases.applicant: Joseph R. Croco, architect (responder requesting extension)
cases.summary: A late-added agenda item and extensive public-comment topic: an architect responding to the town's RFEI for future municipal facilities requested an extension of the Sept. 22 deadline to Oct. 20. The board consistently agreed earlier that any granted extension would apply to all responders and that no responses would be reviewed until all were received. After lengthy debate about fairness, publicity, and whether granting it could 'taint' or delay the process, the board voted to grant the extension, publicize it widely (website, press, bulletin board, supervisor update), and inform anyone who submits on Sept. 22 that additional time is available. The item became a proxy for a broader fight over how open the RFEI process had been. Passed unanimously.
cases.publicComment: Several residents (Marilyn Hucfeld, an unnamed speaker, Sue Miller) questioned how they would know the deadline was extended, whether extensions had a limit, timing relative to the fall election, the fate of 333, and how long the highway crew must work in poor conditions. Tone was engaged and probing, generally constructive.

memberPositions.evidence: Strongly favored granting the extension to get the best ideas, said the town cannot 'kick the can down the road,' and defended the RFEI as open and transparent, objecting to it becoming a 'political football.'
Argued from remote that complaints the process is 'tainted' differ from it actually being tainted; cared about substance, not complaints that 'lack substance,' and urged granting the extension.
Said he 'wasn't crazy about the RFEI' and had voiced concern it was slowing the process, but concluded 'let's give it to him' now that they are here.
Went along with the extension but was 'really offended,' insisting she had objected in July to voting on the RFEI before the public could review it; defended her emails as informing the public.

cases.name: 333 Site / Eminent Domain and Municipal Facilities Direction
cases.summary: In response to resident questions, the Supervisor explained the town is not currently moving forward on 333 and has not taken the next step on eminent domain, because the community wanted alternatives explored. He recounted how a resident-plus-professional committee was considered but abandoned over cost and composition concerns, leading instead to the free RFEI approach. He stressed that any ultimate direction would go to a voter referendum. No action taken.
cases.publicComment: Resident Sue Miller asked whether anything was progressing at 333 and about timing relative to elections; the Supervisor said nothing is being negotiated and a future (possibly new) board plus a referendum would decide.

memberPositions.evidence: Warned 'the clock is ticking' on aging town buildings and that repeated delay forces spending on buildings 'not worth saving,' while committing to a public referendum on any final plan.

cases.name: Approval of Town Board Minutes — August 13, 2025
cases.summary: The board approved the Aug. 13, 2025 minutes. Councilman Berra flagged an apparent inconsistency in how the workplace-violence and sexual-harassment policy actions were recorded (adopted vs. tabled). The Town Clerk clarified the workplace-violence policy had been adopted with a 'reasonable person' clause and then rescinded and tabled along with the harassment policy; she agreed to add the reasonable-person clause note. Approved after the clarification.

memberPositions.evidence: Questioned the minutes, saying he didn't recall voting to adopt the policies and that a rescission should have been reflected; accepted the Clerk's clarification.

cases.name: Daughters of Liberty Legacy Letter — Historic Designation of Two Mount Misery Parcels; Referral to Landmark Preservation Committee
cases.applicant: Cynthia Abbott Coffee, Daughters of Liberty Legacy
cases.summary: The board received a letter from Cynthia Abbott Coffee requesting historical designation of two town parcels on Mount Misery and referred the matter to the Landmark Preservation Committee (LPC). Members confirmed the LPC referral was included and noted the requester may later make a presentation. Received and referred unanimously.

cases.name: KSCJ Consulting Memo — New Street Names/Addresses for Eagle Ridge; Referral to E911 Coordinator
cases.summary: The board received a KSCJ Consulting memo (dated Jan. 13, 2025) assigning new street names and addresses for the Eagle Ridge development and referred it to the town E911 coordinator. Councilman Berra recused himself, citing his association with IBM and consistency with prior Eagle Ridge recusals. Passed with Berra recused.

memberPositions.evidence: Recused himself given his IBM association, saying he had been recusing on anything Eagle Ridge for consistency.

cases.name: 45 Hurlingham LLC — Wetland Mitigation Planting Bond Extension and 5-Year Maintenance/Monitoring Bond Extension
cases.applicant: 45 Hurlingham LLC (represented by attorney Jerry Tortorella)
cases.summary: On the town engineer KSCJ's recommendation, the board approved a one-year extension of the wetland mitigation planting bond plus a corresponding five-year maintenance and monitoring bond extension. KSCJ had not yet verified all plantings were complete; attorney Jerry Tortorella explained plantings were done but a contractor changeover delayed the as-built certification, after which a town inspection would start the five-year monitoring clock. Members confirmed the bonds are de minimis cash amounts. Approved.

cases.name: Receipt of Long Pond Dam 2025 Dam Safety Inspection Report
cases.summary: The board voted to receive the Long Pond Dam 2025 dam safety inspection report. Supervisor Rende recused himself as he has in the past. Received.

memberPositions.evidence: Recused himself from receipt of the Long Pond Dam report as in prior instances.

cases.name: Payment Requisition #1 to Populito Construction — Water District 4 New Well Building Site Work
cases.summary: The board approved payment requisition #1 to Populito Construction for site work at the Water District 4 new well building; the Supervisor noted the work is progressing well. Discussion with Water/Sewer superintendent 'Sal' pivoted to repurposing a town-owned 3,000-gallon fuel tank (from the old tennis-bubble mechanicals at Community Park) for a water-facility generator rather than leaving it unused. Approved.

memberPositions.evidence: Reported the well-building work is progressing and pushed to find an alternative town use for the valuable 3,000-gallon fuel tank rather than scrapping it.

cases.name: Receipt of Letter from Patricia Ann Colombo (dated August 10, 2025)
cases.summary: The board voted to receive a letter from Patricia Ann Colombo dated Aug. 10, 2025, with no substantive discussion. Received.

cases.name: Film Permit — Patch Bay Presence Productions LLC, 15 Middle Patent Road
cases.summary: The board approved a film permit for Patch Bay Presence Productions LLC to shoot a feature film at 15 Middle Patent Road on Sept. 30–Oct. 1, 2025. Members confirmed the PDF was reviewed and off-site parking arranged; police (Tom McCormick) coordinated staging at the Summit Club as before, with the production described as considerate neighbors previously. Approved.

cases.name: Autism Science Foundation Rides Fair Charity Cycling Event — Town Road & Pool Parking Lot Use
cases.address: Town road and pool parking lot
cases.summary: The board approved a request from the Autism Science Foundation to use a town road and the pool parking lot for a charity cycling 'rides fair' for autism research on Oct. 4, 2025. The application was amended to bar road spray-paint marking (signs only, to be removed after), and the same group ran it smoothly last year with two applicant-paid police officers. Approved.

cases.name: Authorization to Sign Agreement with ClearGov for New Budget Software
cases.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign an agreement with ClearGov for new budget software, discovered by the Supervisor, Town Administrator Kevin, and Comptroller Abbas at professional conferences. Members praised it as a transparency tool that presents the budget with graphs and pie charts for the public, with a possible capital-planning add-on for five- and ten-year planning. Enthusiastically approved.

memberPositions.evidence: Called it a great tool he first saw at the Association of Towns that will help the public understand the budget; endorsed adding the capital-planning module.
Enthusiastic about transparency for the public — 'easy to read,' 'great for our departments' — and credited Kevin and Abbas.
Noted colleagues in other municipalities gave good public feedback and called it money well spent.

cases.name: Stipulation of Agreement with CSEA Unit 2 — Add Water Treatment Operator 2A Position
cases.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign a stipulation of agreement with CSEA Unit 2 adding the Water Treatment Operator 2A position to the collective bargaining agreement. Approved with little discussion.

cases.name: Westchester Joint Water Works — Water District 9 Corey Heights Water Supply Improvements (Water Supply Agreement & Bill of Sale)
cases.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign two agreements for Water District 9 Corey Heights improvements — a water supply agreement and a bill of sale/assumption of obligations transferring the public water mains. Superintendent Sal flagged that Section 5 (page 4), covering NYC DEP per-capita charges and a needed population determination, must be clarified with NYC before it is finalized. The board approved the water supply agreement subject to clarification to the town attorney's satisfaction in consultation with Sal, and separately approved the bill of sale. Two connections are active; the other nine await DEC. Adopted with conditions.

memberPositions.evidence: Made the motion to authorize the water supply agreement subject to clarifying Section 5 to the satisfaction of the town attorney in consultation with Sal.

cases.name: Highway Garage Roof Replacement — ELQ Industries via White Plains Job Order Contracting Program
cases.applicant: ELQ Industries (via Gordian / City of White Plains job order contracting)
cases.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign an agreement with ELQ Industries, via the White Plains job order contracting program, to replace the leaking highway garage roof, to be paid from fund balance since maintenance lines are insufficient. Members lamented the near-$200,000 cost, noting prior estimates of ~$150K and ~$170K in past years were never acted on, on a building 'not even worth saving,' but agreed the holes endanger workers and equipment. The ~10-day job should finish before winter closes the garage. Approved with the fund-balance funding notation.

memberPositions.evidence: Frustrated that delay drove the cost from ~$150K to nearly $200K on a building not worth saving, but insisted 'we can't wait any longer' because workers are affected.
Said 'the amount is crazy' but agreed it must be done because there are holes in the roof harming workers and equipment.

cases.name: Stipend for Danielle D. Tomas, Senior Office Assistant, Building Department
cases.summary: The board authorized a stipend for Danielle D. Tomas, senior office assistant in the Building Department, effective Sept. 11, 2025, with members noting she is 'doing the job of two people.' Approved.

cases.name: Resignations/Retirements — Virginia Garcia and Jane Purser (North Castle Public Library)
cases.summary: The board accepted, with regret and good wishes, a retirement resignation from library assistant Virginia Garcia (effective Sept. 12, 2025) and a resignation from library hourly clerk Jane Purser (effective Aug. 9, 2025). Both accepted.

cases.name: Conference Travel Authorizations — Assessor and Highway Personnel
cases.summary: The board approved two travel authorizations: Town Assessor Georgeanne Richardson to attend the NYS Assessors Association Fall Conference in Lake George, Oct. 6–9, with a town vehicle; and Highway General Foreman Jamie Norris to attend the League of Municipalities Conference in Atlantic City, Nov. 18–20, with lead mechanic Matthew Harrisch and a town vehicle. Both approved. A consensus agenda was also approved.

cases.name: Proposed Ethics Code Amendments — Agenda Scheduling and Distribution Dispute
cases.applicant: Ethics Board / Town Board Ethics Liaison
cases.summary: During liaison updates, Councilman Berra (ethics liaison) pressed to distribute special counsel Bob Spolzino's revised ethics-code documents and DiGiacinto's comments and to put receipt of the revised law on the next agenda so a public hearing could be scheduled. The Supervisor said the confidential materials would be distributed the next day but that the item would go on the agenda only after the board deliberates it in executive session, and accused Berra of overreaching as liaison and injecting personal views into the ethics board's work. The exchange escalated into a heated, personal argument involving Rende, Berra, and DiGiacinto over agenda-setting authority (two members may request an item in writing; the Supervisor otherwise sets the agenda), staff use, and prior email blasts. No action taken.

memberPositions.evidence: As ethics liaison pushed to distribute the revised code and comments promptly and to schedule receipt and a public hearing, arguing board members have the right to request agenda items and that the matter has dragged on.
Backed moving the item forward and defended board members' right to request agenda items, while cautioning that privileged documents not be shared with the ethics board.

Refused to agenda it until after executive-session deliberation, defended his authority to set the agenda, and accused Berra of overreaching and putting personal feelings into the ethics code and DiGiacinto of using liaison update to badger him.
Stated he had no additional comments or questions on the ethics matter.

cases.name: Con Edison Proposed 2026 Rate Hikes — Resident Advocacy Appeal
cases.summary: In her liaison update, Councilwoman DiGiacinto urged residents to email State Senator Shelley Mayer and Assemblyman Chris Burdick (both of whom attended her North White Plains gathering) opposing Con Edison's proposed 2026 delivery rate hikes and to have them forward concerns to the Governor and Public Service Commission. The Supervisor confirmed the town had put out messaging. No action taken.

memberPositions.evidence: Called the proposed Con Ed delivery increases 'incredible' and urged residents to email state legislators to fight the hikes.

cases.name: North Castle Public Library Summer Programs Update and Fall Programming
cases.summary: Councilman Hussain shared a screen presentation of the library's summer statistics — over 30,000 total checkouts including 20,000+ books, 2,800+ audio, 8,000+ ebooks, 310 programs, ~9,000 youth attendees, and ~6,000 books read — and promoted fall programming (meditation, art history, knitting, cooking demos) and the Armonk outdoor art show whose proceeds fund library programs. Celebratory discussion, no action.

memberPositions.evidence: Presented the library's summer stats and gave 'a shout out' to the library, tying reading to lifelong enrichment for kids and encouraging support via the art show and fall programs.

cases.name: Supervisor Update — Parks, Turf Field, Dog Park, Water Projects, and Sidewalk Planning
cases.summary: The Supervisor reported progress across many projects: the turf field, the nearly complete dog park (targeting an early-October ribbon cutting), Clove Road field work, the Quarry Heights playground (with an engineer reviewing drainage from an impervious pad), the swimming pool improvements, School Street and the Water 8-to-4 connection waterline, Quarry Heights water expansion, and cleanup of the Sands Mills historic site. He also asked staff to phase long-deferred sidewalk improvements (a 2005 plan) rather than shelving them as too costly. DiGiacinto pushed to prioritize sidewalks across all three hamlets, noting North White Plains residents walk to the train and stores, not just for exercise. Discussion only.

memberPositions.evidence: Enthusiastically catalogued progress on turf field, dog park, waterlines and other projects and urged phasing the long-stalled sidewalk plan into 'palatable' stages.
Insisted sidewalk planning cover all three hamlets and prioritize need, noting North White Plains residents walk to the train and stores, not only Armonk.

cases.name: Community Announcements and 914Cares Volunteer Appeal
cases.summary: Town Clerk Allison Simon announced the 9/11 memorial at Wampus Brook Park, the Armonk Outdoor Art Show (Sept. 27 weekend) and 'Armonk Has Heart' sculpture auction benefiting the libraries, a St. Stephen's string trio concert, a county shredder truck (Oct. 21), and that former town intern Jenny Hsu became a finalist recognizing the town's Revolutionary/1776 role. On DiGiacinto's behalf, the board made an extended plea for volunteers and donations for 914Cares, an Armonk nonprofit distributing clothing and necessities to needy children and families across Westchester. The Supervisor also opened with a personal tribute to civility following the assassination of Charlie Kirk. Announcements only.

memberPositions.evidence: Delivered a lengthy, heartfelt appeal for 914Cares volunteers, describing the sorting/matching work and the organization's reach among needy families.

themes.note: Town-hall RFEI, 333, highway-garage roof, water-district builds, turf/dog park, and pool dominated the meeting.
Two bitter disputes — RFEI transparency and ethics-code agenda scheduling — over process, agenda-setting authority, and email blasts.
Water District 4 well payment, WD9 Corey Heights agreements, CSEA operator position, and Water 8-to-4 connection.
Building Dept stipend, two library resignations, and conference travel authorizations.
ClearGov budget-transparency software approved; garage roof funded from fund balance; Con Ed rate-hike concern.
Art show, 914Cares, film and cycling permits, library programs, and historic-site recognition.
Dog park nearing completion, turf field, pool improvements, and library programming celebrated.
Special counsel's ethics-code revisions and privileged documents were central to the liaison-update dispute.
Con Ed rate hikes and sidewalk prioritization across all three hamlets raised as resident issues.

staffInput.summary: Delivered community announcements (9/11 memorial, art show, concerts, shredder truck, intern Jenny Hsu finalist), confirmed permit application reviews and off-site parking provisions, tracked motions/seconds, and clarified the minutes' policy rescission wording.

Advised on the fairness/legal risk of granting the RFEI extension (not binding, no legal cause of action, but potential process-taint and developer-goodwill concerns) and confirmed the WD9 agreements largely mirror the Water 8 (King Street) agreements.
Championed the ClearGov budget software after seeing it at the administrators' conference, and coordinated the highway-garage roof project timing/permits and fund-balance funding.

Water/Sewer superintendent: reported the WD4 well work progressing, flagged the unresolved NYC DEP per-capita/population clause in the WD9 water supply agreement, and proposed reusing a town-owned 3,000-gallon fuel tank for a water-facility generator.
Special counsel who drafted the revised ethics code and responded to DiGiacinto's comments; his confidential documents were at the center of the ethics-code agenda dispute.

meetings.attributionNote: The presiding/supervisor voice was attributed to Joseph Rende; Barbara DiGiacinto and Jose Berra were clearly identifiable as the two members in the contested RFEI and ethics exchanges (Berra named in roll-call/recusal and as ethics liaison). Saleem Hussain self-identified via the library presentation. Matt Milim participated remotely and was addressed by name ('Matt, you still with us?'). This is a 2025 meeting so Jose Berra is attributed and Sonny Vataj does not appear. ASR garbling normalized (DiGiacinto, Milim, Spolzino). Staff (Allison Simon, Roland, Kevin, Sal, Bob Spolzino) and outside attorney Jerry Tortorella kept out of memberPositions. No absences noted beyond Berra briefly stepping out and Milim attending remotely.

meetings.meetingSummary: The Town Board opened late after a court arraignment tied up the courtroom, then held a work session with the Open Space Committee and Westchester County GIS staff on a new digital Natural Resources Inventory map. After public-service announcements (police re-accreditation, a new high-school internship program, Clove Field and dog-park updates) and public comment urging action on ethics-code amendments, the board worked through routine miscellaneous, agreement, and personnel items. The signature debate was a change order on the Community Park artificial-turf project: the board unanimously approved the sports-line package but split on adding a ~$45K North Castle Eagle logo (approved 3 aye, 1 no, 1 abstain). A major water-district item — extending Water District 4 to Byram Hills High School, Brentwood/Summit, and supplementing Windmill's Water District 2 — was approved.
meetings.durationNote: Meeting delayed by a court arraignment that needed the courtroom; reopened publicly at ~5:30 PM after an executive session (contracts, boards/committees, advice of counsel). Quorum present. Councilwoman DiGiacinto participated remotely via Zoom because she was unwell; board reconvened in executive session and did not return to public session afterward.

cases.name: Open Space Committee Work Session — Digital Natural Resources Inventory (NRI) Map
cases.applicant: Open Space Committee (Carrie Kasak, chair) with Westchester County GIS (Anna Geraldo Gomez)
cases.summary: Open Space Committee chair Carrie Kasak, Town Planner Adam Kaufman, and Westchester County GIS staff presented a web-based Natural Resources Inventory map layering wetlands, forests, slopes, tax parcels, zoning, and other data for every parcel in town, provided free by the county (saving the town thousands). It was described as phase one of a plan leading to a Mianus River Gorge conservation-scoring algorithm and a possible Community Preservation Fund referendum (real-estate transfer tax) via the Trust for Public Land. The tool will be posted publicly and is intended for all boards (Planning, ZBA, Conservation, Town Board). No vote; work session/discussion only.
cases.publicComment: Presentation by committee/county staff and Town Planner, not residents; uniformly enthusiastic reception.

memberPositions.evidence: Expressed gratitude for the 'impressive' work, praised the committee, Adam, and county for making a hard effort look simple and hoped it would help preserve open space and expand to other towns.
From Zoom: 'very grateful... incredible that this has not cost the town anything,' noting the county also saved the town money on the comprehensive-plan update.
Praised the county service and stressed how much county support goes into town operations; sees it aiding future open-space acquisition and planning.

cases.name: Recognition of Police Department State Re-Accreditation
cases.summary: Supervisor Rende reported the police department passed its five-year state accreditation review 'with flying colors,' with retired-chief assessors reviewing 112 processes and conducting unannounced ride-alongs and one-on-one interviews. He recognized Chief Simonson, Lt. Huffnagel, Sgts. Joel Thomas and Chris Costa, and the whole department. Board members echoed pride and noted the voluntary process aids public safety and possibly insurance costs. No formal action.

memberPositions.evidence: 'How blessed we are to have a department like this'; detailed praise of the accreditation results.
Noted the accreditation 'helps them keep us safe,' has practical impact and likely lowers insurance costs despite the work required.

cases.name: Welcome of Fall High-School Interns / Town Internship Program
cases.applicant: Town internship program (spearheaded by Josephine Egan)
cases.summary: The board welcomed two new high-school interns, Arnhem Das and Jack McNulty, in the town's newly formed rotating internship program (crediting Josephine Egan and the town clerk/administrator offices). Both interns spoke about their interest in local government. Board members encouraged them to ask questions and even criticize the board. No formal action.
cases.publicComment: The two student interns addressed the board expressing enthusiasm; warmly received.

memberPositions.evidence: From Zoom: 'very exciting to have high school students that want to participate in local government,' hopes it becomes a lifelong passion.
Thanked Josephine Egan for starting the program; 'this is where the rubber meets the road,' encouraged the interns to reach out to anyone on the board.

cases.name: Clove Field / Community Park Field Improvement Update
cases.summary: Supervisor Rende updated on the Clove Field project: a next-day meeting with Highway, Parks, and staff (Jamie, Kevin, Matt, Joe Chamele) to set a firm start date, likely early the following week, beginning with drainage rerouting. Topsoil saved from Community Park is stockpiled for relocation to Clove Road, and work is coordinated with contractor Matt DeRosa's turf schedule to finish before winter sod season. Discussion only, including a resident/attendee who asked about timing.
cases.publicComment: An attendee (who had emailed) came to the mic; expressed gratitude the project is moving forward and shared observations from watching the IBM turf-field installation.

memberPositions.evidence: Laid out drainage-first sequencing and the goal to have fields playable by spring.

cases.name: Ethics Board Proposed Ethics-Code Amendments (Resident Request for Action)
cases.summary: During public comment, resident Susan Scheimer (who helped draft the current code) urged the board to act on ethics-code amendments the Ethics Board proposed on January 8, asking that a new public hearing be noticed if that is what it takes to move forward. Supervisor Rende responded that the proposed changes would be discussed with counsel in that evening's executive session and that a new public hearing could likely be set by October 8. No formal action taken in public session.
cases.publicComment: Resident Susan Scheimer spoke, frustrated at months of delay ('let's get this show on the road'); tone insistent but constructive.

memberPositions.evidence: Said the original code 'is not as good as it can be' and committed to discussing amendments in executive session and setting a new public hearing by ~October 8.

cases.name: Approval of Town Board Meeting Minutes — September 10, 2025
cases.summary: The board approved the minutes of the September 10, 2025 meeting. Motion made and seconded; carried on a unanimous voice vote ('all in favor, aye'). Routine.

cases.name: Receipt of Letter from Francesca and Frederick Azada (received Sept 4, 2025)
cases.summary: The board voted to receive a letter dated/received September 4, 2025 from Francesca and Frederick Azada, submitted as property owners. Brief clarifying discussion on the name/status; motion made, seconded, and carried by voice vote. Routine receipt.

cases.name: Petition Opposing Basketball 'Court' at Quarry Heights Park
cases.address: Quarry Heights Park, North White Plains
cases.summary: The board formally received a resident petition opposing construction of a basketball court at Quarry Heights Park. Members pushed back on the petition's accuracy, stressing the plan is a small permanent hoop and pad (not a full court, no parking lot), replacing a portable hoop that neighbors the Candreas installed years ago; the chief reported zero complaints about the existing portable hoop. The board voted to receive the petition (motion, second, voice vote) while signaling intent to proceed with the improvement, using pervious asphalt and stockpiled topsoil, and to consider refurbishing the playground in the 2026 budget. Members emphasized keeping kids off the road for safety.
cases.publicComment: Petition from neighborhood residents opposing the project; board viewed it as based on inaccurate assumptions and largely disagreed while remaining open to dialogue.

memberPositions.evidence: Defended the hoop at length: it's a pad not a court, praised the Candreas, checked with the chief (no complaints), and as a former teacher embraces sports to keep kids busy; wants the playground refurbished in the 2026 budget.
Framed it as a small neighborhood improvement, cited the safety of kids currently bouncing balls in the road, and offered to meet any resident to explain the plan.
Argued it's a park/playground, not a tournament venue, and that choosing to live next to a park means accepting the sounds of kids playing.

cases.name: Retroactive Special-Event Permit — Spectrum Painting/JB Auto Body Charity Car Show
cases.applicant: Spectrum Painting / JB Auto Body Works
cases.summary: The board granted retroactive approval of a special-event permit for a charity car show held Sunday, September 28 at 135 Bedford Road, benefiting a women's-cancer foundation. Approved by motion, second, and voice vote, with a request that organizers apply in advance next year. The discussion prompted a plan to revise the local law (with Town Planner Adam Kaufman) to let the board refer routine recurring special-event permits to professional staff rather than hold public hearings, targeting a November meeting.

memberPositions.evidence: Backed the good cause, praised the well-attended event, and pushed to streamline the permit process by referring routine events to staff instead of public hearings.

cases.name: Community Park Artificial-Turf Change Order No. 1 (Shaw Sports Turf) — Sports Lines & Eagle Logo
cases.summary: The board received a KSCJ Consulting memo and considered Shaw Sports Turf change order no. 1 on the Community Park artificial-turf project, covering added sports-line striping (for two micro soccer fields and a practice football field) and an optional North Castle Eagle logo; a negotiated reduction (3% on striping, 6% with the logo) was secured via Joe Chamele and Matt DeRosa. The board split the vote into two motions. The line package (~$29,677) passed unanimously (5-0). The Eagle logo (~$45,406 before reduction) passed by roll call 3 aye (Milim, Hussain, and presiding Supervisor Rende) to 1 no (DiGiacinto) with 1 abstention (Berra). DiGiacinto criticized the change-order process and the logo cost as cosmetic; supporters argued change orders are normal and the branding adds value.

memberPositions.evidence: Called the ~$45K Eagle cosmetic and 'not a need,' criticized that the added lines/fields weren't finalized before the turf vote, and voted no: 'a beautiful design... just too much money' out of fund balance.

Supported the line package as a wise investment but abstained on the Eagle: 'I love the Eagle... but I really would not spend the 40,000 plus,' suggesting a sign or plastic eagle instead and noting it would appear upside down on one field.
Explained how the Eagle idea arose, said he 'fell in love with it' and it 'looks great,' touted the fields' multi-sport versatility, while leaving the logo to the board's decision.

Defended consultant Joe Chamele ('throwing him under the bus... not fair'), called change orders a normal minor part of construction, and argued the Eagle branding matters for visiting teams; voted aye.
Brief statement that the logo is 'an excellent add on and worth the cost,' fully supporting the change order; voted aye in the roll call.

cases.name: Tie the Town Pink Campaign — Pink Ribbons Benefiting Soul Riders (Barn Hills)
cases.summary: The board approved the Barn Hills 'Tie the Town Pink' campaign to place pink ribbons around town (Main Street, Town Hall pillars and staircase railings) benefiting Soul Riders, a nonprofit supporting people impacted by cancer. Discussion focused on not rigidly capping the number at nine; the board approved it as proposed, allowing additional reasonable locations. Motion, second, and voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: As a breast-cancer survivor, called organizations like Soul Riders that offer support during treatment 'incredibly meaningful.'

cases.name: KSCJ Proposal — Water District 4 Extension (Byram Hills HS, Brentwood/Summit) and Supplement to Water District 2 (Windmill)
cases.summary: The board approved a KSCJ engineering-services proposal to study extending Water District 4 to Byram Hills High School and the proposed Brentwood/Summit community, and to supplement Water District 2 (Windmill) supply, authorizing the supervisor to sign. Water/Sewer Superintendent 'Sal' explained the engineering, elevations, hydraulics, pump-station needs, easements, added fire hydrants, and how selling water to Summit and Windmill creates efficiencies and backup supply while addressing stressed wells and PFAS at the high school. Members noted costs are recovered through district bonds paid by users. Approved by motion, second, and voice vote.
cases.publicComment: Water/Sewer Superintendent 'Sal' (staff) presented; no residents spoke.

memberPositions.evidence: Called the District 4 extension 'amazing' and 'big,' thanked Sal repeatedly, and explained that advanced costs return via district bonds paid by users.

Initially skeptical ('putting the cart before the horse') and less sold on focusing on the Summit, but after Sal's explanation of efficiencies and helping Windmill/high-school wells (PFAS), said 'I'm fully in support.'

cases.name: Purchase of Radios for Parks & Recreation (Metrocom Wireless, via County Contract)
cases.summary: The board approved purchasing radios for Parks & Recreation trucks and home bases from Metrocom Wireless through the Westchester County contract. Members noted this puts Highway, Police, and Parks on the same radio system, important for snow emergencies, bad-weather coordination, and school-district bus transportation. Motion, second, and unanimous voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Highlighted that Highway, Police, and now Parks can communicate on one system in snow emergencies, and that school buses are included.

cases.name: Stipulation Agreement — Town of North Castle, CSEA, and Employee No. 3420
cases.summary: The board authorized the supervisor to sign a stipulation agreement between the Town of North Castle, the CSEA, and employee number 3420. Approved by motion, second, and voice vote with no substantive discussion in public session.

cases.name: Excelsior Housing Group — Request to Extend RFEI Submission Deadline
cases.summary: Supervisor Rende raised a same-day letter from Excelsior Housing Group LLC, an interested RFEI respondent, requesting the submission deadline (currently extended to about October 20) be pushed to December 1. Rather than add it as a last-minute item, the board agreed to take it up at the October 8 meeting, with Rende suggesting a possible compromise November date. No action taken; deferred.

memberPositions.evidence: Suggested a November compromise rather than December 1 but left it to the board; comfortable deferring the item to the October 8 agenda.

cases.name: Personnel — Library/Board Appointments and Resignation
cases.summary: The board acted on four personnel items, each by motion, second, and unanimous voice vote: appointment of Jennifer Paglieli as Librarian (effective Sept. 25, 2025); acceptance 'with regret' of Mary Jacobs's resignation as hourly Library Clerk (effective Oct. 18, 2025); reappointment of Beira Bull Tata to the Architectural Review Board for a five-year term ending Sept. 30, 2030; and appointment of Eric Bell to the Library Board for a five-year term ending Dec. 31, 2030. The consensus agenda was also approved.

cases.name: Town Board Liaison Updates — Sustainability, Invasive Vines, Food-Waste Recycling, Art Show
cases.summary: In liaison updates, members recognized the Sustainability Committee and the invasive-vine volunteer group for staffing tables at the art show and access road to promote composting, recycling, and vine removal. The board discussed low uptake of the food-waste recycling program (about 90 of 850 bins sold) and committed to promoting it more, including recurring mentions in the supervisor update. The record-setting art show and its ~300+ volunteers were praised. No formal action.

memberPositions.evidence: Recognized the Sustainability Committee and invasive-vine group for their weekend outreach and praised the art-show volunteers.
Urged a continued push on the underused food-waste recycling program and pledged recurring promotion in his supervisor update.

themes.note: Turf change order (lines/Eagle), Clove Field, Quarry Heights hoop, and Parks radios dominated the action items.
Open Space NRI work session plus sustainability/invasive-vine and food-waste recycling liaison updates.
Enthusiastic approval of the Water District 4 extension to the high school, Brentwood/Summit, and Windmill supplement.
Turf fields, Clove Field, and water-line extensions are the town's major ongoing capital work.
Turf change order, water engineering proposal, radios, and CSEA stipulation; change-order process drew a split.
Fund-balance sensitivity drove the Eagle-logo dispute; cost recovery via water-district bonds discussed.
Police re-accreditation praised; radios and hoop safety framed around public safety.
Internship welcome, Tie the Town Pink, charity car show, art show, and community announcements.
Ethics-code amendment timing, special-event permit streamlining, and RFEI deferral.
Librarian and board appointments, a library-clerk resignation, and the CSEA stipulation.

staffInput.summary: Town Planner; explained how the digital NRI serves all boards as a central environmental-data hub and outlined the phased plan (NRI data, Mianus scoring algorithm, possible Community Preservation Fund referendum). Also drafting the local-law change to streamline special-event permits.

Water/Sewer Superintendent; detailed the engineering, hydraulics, pump-station and easement needs, added fire hydrants, and the cost/efficiency case for extending Water District 4 to the high school and selling/backup water to Summit and Windmill; also updated on the new well in construction (~350 gpm).

Announced community events (Staying Alive charity run Oct 4, Historical Society dinner, Oct 7 memorial, county shredder truck Oct 21) and reported food-waste bin sales (~90 of 850 ordered) and Tie the Town Pink ribbon locations.
Negotiated with consultant Joe Chamele and Matt DeRosa to reduce the turf change-order cost (3% on striping, 6% with logo) and supported permit/process coordination.

meetings.attributionNote: The transcript is unlabeled running ASR text; the presiding/supervisor voice (rendered 'Endy'/'Joe') is Joseph Rende, and the roll-call vote on the Eagle logo gave firm attribution: 'Councilman Millen' = Matt Milim (aye), 'Councilman Hussein' = Saleem Hussain (aye), 'Councilman Barra' = Jose Berra (abstain), 'Councilman Digicinto' = Barbara DiGiacinto (no, via Zoom), 'Supervisor Endy' = Joseph Rende (yes).
