Town Planner; presented the EV charging law history and IBM request, and recommended adding EV charging as a minor site-plan category and excluding EV spaces from off-street parking minimums; will redraft for January.

Special counsel; advised on the legal distinction between receiving vs. considering the rezone petition, on abstentions/liability, on treating the building demolition as a permissible contract addition, and on the bond resolution's delegation and permissive referendum.
Retiring Police Chief; formally recommended the provisional appointment of Mary Madsen as Animal Warden/Parking Enforcement Officer and conducted the swearing-in.
Police Lieutenant; presented the site investigation and photos supporting the Crossroad North one-way and prohibited-left-turn traffic law.

meetings.meetingSummary: The Town Board held its annual reorganizational meeting for 2026, opening with the swearing-in of newly elected Councilman Sonny Vataj and re-elected members (Supervisor Rende and Councilwoman DiGiacinto). Saleem Hussain was named Deputy Supervisor, and the board adopted the full organizational agenda (depositories, officer/secretary appointments, annual policies, master fee schedule, salary schedule, and numerous service, legal, fire/ambulance and intermunicipal agreements). Substantive water-infrastructure business dominated the miscellaneous agenda: payment applications for the School Street water main and Water District 4 well building, and a call for a public hearing on the long-awaited Water District 9 (Quarry Heights) extension. The board also received a short-term rental local law and an EV level-3 charging local law and scheduled public hearings for January 28, handled recreation equipment purchases, several permits, personnel resignations/appointments, liaison updates, and closed with in-memoriam tributes.
meetings.durationNote: Reorganizational meeting; opened 5:30pm (recessed to executive session for interviews/personnel/real-estate counsel), reconvened publicly, adjourned ~9:00pm. All five 2026 members present: Rende, DiGiacinto, Hussain, Berra, Vataj. Quorum present. Special counsel Bob Spolzino absent. Multiple recusals/abstentions noted (see cases and attributionNote).

cases.name: 2026 Reorganization — Oaths of Office and Deputy Supervisor Appointment
cases.summary: New Councilman Sonny Vataj was sworn in (a second, ceremonial oath by a visiting justice), and re-elected Supervisor Joseph Rende and Councilwoman Barbara DiGiacinto were recognized (DiGiacinto already re-sworn by the Town Clerk). Each gave brief remarks thanking residents. The board then appointed Saleem Hussain as Deputy Town Supervisor on a unanimous voice vote, with a member remarking it was 'a great choice.'
cases.publicComment: Resident Asad Ghulani congratulated the officials and praised the board's openness, pledging to attend meetings in person this year; warm, appreciative tone.

memberPositions.evidence: As a son of an immigrant thanked residents for their trust; 'I'm here for the right reasons... looking forward to serving each and every one of you.'
Grateful for renewed trust; pledged to carry out responsibilities and 'never forget that you the people are the ones who put me in this position.'
Presided over the swearing-in, thanked all residents and family, and asked Saleem Hussain to serve as his Deputy Supervisor.
Accepted the Deputy Supervisor role offered by the Supervisor.

cases.name: Organizational Agenda — Depositories, Officer/Secretary Appointments, Annual Policies, Fee Schedule and Salaries
cases.summary: The board adopted the bulk annual reorganization items on unanimous voice votes: designating depositories, authorizing ACH/wire/facsimile payment authority, and reappointing statutory officers and board secretaries (Town Clerk Allison Simon as Records Management/Access Officer, Registrar, and Board of Elections liaison; Deputy Clerk Maria Scharf; Director of Finance Abbas; Assessor Georgeanne Richardson; Confidential Secretary Josephine Egan; historians, ZBA/Planning/ARB secretaries; fire inspectors including new hire Henry Sieno; engineer KSCJ; town counsel Abrams Fensterman). It also readopted town policies (procurement, investment, workplace-violence, sexual-harassment, IT-usage, videoconferencing, vehicle), the 2026 master fee schedule, meeting schedule (2nd/4th Wednesdays 7:30pm), 72.5 cents/mile mileage, the 2026 salary installment schedule, code-of-ethics posting, and charge-card/advance-payment authorizations.

memberPositions.evidence: Questioned that the purchase-order/procurement policy is being revised; welcomed that a revised version would come to the next meeting ('I think that's important').
Noted the master fee schedule was adopted as-is but that staff (administrator, Adam Kaufman, Rob Melillo) would review it for code-driven changes to revisit later.
Gently advised the Supervisor he could read the salary dates 'as posted' rather than aloud, and to remind him of such shortcuts.

cases.name: Annual Service, Legal and Fire/Ambulance Agreements for 2026
cases.applicant: Various vendors/districts (KSCJ Consulting, Abrams Fensterman, Patrick Bliss Esq., labor counsel, Valhalla/North White Plains Ambulance, Banksville and Armonk fire districts)
cases.summary: As part of reorganization, the board authorized the Supervisor to execute the recurring 2026 professional and public-safety agreements on unanimous voice votes: legal services (Abrams Fensterman; Patrick Bliss for Justice Court; labor counsel), KSCJ Consulting for engineering, wetlands, and MS4 stormwater-management/IDDE services, and fire-protection and emergency-ambulance agreements for the ambulance district and Banksville/Armonk fire districts. These are routine annual renewals with no controversy.

cases.name: Long Pond Park District Agreement for 2026 (Member Recusal)
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle / Long Pond Park District
cases.summary: The board considered the 2026 agreement between the town and the North Castle Long Pond Park District. One council member announced a recusal on this item; the board confirmed no roll-call vote was required despite the recusal and passed it on a voice vote of the remaining members. The recusing member was referred to in the ASR as 'councilman Vera.'

memberPositions.evidence: 'You'll note that councilman Vera has recused from the vote' — a member recused on the Long Pond Park District agreement (ASR 'Vera'; attribution uncertain, see attributionNote).

cases.name: Approval of Town Board Minutes — December 10, 2025 (New Member Abstention)
cases.summary: The board approved the minutes of its December 10, 2025 meeting. The newly seated member abstained because he was not part of the board when those minutes were made (he attended only the executive session, which has no minutes), on the advice that he could not attest to their accuracy. The minutes were approved on a voice vote with that abstention noted.

memberPositions.evidence: As the new member not on the board in December 2025, he abstained from approving the December 10, 2025 minutes ('you weren't part of those minutes').

cases.name: Local Law — Regulation of Short-Term Rental of Homes
cases.summary: The board received the draft short-term rental (STR) local law, short environmental assessment forms, and a resident email (Tan Nguyen, Dec 18, 2025), then scheduled a public hearing for January 28, 2026. Following a Zoom meeting that day with Airbnb representatives (attended by the Planner, Town Administrator and counsel), the board opted to hold the referral to the town/county planning boards until a more finalized draft exists after a follow-up Airbnb meeting, while still setting the hearing date (which may be opened and adjourned/kept open). Rende stressed the town needs a defensible law 'with teeth' to pursue offenders. A council member pressed that a standalone (non-zoning) law still requires a mandatory referral at some point.
cases.publicComment: Applicants/originators were present and offered the chance to speak; they largely deferred given an extensive public hearing to come.

memberPositions.evidence: Pressed that as a standalone (non-zoning) law it is a mandatory referral to the planning boards at some point and that the referring agency has 30 days; Rende thanked 'Jose' for recognizing this.
Recognized a real need for the law but wanted to slow the process to ensure the law 'has some teeth' and can be upheld against court challenges before referral.

cases.name: Local Law — Amend EV Charging Station Definition (Sec. 355-4) to Permit Level 3 Charging
cases.summary: The board received the proposed local law amending the town code definition of 'electric vehicle charging station' (Sec. 355-4) to permit level-3 charging, plus full environmental assessment forms (parts 1-3). It referred the law to the Westchester County and town planning boards and circulated to interested/involved agencies, and scheduled a public hearing for January 28, 2026 — all on voice votes. Before the item was formally stated, a council member recused himself, explaining the item originated from a request by his employer, IBM, creating an appearance of conflict; counsel recommended the recusal.

cases.name: Payment Application No. 1 — Aquaworx (School Street Water Main Extension)
cases.summary: The board approved Payment Application No. 1 to Aquaworx for the School Street water main extension on a voice vote, after superintendent Sal reported the completed work had passed pressure testing and bacteriological sampling and was submitted to the Health Department for approval to energize the main, with service connections to follow (including Lombardy Park). Rende raised the idea of eventually offering Anthony Court residents (5-6 homes) the chance to extend the main and join the district, noting service tees were already provided for future extension, and stressed sequencing paving work to avoid reopening roads.

memberPositions.evidence: Enthusiastic about progress; asked about extending the main to Anthony Court homes and about coordinating with the resurfacing so roads are not reopened; visits job sites 'a couple times a week.'

cases.name: Water District 4 New Well/Control Building — EFI Payment App No. 2 and WSP USA Amendment No. 2
cases.summary: The board approved Payment Application No. 2 to Engineered Fluid Incorporated (EFI) for the Water District 4 new well building and control (work ~90% complete; contract pays 65% at this stage with a final payment on completion; building delivered in two parts including a ~70,000-lb structure). It also approved WSP USA Amendment No. 2 for engineering/construction services, but conditioned it: the town attorney flagged that WSP re-attached its standard terms and conditions rather than the more favorable originally negotiated terms, so Sal will obtain a revised amendment referencing the original agreement's terms, subject to the town attorney's approval, before signing. Members expressed interest in touring the site.

memberPositions.evidence: Reported a virtual tour of the finished building interior, described delivery logistics enthusiastically ('It's exciting'), and encouraged members to visit the site.

cases.name: Call for Public Hearing — Extension of Water District No. 9 (Quarry Heights, North White Plains)
cases.summary: The board adopted, by roll-call vote, the order calling a public hearing on the long-awaited extension of Water District No. 9 to serve the Quarry Heights section of North White Plains, where residents have faced dry wells and high PFAS levels; water will be supplied by Westchester Joint Water. Members discussed notifying the roughly 44 additional (plus 11 original = ~55) affected property owners, who will share the bond/debt service; the board directed the Town Clerk to mail notice (regular/certified, not registered) with an affidavit of mailing, per counsel, and to post the order on the project landing page. Counsel outlined next steps (design, Health Department submittals, bidding, grants, and state comptroller approval after the hearing). Roll call recorded ayes from Vataj, DiGiacinto, Hussain and Supervisor Rende.

memberPositions.evidence: Framed this as the 'long awaited' relief for Quarry Heights residents with failing wells and PFAS; pushed to over-notify residents and to keep the project moving.

Drawing on summer mail-delivery experience, recommended certified mail (not registered) so notices are trackable yet not 'ducked' by recipients; clarified the ~44 additional vs. 11 original homes sharing the bond.

cases.name: Recreation & Parks Equipment Purchases — Ventrac and Wacker Neuson Wheel Loader
cases.summary: The board approved Superintendent Matt Traynor's requests to purchase a new Ventrac machine and a Wacker Neuson wheel loader (via Sourcewell contract), both funded from the 2026 operational budget, on voice votes. Rende noted staff identified an unused piece of equipment to be sold at auction to offset the cost, choosing auction over a vendor trade-in for greater value.

memberPositions.evidence: Explained staff would auction an underused machine to offset costs, judging auction more valuable than a trade-in.

cases.name: Ramadan Crescent Moon & Star Display at Wampus Brook Park (and Annual Display Policy)
cases.summary: The board approved a resident request to install a crescent moon and star display at Wampus Brook Park to mark Ramadan (Feb 17-Mar 19, 2026), separate from the December holiday-season display of prior years. Because Ramadan shifts annually by the lunar calendar, the board established a protocol: the requester need only notify the Town Clerk in writing each year of the holiday's start and end dates by the last board meeting of the month prior, and directed Parks staff not to place this display during December. Discussion emphasized not burdening the resident with an in-person appearance each year.
cases.publicComment: Requester Asad Ghulani explained the rationale; a resident spoke up that it is unfair to make him return every year, prompting the notify-by-email protocol. Supportive tone.

memberPositions.evidence: Reviewed the 2006 resolution language, proposed a standing annual notification protocol and directed Parks not to place the display in December.

cases.name: Friends of North Castle Public Library — Armonk Outdoor Art Show Park Use and Permit Waivers
cases.applicant: Friends of North Castle Public Library
cases.summary: The board approved the Friends of the Library's request to use North Castle Community Park (including access road and parking) for the annual Armonk Outdoor Art Show on September 26-27, 2026, together with an alcohol permit and waivers of the permit fee and tent permit fee, on a voice vote.

cases.name: Filming Permit, Mount Pleasant Easement Letter, and Miscellaneous Agreements

memberPositions.evidence: On the county snow/ice removal IMA, confirmed with the Town Administrator that the town qualifies for the higher reimbursement rate.

cases.name: Personnel — Resignations/Retirements, Appointments, and Terminal Leave

cases.name: Town Board Liaison Updates — Library Website Redesign, Chamber of Commerce, Pool Project Delay
cases.summary: Board liaison updates: Hussain (library liaison) reported the board-approved library website redesign is fully underway with a specialized library-focused vendor and strong early feedback, currently in branding/graphics. Rende also delivered disappointing news that the Community Pool improvements will not proceed this winter: an 8-12 week (vs. expected ~2 week) wait for stainless-steel gutter material makes pre-season completion too risky, so the pool will open Memorial Day, close Labor Day, and the resurfacing work will bid now to start immediately after Labor Day; counsel and Sal cautioned about Health Department inspection delays and locking in prices.

memberPositions.evidence: As library board liaison, reported the website redesign is 'going really well' with a specialized vendor and good feedback on branding/graphics work.

Enthusiastic about the growing Chamber of Commerce but 'a little bit disappointed' the pool improvements must be deferred due to gutter lead times; wants the bid locked in to start day-one after Labor Day without driving up cost.

cases.name: In Memoriam — Heidi Slater, Wilfred Mincken, Tony Cecia
cases.summary: The board closed with condolences to the families of Heidi Slater (longtime resident active in the Armonk Methodist Church), Wilfred Mincken (decades-long Armonk resident), and Tony Cecia, whom DiGiacinto described as 'the glue' of the American Legion. Rende and DiGiacinto shared personal reflections on Cecia, and another member recalled his son's eulogy advice to 'laugh' and 'cry' daily and noted that political differences never prevented friendship. The board then adjourned.

Recalled Cecia as an important 'cog in the wheel' who told it like it is — 'you could never call Tony a phony.'

Reflected that he and Cecia had differing political views but could always talk, and was moved by the son's eulogy advice to laugh and cry each day (speaker not explicitly named; attribution uncertain).

themes.note: Annual reorganization: oaths, appointments, policy readoptions, recusals/abstentions, and public-hearing scheduling dominated the meeting.
Major water infrastructure focus: School Street main, WD4 well building, and the WD9 Quarry Heights extension (PFAS/dry-well relief).
Water buildings/mains progressing well; pool improvements deferred to post-Labor-Day due to material lead times.
Deputy Supervisor (Hussain), statutory officers/secretaries reappointed, resignations/retirements and new probationary appointments.
Numerous annual service/legal/fire agreements and equipment purchases; procurement policy under revision; WSP amendment conditioned on corrected terms.
Snow/ice removal, RICI records, Mount Pleasant easement, fire/ambulance and Bedford tax-review IMAs.
STR local law hearing set for Jan 28; referral deferred pending Airbnb feedback and a defensible, enforceable draft.
Ramadan display and standing policy, library art show, Chamber activity, and in-memoriam tributes.
Recreation equipment purchases and park-use permits offset against a disappointing pool-project deferral.
STR standalone law and EV level-3 charging code amendment, both headed to Jan 28 hearings; EV item referred to planning boards.
Master fee schedule, salary schedule, and bond/debt-service considerations for WD9 and the pool project.
PFAS remediation via WD9 water and EV level-3 charging expansion.
Fire inspector appointments, fire/ambulance agreements, police-clerk appointment, chief's terminal leave, and Custis tower police comms.

staffInput.summary: Gave community announcements (school-tax deadline Feb 2, commuter parking lottery Feb 1-18, new parking enforcement, winter snow-parking ordinance); recorded reorganization appointments; identified the STR documents to be received; advised the required notice for the WD9 hearing is publication of the order, with regular/certified mail as a courtesy and an affidavit of mailing to the Exhibit A list plus the 11 original-district properties.

Advised holding the STR referral until a more final draft; recommended the recusal on the IBM-originated EV charging item; flagged that WSP re-attached its standard (less favorable) terms and directed obtaining a corrected amendment referencing the original agreement's terms subject to his approval; explained WD9 legal-notice requirements and the post-hearing state-comptroller approval process.

Water/Sewer Superintendent: reported School Street main passed pressure and bacteriological testing and awaits Health Department approval to energize; detailed WD4 well building at ~90% with two-part delivery late this month; described WD9 process, tracer-wire/pipe practices, and the difficulty of locating buried plastic pool piping; agreed to check unbagged hydrants on Route 120.

Confirmed the town qualifies for the higher reimbursement rate under the county snow/ice-removal IMA; participated in equipment-purchase and pool-bidding discussions with Recreation and engineering staff.

cases.name: Probationary Appointment of Reagan Hufnagle as Police Chief

cases.name: Separation Agreement with Police Chief Peter Simonson

cases.name: Commendation of Personnel for Snowstorm Response
cases.summary: Supervisor Rende commended the highway department, police, parks and public-safety personnel for their handling of a difficult weekend storm, thanking residents for heeding safety warnings and staying off the roads, and crediting Town Administrator Kevin Hay's advance department-head planning meeting. No formal action taken. Councilwoman DiGiacinto added praise for first responders.

memberPositions.evidence: Commended all personnel and thanked residents for adhering to warnings, saying advance planning 'makes a big difference.'
Said 'all of our first responders are just wonderful when it comes to any adversity' and expressed pride in them during a scary storm.

cases.name: Revolutionary War 250th History Moment — Miller Hill Park
cases.address: Miller Hill, Route 22, North White Plains
cases.applicant: North Castle Revolutionary War 250th Committee / Historical Committee
cases.summary: Jed Schisler, a junior at Byram Hills High School, delivered a monthly 'history moment' presentation on Miller Hill Park in North White Plains and its Revolutionary War significance. cases.name: Local Law to Amend EV Charging Station Definition (Permit Level-Three Charging)
cases.summary: Public hearing on a local law to amend the definition of electric vehicle charging station in section 355-4 of the town code to permit level-three charging. Councilman Saleem Hussain recused himself (employed by IBM, which prompted the item). The core debate was whether level-three spaces should count toward the minimum off-street parking requirement; DiGiacinto and Rende argued they should count (like level one and two), while Berra preferred keeping the exclusion. The board agreed by consensus to remove the exclusion sentence, closed this hearing, directed the Town Planner to revise the language, and scheduled a new public hearing for February 11, 2026.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public spoke on the hearing.

memberPositions.evidence: Fully supported the law but wanted the exclusion deleted, calling it 'punitive' that level-three spaces would not count toward off-street parking.
Favored the original proposal, worried broader level-three access 'could lead to extra crowdedness,' liked keeping the parking provision as-is, but was 'willing to go along with the board majority.'
Said level three should count as off-street parking 'just as we do with level one and two,' opposed discriminating against EV charging and saw no evidence of clogging.

cases.name: Local Law to Regulate Short-Term Rentals of Homes
cases.applicant: Town (Town Planner Adam Kaufman; special counsel Bob Spolzino)
cases.summary: Extended public hearing on a proposed local law regulating short-term rentals and referral to the town and county planning boards. The board worked through disputed policy provisions: it kept the waiting-period requirement in provision C (two years after initial CO for new construction, one year after acquiring title otherwise), kept the quiet-hours provision K, and by majority voted to remove provision E (requiring the owner to stay overnight during a rental) as overly restrictive, with DiGiacinto dissenting. Special counsel Spolzino was directed to draft an expedited revocation procedure (likely a building-inspector hearing officer with quick timeframes) to give the law 'teeth' while surviving judicial scrutiny. The board closed the hearing rather than adopt the draft as written, directing a redraft and a new public hearing to be set (targeting February 25, 2026).
cases.publicComment: Resident Joyce Evgries (41 Washington Avenue, North White Plains) described a disruptive Airbnb with up to 40 people on a small lot causing noise and garbage, and urged strict laws; the board noted the draft's occupancy limits would bar such use.

memberPositions.evidence: Strongly wanted to KEEP the owner-must-stay-overnight requirement to deter late-night parties; dissented from the majority vote to remove provision E ('I disagree').

Strongly opposed the overnight-stay requirement, arguing it would punish responsible residents who rent their homes for extra income; supported at least a one-year CO requirement and added outdoor-gathering/quiet-hours clarifications.

Favored removing the overnight requirement (unworkable in a single residence), was empathetic to affordability reasons, and pushed for a swift board-controlled revocation process rather than lengthy court proceedings.

Wanted the primary-residence requirement to bar speculators and swift enforcement, but agreed the overnight-stay requirement was too restrictive and should be pulled; stressed protecting residents without over-legislating.
Voted with the majority to remove provision E (the overnight-stay requirement).

cases.name: Approval of Town Board Minutes (January 14, 2026)
cases.summary: The board approved the town board minutes from January 14, 2026. Motion made and seconded, all in favor. Routine consent item.

cases.name: Open Space Committee Recommendation — John Fava Nature Preserve
cases.applicant: Open Space Committee / Westchester Land Trust
cases.summary: The board received the Open Space Committee's recommendation to create the John Fava Nature Preserve (previously the Children's Land Preserve) on Byram Lake Road, Armonk. Councilman Berra moved to receive and praised Fava's decades of conservation work; Rende and DiGiacinto supported naming the preserve for Fava. Councilman Hussain objected to the naming approach, arguing preserves should be named for the principles they represent with an honoree recognized on a plaque instead, and asked to discuss alternatives with Open Space chair Kerry Kasak. The board received the recommendation and deferred a formal resolution pending that conversation.

memberPositions.evidence: Made the motion to receive, saying he'd 'love to' because 'John was such a great asset to this town.'
Argued naming it for Fava honors the man and passes his open-space legacy to future generations; suggested a plaque with his history.
Said he would not favor naming the preserve after a person; preferred a name reflecting principles with Fava recognized on a plaque, and would not support the person-named version when it returns.
Supported the honor and cited other person-named preserves; comfortable moving it forward after Hussain speaks with Kasak.

cases.name: Revised Purchase Order / Procurement Policy
cases.summary: Consideration of the revised town purchase order and procurement policy was tabled to allow Town Attorney Roland more time to review and to gather board questions. Councilman Berra requested a work session to hash out the policy, which Rende agreed to try to schedule for the February 11 meeting. Motion to table made and seconded, all in favor.

memberPositions.evidence: Applauded the effort, said he'd long wanted improved procurement practices, and requested a work session to work through it.
Agreed to table for attorney review and to try to add a work session to the next agenda.

cases.name: Payment Application No. 5 — Papatito Construction (Water District No. 4 New Well)
cases.summary: The board approved payment application number five to Papatito Construction for site work on the Water District No. 4 new well project. Town Administrator Kevin Hay reported strong progress, with the tank backfilled and the building expected early February. Motion made and all in favor.

cases.name: Tony Castell Inc. — Kent Place Parking Lot (Former Verizon Property) Final Payment
cases.summary: The board accepted the contractor's affidavit of release of liens and a one-year guarantee bond and approved final payment requisition number five to Tony Castell Inc. for the Kent Place parking lot improvements. Councilwoman DiGiacinto recused herself because her family owns commercial property on the west side of Main Street. Motion made and all in favor.

cases.name: Shaw Sports Turf Change Order No. 3 — Community Park Artificial Turf Field
cases.summary: The board considered a memo from KSCJ Consulting and Change Order No. 3 (about $75,000) for additional electrical power and data improvements on the community park artificial turf field project, authorizing the Supervisor to sign. DiGiacinto objected to the letter's 'as requested by the town' wording and pressed for detailed justification, learning much of the cost stemmed from rerouting buried electrical lines and adding access boxes discovered during excavation. Vataj and Berra questioned pricing reasonableness and asked to be notified of change orders in advance; staff confirmed the same approved unit rates applied. The board approved the change order.

memberPositions.evidence: Called the ~$75k change order and 'as requested by the town' language misleading, wanted more detailed explanation, but ultimately made the motion to approve.
As someone with an electrical background, asked about scope and wanted advance email notice of change orders, while acknowledging the project must move forward.
Asked what was done to verify the additional footage and unit-cost pricing was reasonable and appropriate.
Explained the unforeseen subterranean electrical rerouting and access-box work justified the change order and that stopping the project would risk delays and higher costs.

cases.name: Provisional Appointment of Kenny Keneally — Appraisal Technician
cases.summary: The board approved the provisional appointment of Kenny Keneally as appraisal technician in the Assessor's Department, effective January 29, 2026. DiGiacinto congratulated him, noting he had been doing two jobs. Motion made and all in favor.

memberPositions.evidence: Seconded 'with congratulations,' saying he'd been doing two jobs and a great job.

cases.name: Travel Authorization — Director of Finance Abbas (2026 NYS GFOA Conference)
cases.summary: The board approved Director of Finance Abbas attending the 2026 New York State GFOA Conference, April 15-17, 2026. DiGiacinto complimented Abbas for checking every box of the procurement/travel submission requirements. Motion made and all in favor.

memberPositions.evidence: Praised Abbas's conference submission as 'absolutely perfect,' checking every required box.

cases.name: Reappointment of Tom Crispy to the Planning Board
cases.summary: The board reappointed Tom Crispy to the Planning Board for a five-year term expiring January 30, 2031, with congratulations. Motion made and seconded, all in favor.

cases.name: Committee Resignations — Christine Eggleton (Landmark Preservation) and Alyssa (Open Space)
cases.summary: The board accepted, with regret, the resignation of Christine Eggleton from the Landmark Preservation Committee and the resignation of a member (Alyssa) from the Open Space Committee. Both motions made, seconded, and passed. Members expressed regret at losing them.

cases.name: Town Liaison Updates (Invasive Vines Recognition, Rare Disease Day Request)
cases.summary: In liaison updates, Councilman Berra reported the North Castle invasive-vines program was selected for a Westchester Land Trust gala honor in June (crediting Doug Mancinelli and volunteers) and asked the board to let Rhys Skeller present on Rare Disease Day at the next meeting; Rende agreed to route the request through staff. Other updates covered the ARB and 88-unit Eagle Ridge/IBM housing project moving forward, and the Beautification Committee's spring plans tied to the Revolutionary War 250th. Discussion only.

memberPositions.evidence: Announced the invasive-vines program's gala honor and advocated for a Rare Disease Day presentation at the next meeting.

cases.name: Closing in Memory of Maria Palacio
cases.summary: The board closed the meeting in memory of Maria Palacio, a nearly 60-year Armonk resident who worked for the North Castle Recreation Department serving seniors, extending condolences to her family. Councilwoman DiGiacinto delivered the memoriam and also thanked sanitation workers for double garbage pickup amid the snow. Motion to close made and all in favor.

memberPositions.evidence: Delivered the closing memoriam for Maria Palacio and thanked sanitation workers for their storm-week service.

New Police Chief sworn in, outgoing chief separation, and heavy praise for storm response.
Turf field change order, water well payment, and Kent Place lot final payment.
EV level-three charging local law hearing focused on off-street parking treatment.
Multiple appointments, a reappointment, and two committee resignations.
Procurement policy tabled for review/work session; scrutiny of the turf change order.
John Fava Nature Preserve naming recommendation and turf field improvements.
History moment, invasive-vines honor, Rare Disease Day request, and memoriam.
Snowstorm cleanup, mailbox/senior-driveway assistance, and downtown snow removal.

Town Planner; presented both local laws, explained the EV level-three parking provision and the disputed STR policy items (waiting periods, overnight-stay, quiet hours, registration/permit), and was directed to revise both drafts.

Special counsel; advised on a legally defensible expedited STR revocation procedure (hearing officer / building inspector with quick timeframes, appeal via Article 78) and cautioned that STR constitutional issues are unsettled.

Recreation & Parks Superintendent; gathered league feedback that drove the turf field electrical/data change order and participated in staff planning meetings.

meetings.attributionNote: All five 2026 board members present and identifiable: Supervisor Joseph Rende (presiding voice), Barbara DiGiacinto, Saleem Hussain, Jose Berra (joined via Zoom, ASR-mangled at the open as 'Jose Vera'), and Sonny Vataj. Recusals were explicit (Hussain on EV charging for IBM; DiGiacinto on Kent Place lot). Matt Milim was NOT present or attributed (off the board in 2026). 'Jose' consistently disambiguated: presiding/motion-calling voice = Rende, remote member being polled = Berra. Some short procedural exchanges (motions/seconds) could not be pinned to a specific member and were left unattributed rather than guessed.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Town Board opened with a lengthy work session reviewing a comprehensive new town procurement policy line-by-line, then held two public hearings: one on the Quarry Heights extension of Water District No. 9 (two preliminary resolutions adopted 5-0 by roll call) and one on a local law permitting Level 3 EV charging (adopted, with Councilman Hussain recused as an IBM employee). The board also adopted a resolution creating the John Fava Nature Preserve after an extended philosophical discussion about how the town names public spaces, referred a short-term-rental local law to the planning boards with a Feb. 25 public hearing, and approved a series of contracts, change orders, appointments, and the formation of a Town Hall Advisory Committee.
meetings.durationNote: Quorum present; all five members participated. Councilman Saleem Hussain was out of the country and participated virtually from a posted public location. Hussain recused himself from the Level 3 EV charging local law due to his employment with IBM (the original requester). Meeting opened at 5:30 with executive session, reconvened to work session ~6:45.

cases.name: Revised Town Procurement Policy
cases.summary: In a work session the board reviewed a completely rewritten town procurement policy drafted by Comptroller Abbas using auditor/state-comptroller guidance and peer Westchester municipal policies. The board went page-by-page through Councilman Jose Berra's extensive written comments, sorting them into town-attorney/administrator edits (handled by Kevin), legal questions (for Town Attorney Roland), substantive changes, and error corrections. Numerous wording refinements were agreed (e.g., prices confidential 'prior to award,' grant purchases planned when the grant 'is approved,' softening bid-specification language, adding 'or other entity' to non-collusion language, credit-card purchase limits set at $25,000 with Sam's/Home Depot capped at $2,000 each). No vote was taken; Abbas will produce a redraft in a distinct color for review by Berra, Kevin, and Roland, targeting placement on the agenda for a formal vote at an upcoming meeting.

memberPositions.evidence: Authored the bulk of the detailed comments strengthening the policy and drove the page-by-page review; praised Abbas's work while pushing numerous refinements.
Commended Abbas for tackling the overdue rewrite ('grabbed the bull by the horns'); guided the review and stressed getting it onto the agenda to formally vote.
Engaged on wording, e.g., questioned whether to use 'comptroller' vs. 'director of finance' on page five.
Followed along with the draft (e.g., tracking the page-11 discussion) but offered limited substantive input.

cases.name: Rare Disease Day Recognition Request
cases.applicant: Susan Cardillo (Star Spangled Carousel) and Reese Geller
cases.summary: During public comment, resident Susan Cardillo and Byram Hills junior Reese Geller presented on Rare Disease Day (Feb. 28), describing FOXP1 syndrome and asking the town to allow awareness banners, to publicize a fundraiser via town email/newsletter, and to offer any additional guidance. Supervisor Rende responded supportively, offering to feature it in the daily supervisor's update, share it on town social media and community pages, and connect the effort with the Chamber of Commerce, inviting Cardillo to come to the office to coordinate. No formal action was required.
cases.publicComment: Susan Cardillo and student Reese Geller spoke warmly and personally in support; the board was receptive and encouraging.

memberPositions.evidence: Offered to promote the effort through the supervisor's update, community pages, and the Chamber of Commerce, and invited the presenters to coordinate at the office.

cases.name: Water District No. 9 — Quarry Heights Extension
cases.address: Quarry Heights area (Johnson Place, Memorial Lane, Starkey Road, Old Orchard Street, William Street, McClure Street)
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (AI Engineers map/plan/report)
cases.summary: The board held a public hearing on extending Water District No. 9 to the Quarry Heights area under Article 12A of Town Law, addressing chronic well-water/PFAS problems among roughly 48 homes. Town Attorney Roland explained that two preliminary resolutions would let the town apply to the State Comptroller and better position the project for grant funding, with a worst-case per-home cost around $46,700 over the life of the bond. Residents spoke strongly in favor (a signed petition and letter were submitted into the record), and the board adopted a 21-day open comment period before both preliminary resolutions passed 5-0 by roll call (Berra, Vataj, DiGiacinto, Hussain, Rende all aye). Board members voiced unanimous, emphatic support and commitment to pursue grants.
cases.publicComment: Numerous Quarry Heights residents attended and spoke strongly in favor; Lisa Alvarez read a signed support letter and submitted a petition, and residents detailed high well-maintenance/PFAS costs. Tone was appreciative and supportive.

memberPositions.evidence: Recounted his own neighborhood's cooperative sewer project, called it a worthwhile investment in health and home value, and praised Sal's grant work.
Cited a resident's text about having no water and said the board is '100% committed to do whatever we can do to make your lives whole.'
From his virtual connection said he is '100% supportive' and would work on everything possible to progress the project; noted residents' voices matter.
Told residents 'your voice really matters' and that the petition would help push their perspective forward; voted aye.
Pledged to leave no stone unturned and to use state/federal connections to secure grant money to ease the financial burden.

cases.name: Local Law Amending EV Charging Station Definition (Level 3 Charging)
cases.summary: The board held a public hearing on a local law amending the definition of 'electric vehicle charging station' in Town Code section 355-4 to permit Level 3 (fast) charging and to exclude Level 3 stations from off-street parking calculations. The request originated with IBM, so Councilman Hussain recused himself. No members of the public spoke and the town planner had nothing to add. The board adopted the negative declaration and then the local law by voice vote; Supervisor Rende said he was 'very satisfied' with the law.
cases.publicComment: No public comment offered.

memberPositions.evidence: 'Very satisfied with the proposed local law... only right that we allow the level three charging stations.'
Said he had nothing more to add and that the board can move forward.
Recused himself from the matter due to his employment with IBM, the original requester; did not participate or vote.

cases.name: Approval of Town Board Minutes — January 28, 2026
cases.summary: Under old business, the board approved the minutes of the January 28, 2026 town board meeting by voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Resolution Creating the John Fava Nature Preserve
cases.summary: The board considered naming a 63-acre town-owned parcel on Byram Lake Road the 'John Fava Nature Preserve' to honor Fava's decades of environmental stewardship (35 years with Westchester County Parks and 40 years on the North Castle Conservation Board). Open Space Committee chair Carrie Kasak spoke in favor, and resident Susan Miller spoke strongly for it while sharply criticizing Councilman Hussain's prior hesitation. Hussain delivered an extended screen-shared explanation of his philosophical view that the town should name land for its natural features and recognize people durably (plaques, archives, expandable recognition) with clearer precedent-setting standards, but he ultimately voted in favor. The resolution passed by voice vote; DiGiacinto and Berra strongly supported honoring Fava directly while respecting differing views.
cases.publicComment: Open Space Committee chair Carrie Kasak spoke eloquently in favor; longtime resident Susan Miller strongly supported the naming and publicly rebuked Councilman Hussain's earlier reservations. Tone was passionate and largely celebratory.

memberPositions.evidence: Voted yes and stated '100% support' for the proposal, but argued at length for a different long-term approach to naming (features over people, durable/expandable recognition, precedent standards); pushed back on being called 'analytical and sterile.'
Called Fava a 'missionary' for the environment, said a groundswell not criteria should drive such honors, disagreed with Hussain's approach, and voted yes.
Praised Fava's influence, valued the diversity of perspectives, and enthusiastically supported the naming.
Briefly stated he is 'in favor and that's all.'
Reflected that the delay allowed both Kasak's tribute and Hussain's viewpoint to be aired ('Baskin Robbins makes 31 flavors'), and supported honoring Fava.

cases.name: Short-Term Rental Local Law — Referral and Public Hearing Scheduling
cases.summary: The board received a proposed local law to create regulations governing the short-term rental of homes, referred it to the town and county planning boards, and scheduled a public hearing for February 25, 2026. A new procedure (worked out with the Town Clerk and special counsel Bob Spolzino) will allow certain changes during a public hearing without requiring a second hearing, via added posting language. Councilman Berra supported enacting it to end resident hardships while cautioning it may be too restrictive and could be revisited; Rende noted he would still favor republishing for substantial changes, especially where litigation risk exists.

memberPositions.evidence: Supported enacting it to end the 'horrible treatment circumstances' residents suffered, while noting it may be too restrictive and could be tinkered with later.
Backed the referral but cautioned he would still prefer republishing for substantial changes, particularly where the town could face litigation.

cases.name: Payment Requisition No. 1 — Shaw Integrated & Turf Solutions (Artificial Turf Field)
cases.applicant: Shaw Integrated and Turf Solutions Incorporated
cases.summary: The board approved payment requisition No. 1 from Shaw Integrated and Turf Solutions Incorporated for the artificial turf field improvements. There was noticeable initial hesitation among members to make the motion, which Supervisor Rende remarked on, though it ultimately passed by voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Noted aloud there was 'not even a willingness to make the motion at first,' signaling some board reticence, but moved it to approval.

cases.name: Change Order No. 4 — Shaw Integrated Turf Solutions (Irrigation at Clove Road Fields)
cases.address: Clove Road Little League and Babe Ruth League baseball fields
cases.applicant: Shaw Integrated Turf Solutions Incorporated (per KSCJ Consulting memo)
cases.summary: The board received a memo from KSCJ Consulting and approved Shaw Integrated Turf Solutions' Change Order No. 4 for installing an irrigation system at the Clove Road Little League and Babe Ruth League baseball fields, part of the Community Post park artificial turf project, and authorized the supervisor to sign the proposal. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Crescent and Star Lighting Ceremony for Ramadan
cases.summary: The board approved a request from Assad Giuliani for a crescent and star lighting ceremony in observation of Ramadan at Wampus Park on February 17. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: NYS Association of Towns Membership and Voting Delegate Designation
cases.summary: The board approved 2026 membership in the New York State Association of Towns and designated Supervisor Joseph A. Rende as the town's voting delegate at the February annual meeting. A member asked how the delegate's votes could be viewed; Rende agreed to share how he votes and noted the legislative agenda and outcomes are available via the association. Approved by voice vote after brief discussion.

memberPositions.evidence: Accepted the voting-delegate role and agreed to share his votes with the board, noting members can attend the annual meeting.

cases.name: Change Order No. 4 — Aqua Works (Lombardi Park / School Street Water Main Extension)
cases.applicant: Aqua Works Incorporated (per KSCJ Consulting memo)
cases.summary: The board received a KSCJ Consulting memo and approved Aqua Works Incorporated's Change Order No. 4 for the Lombardi Park / School Street water main extension, covering additional asbestos removal related to the Lombardi Park building demolition. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Formation of the Town Hall Advisory Committee
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (Alan Blum, committee lead)
cases.summary: The board approved forming a Town Hall Advisory Committee and adopted its mission statement and committee structure to plan for the town's inadequate town hall, highway, and water department facilities. Volunteer lead Alan Blum described an independent, non-political, expertise-driven committee that will gather needs-based data and keep the community informed, with a short window for additional volunteers. Discussion clarified that Town Planner Adam Kaufman would serve as a resource rather than a formal liaison, preserving the committee's independence; Hussain asked about accepting volunteers and Berra and Rende stressed letting the group work independently. Approved by voice vote.
cases.publicComment: Committee lead Alan Blum spoke at length, enthusiastic and urging residents to volunteer rather than merely complain; tone was energetic and constructive.

memberPositions.evidence: Praised the committee for bringing forward unbiased data and asked Blum to clarify the process/timeline for accepting additional volunteers.
Valued the committee's independence and trust-building, urged North White Plains representation, and quoted 'surround yourself with good people and have the self-control to let them work.'
Questioned whether Adam Kaufman should be a formal team member versus a resource/liaison in keeping with the committee's independence.
Supported posting committee info on the town hall landing page and emphasized letting the group deliberate independently and report back.

cases.name: AI Engineers Proposal — Water District No. 9 Quarry Heights Water Main Extension Distribution System
cases.summary: Under agreements, the board approved receipt of a proposal from AI Engineers for the Water District No. 9 Quarry Heights water main extension distribution system (design work supplementing the map/plan/report). Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Resignation of Angela Colombo from the Board of Assessment Review
cases.summary: The board accepted, with thanks and appreciation, the letter of resignation from Angela Colombo from the Board of Assessment Review, effective January 6, 2026. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Appointment of Denise Lombardi to the Board of Assessment Review
cases.summary: The board appointed Denise Lombardi to the Board of Assessment Review for a term ending September 30, 2026. DiGiacinto praised her as a well-qualified, licensed appraiser familiar with the assessor's office. Approved by voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Expressed gratitude that Lombardi agreed to serve, calling her a very qualified licensed appraiser familiar with the assessor's office.

themes.note: Dominant theme: Quarry Heights Water District 9 extension public hearing and 5-0 preliminary resolutions, plus AI Engineers and Aqua Works agreements.
Extensive procurement-policy rewrite work session plus multiple contract/change-order approvals.
John Fava Nature Preserve naming and Clove Road/Community Post turf and irrigation work.
Naming-precedent debate, town hall advisory committee independence, and public-hearing posting procedures.
Town hall/highway/water facilities planning committee and water main and turf projects.
Level 3 EV charging local law and short-term rental local law referral.
Rare Disease Day request and the Ramadan crescent-and-star lighting ceremony.
Board of Assessment Review resignation and appointment; advisory committee membership.
Short-term rental regulation referred to planning boards with a Feb. 25 public hearing.
