Reviewed and edited the procurement policy and will incorporate the agreed redraft changes; gave the administrator update on the Water District 4 control building delivery, the mandated .com-to-.gov website/email transition, and the ClearGov financial-transparency rollout.

Provided legal opinions across the procurement policy (confidentiality prior to award, bid rejection rights, prevailing-wage language); explained the Water District 9 process and State Comptroller application; advised on the EV local law negative declaration and the short-term-rental hearing posting procedure and volunteer insurance coverage.
Gave community announcements (Fisher Lane commuter parking lottery, March 1 blood drive, snow parking ordinance) and read the documents comprising the record for both public hearings.
Town Planner; had no changes to add on the EV charging local law and was designated a resource (not a formal member/liaison) to the Town Hall Advisory Committee.
Water/Sewer superintendent; credited with the cost analysis (worst-case ~$46,700 per home) supporting the Water District 9 application and for pursuing grant funding.

meetings.attributionNote: Roll-call votes on the two Water District 9 resolutions clearly named each member (ASR: 'Councilman Bera'=Jose Berra, 'Councilman Vitage/Bataj'=Sonny Vataj, 'Councilman Digacento'=Barbara DiGiacinto, 'Councilman Hussein'=Saleem Hussain, 'Supervisor Endy'=Joseph Rende), both passing 5-0. Saleem Hussain participated virtually (out of the country) and recused from the EV charging local law due to his IBM employment. Most other items passed by voice vote, so individual attributions there rely on named discussion. Staff (Abbas, Kevin, Roland, Allison, Adam Kaufman, Sal) were kept out of member positions. Matt Milim did not appear and was correctly not attributed as a 2026 board member.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Town Board opened with a work session presentation from the Trust for Public Land on a conservation finance feasibility study, with the board coalescing around polling a real estate transfer tax (community preservation fund) rather than a property-tax increase or bonding. In the regular meeting the board continued the public hearing on a proposed short-term rental local law (adding a primary-residence affirmation and rejecting a one-acre minimum, adjourned to March 11 pending a Planning Board referral), adopted a procurement policy, scheduled a public hearing for a Coptic church special-use permit, and handled several agreements, payments, and personnel matters. Notable votes included a 4-1 adoption of department-head salary increases (DiGiacinto opposed on methodology) and the tabling of a storage-container purchase for IBM community park. Saleem Hussain chaired as deputy supervisor with Supervisor Rende participating remotely from California.
meetings.durationNote: All five 2026 board members present; Supervisor Rende participated via video conference from Newport Beach, California, and Saleem Hussain chaired as deputy supervisor. Quorum present.

cases.name: Trust for Public Land — Conservation Finance Feasibility Study (work session)
cases.applicant: Trust for Public Land (Will Aberger & Andrew Dumoulin); North Castle Open Space Committee (Carrie Kasak)
cases.summary: TPL presented a draft feasibility study on funding options to establish a dedicated conservation/land-preservation fund: a real estate transfer tax under the Hudson Valley Community Preservation Act, a property-tax-funded special reserve, or general obligation bonds. No action was required as it was a work session. The board's clear consensus was to advance the real estate transfer tax option for voter polling, with several members opposing any property-tax increase. Next steps are a voter poll (which the board will review) aiming toward a possible November 2026 ballot referendum.
cases.publicComment: Carrie Kasak (Open Space Committee chair) introduced and strongly supported the effort; no residents spoke against.

memberPositions.evidence: "I absolutely am in favor of doing the transfer tax. To me that seems like the best option across the three."
Favored polling the real estate transfer tax but stated "I personally am not in favor of raising taxes" (property tax).

Wanted to hear from residents, cited the Erico property and Quarry Heights water problems as reasons to have funds; opposed a property tax, open to transfer tax, less keen on bonds; asked whether a referendum is required.
Asked to review the survey before it goes out, stressed educating residents and comparing bonding vs. the preservation-fund matrix, and cautioned against rushing a 20-year commitment.
Called it "a very interesting concept," said the transfer tax is "an interesting way to go," and asked whether the $865k threshold is statutory and whether the fund would be interest-bearing.

cases.name: Proposed Local Law — Short-Term Rental Regulations (Chapter 355)
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (Town Planner Adam Kaufman)
cases.summary: The board continued its public hearing on a proposed local law regulating short-term rentals of homes, incorporating prior board and town-attorney comments. No residents spoke. The board agreed to add a sworn affirmation (class E felony if false) that the dwelling is the owner's primary residence at both permit-application points, but rejected DiGiacinto's proposals to limit short-term rentals to lots of one acre or greater and to require owner presence. Because the law amends the zoning chapter, the board could not adopt it without the pending Planning Board referral, so the hearing was adjourned to the March 11 meeting.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public spoke; town clerk confirmed no online attendees waiting.

memberPositions.evidence: Supported the law but pushed for a primary-residence affidavit/affirmation, a one-acre-minimum lot restriction, and an owner-presence requirement, and repeatedly raised enforcement concerns given building-department hours.
"I think the law is robust enough. I'd be really hesitant to go ahead and layer on this additional restriction"; asked about ability to enact subject to the planning board referral.

Argued existing house rules and occupancy/vehicle limits suffice, opposed adding restrictions, and stressed police will respond to every complaint; opposed a permanent bar on re-applying after a violation.
As chair, favored keeping the current draft, wanting a smooth process for the ~95% compliant owners while targeting bad actors; opposed the one-acre restriction as penalizing legitimate renters.
Backed a primary-residence affirmation at permit filing and framed the law as targeting "the bad actors" misusing short-term rentals, not responsible renters.

cases.name: Approval of Town Board Minutes — February 11, 2026
cases.summary: The board approved the minutes of its February 11, 2026 meeting by voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Town Purchase Order and Procurement Policy
cases.applicant: Town Administrator Kevin (with Comptroller Abbas and Town Attorney Roland)
cases.summary: The board considered adoption of a revised purchase-order and procurement policy that staff had updated per prior work-session direction. Berra raised a late wording tweak on grant-related purchases that he said Roland found meritorious, but DiGiacinto challenged why that input was not circulated to the full board beforehand; Berra then withdrew the suggestion as non-substantive. The policy was adopted by voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Proposed a wording change to grant-purchase timing ("planned early enough to be able to apply or qualify for the grant") vetted with Roland, then withdrew it after questions about process.
Questioned why Roland's suggested changes were not communicated to all board members between the Friday distribution and the vote.
Thanked staff (Kevin, Abbas, Roland) for the well-vetted work and offered to make or second the motion.

cases.name: Special Use Permit — Virgin Mary & St. Damiana Coptic Orthodox Church (ADA access) + Schedule Public Hearing
cases.applicant: Virgin Mary and St. Damiana Coptic Orthodox Church
cases.summary: The board acted on the church's request for a special use permit to support an ADA-compliant accessible-access sidewalk improvement for elderly parishioners, along with referral to the town and county planning boards. Adam Kaufman explained the church has operated for decades without an existing special use permit, which the Planning Board needs on record to approve the site plan. The board voted to receive the application and to schedule a public hearing for March 25, 2026 (moved from an initial March 11 suggestion to allow proper notice).

cases.name: Payment Application No. 6 — Papito Construction (Water District No. 4 well project)
cases.summary: The board approved payment application number six from Papito Construction for site work performed on the Water District No. 4 new well project. Approved by voice vote with no substantive discussion (Vataj moved, DiGiacinto seconded).

cases.name: Purchase of Two Storage Container Units for IBM Community Park (Connex West)
cases.address: IBM Community Park (near the turf fields)
cases.applicant: Recreation & Parks (Superintendent Matt Traynor); vendor Connex West
cases.summary: The board considered a request to purchase two new green storage container units for equipment near the IBM Park turf fields, to be paid from fund balance, replacing rotted existing containers. Vataj strongly objected that metal containers cheapen a multimillion-dollar turf investment (his "Ferrari with used tires" analogy) and pushed for a prefab garage-style structure, while DiGiacinto defended the containers as utilitarian, secure, and cost-conscious but asked for full all-in cost comparisons of any alternative. With no motion made, the item was tabled to the next meeting for staff to bring back options.

memberPositions.evidence: "You've built a Ferrari in that field and you're asking to go buy used tires." Wanted a prefab garage-style structure instead and objected to staff pre-arranging purchases before board approval.
Called the containers "very utilitarian" and maintenance-free and was ready to approve, but insisted any alternative include full "all-in" costs, recalling the prefab-bathroom cost overruns.
As chair noted the containers are a security advantage over a wood shed, but agreed to hold the item so Matt Traynor could present options.
"I think that Sonny's raising some good points. I don't think it hurts to wait a couple of weeks."
Suggested tabling the item to gather more options rather than deciding tonight.

cases.name: Declaration of Restrictive Covenants — 12 AFFH Units, Airport Campus Development
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle / Westchester County
cases.summary: The board approved receipt of a declaration of restrictive covenants regarding the 12 Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing (AFFH) units at the Airport Campus development and authorized the supervisor to sign the agreement and county reporting forms. Staff explained this is now a standard county requirement that the local municipality co-sign. Adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: Agreement with Northeast Westchester Special Recreation for 2026
cases.summary: The board authorized the supervisor to sign the 2026 agreement with Northeast Westchester Special Recreation. Adopted by voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Salary Increases for Department Head / Non-Union Employees (effective Jan 1, 2026)
cases.summary: The board considered salary increases for department-head and non-union employees retroactive to January 1, 2026. DiGiacinto voted no and requested a roll call, objecting not to the raises themselves but to the methodology used to determine them, which she said differs from comparable municipalities; discussion was limited because details were set in executive session. The resolution was adopted 4-1 (Berra aye, Vataj aye, DiGiacinto no, Hussain aye, Rende yes).

memberPositions.evidence: Voted no on roll call, objecting to the methodology for setting non-union department-head raises while praising the employees and supporting that they receive increases.
Voted aye and wanted to proceed: "I don't see a reason to [delay] it more. People like to know the raises they're getting."
Voted aye on roll call ("Councilman Vera — aye").
Voted aye on roll call; clarified for the public that all non-union employees receive a raise.
Voted yes; offered to table for further executive-session discussion of the formula if members wished, noting raises are retroactive to Jan 1 regardless.

cases.name: North Castle Public Library Hourly Staff Salary Increases (effective Jan 1, 2026)
cases.summary: The board approved salary increases for the North Castle Public Library's hourly staff, effective January 1, 2026, consistent with the library director's memo and the budget. Adopted by voice vote after brief confirmation that the figures were budgeted.

memberPositions.evidence: "These are very valuable employees, the hourly staff. They really fill a lot of important positions."

cases.name: Appointments to the Town Hall Advisory Committee
cases.summary: The board appointed Alan Blum, Diana Barrera, George Dropo, Howard Fisher, Susan Geffen, and Rich Rosen to the town hall advisory committee, an initial list with more names to follow. After discussion led by Berra, the board changed Town Planner Adam Kaufman from a committee member to a non-member advisor/resource, to preserve the committee's perceived independence and public trust. Adopted as modified by voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Praised Adam Kaufman but argued he should be an advisor/resource, not a committee member, so the committee is "independent and even more so perceived by the public as being independent."
Preferred Kaufman as a member (he would save the committee time on legal/procedural matters) but respected making him an advisor instead.
As chair, agreed Kaufman's value could be captured fully as an advisor, supporting community trust in the committee's decisions.
Stated for the record he is comfortable the committee will work "without the overbearance of anyone or any outside sources."

cases.name: Receipt of Resignation — Brendan Malloy, Parks & Recreation Advisory Board
cases.summary: The board received the letter of resignation from Brendan Malloy from the Parks and Recreation advisory board, effective February 14, 2026, and thanked him for his service. Accepted by voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Seconded "with great appreciation and regret," calling Malloy "a tremendous individual" who volunteers with him but understanding his reasons.
Said Malloy did a great job and will be sorely missed, expecting him to serve on other committees.

cases.name: Consensus Agenda
cases.summary: The board approved the consensus agenda in a single motion by voice vote with no discussion.

themes.note: TPL conservation-finance study dominated the work session; board leaned toward a transfer-tax preservation fund.
Continued STR local-law hearing; primary-residence affirmation added, one-acre limit rejected, adjourned to March 11.
Dept-head raises adopted 4-1 (DiGiacinto opposed on methodology); library raises, committee appointments, and a resignation handled.
Cost consciousness recurred — transfer tax vs. property tax, container spending, raise methodology, snow-budget impact.
IBM Park storage-container purchase tabled amid a dispute over containers vs. a prefab structure.
Procurement policy adopted; Papito water-district payment and Special Recreation agreement approved.
Repeated thanks to highway/police/parks/fire for snow response; police-enforcement role debated for STR law.
Independence of the town hall advisory committee and process for circulating staff/attorney input were discussed.
AFFH covenant co-signature for county and Special Recreation agreement.

staffInput.summary: Town Planner: gave overview of the STR local law (incorporating board and attorney comments, noting the missing Planning Board recommendation due to a cancelled snow-day meeting), explained the Coptic church special-use-permit process, and provided context on the park storage containers and the advisory committee.

Special counsel: advised the STR law amends the zoning chapter so the Planning Board referral is needed before adoption, that New York now allows a sworn affirmation (no notary) with the same legal effect as an affidavit, and that the advisory committee has no legal restrictions on composition.

Presented the updated procurement policy, explained the storage-container proposal and prior prefab-building cost, confirmed budgeted library raises and department-head raise methodology, and issued a public warning about an email/wire scam targeting Planning/Zoning applicants.

Read the public hearing notice, confirmed no online attendees waiting to speak, delivered community announcements (blood drive, town-wide cleanup day with shredder/e-waste, volunteer opportunities), and conducted the roll-call vote.

meetings.attributionNote: All five 2026 board members were reliably identified: Saleem Hussain chaired as deputy supervisor (ASR mangled his self-introduction as 'Celine Hussein' and closing thanks as 'Selim'), and Supervisor Joseph Rende participated remotely (ASR 'Rendy'/'Endy'/'Rundy'). The Personnel A roll call explicitly named each member — 'Councilman Vera' (Jose Berra), 'Councilman Vitage' (Sonny Vataj), 'Councilman G' (Barbara DiGiacinto, the lone 'no'), 'Councilman Hussein' (Saleem Hussain), and 'Supervisor Rendy' (Joseph Rende) — confirming the corrected 2026 roster. Matt Milim did not appear at all. 'Sunny/Sonny' = Vataj; 'Jose' in member context = Berra (distinct from Supervisor Rende). Staff (Kaufman, Spolzino/'Bob', Kevin, Abbas, Roland, Allison, Matt Traynor) and outside presenters (TPL's Aberger/Dumoulin, Carrie Kasak, student Jed Schisler) were kept out of member positions. No board members were absent.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Town Board held its March 2026 monthly meeting, opening with public announcements (town-wide cleanup day, local sports championships, a 'delay until 8' cell-phone program, and an Association of Towns essay/documentary honoring the town's Revolutionary War history). The centerpiece was a public hearing and adoption of a new local law regulating short-term rentals, prompted by resident complaints about an Airbnb-related driveway/towing incident. The board also passed two late-added resolutions (one urging the Governor to pursue SEQRA reform as a standalone bill rather than through the budget, and one authorizing an $8.62M TAP grant application for North Broadway pedestrian improvements), approved water-district payments and well-rehabilitation and personnel actions, and closed in memory of longtime resident Herb Sidney.
meetings.durationNote: Full board present (Rende, DiGiacinto, Hussain, Berra, Vataj); reconvened from executive session; no absences noted.

cases.name: Local Law — Short-Term Rental Regulations
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (Town Planner Adam Kaufman)
cases.summary: The board held a public hearing on a proposed local law creating a regulatory framework for short-term rentals, requiring a building-department permit plus an operating permit, occupancy/vehicle limits, a 120-day annual cap, noise restrictions, and a notarized affidavit or affirmation of primary residence. Town Planner Adam Kaufman summarized the draft and Attorney Roland answered questions on enforcement (police can issue violations) and affirmation forms. After public comment, the board closed the hearing, received the Planning Board memo (dated March 10), adopted a negative declaration, and adopted the local law by voice vote. Enforcement, public education, and a license-fee schedule were flagged as follow-up items.
cases.publicComment: Supportive/appreciative. Joyce Greaves (41 Washington Ave, 67-year resident) thanked the board and asked about license fees; John Solomon (Washington Ave) asked about occupancy/vehicle caps; Tan Nguyen (33 Washington Ave) described a red Florida pickup blocking their driveway for a day and a half with no police tow, which the board cited as the motivating problem.

memberPositions.evidence: Pressed that the primary-residence affidavit/affirmation be binding and that the police department be trained to enforce the law; welcomed 'finally enacting this law.'
Presided, framed the law as a response to residents' 'almost torture,' and committed to public education and website posting.
Flagged a typo addressing 'Supervisor Schalero' and asked how many short-term rentals exist; noted he found about four properties listed on Airbnb and asked Adam to email the board that data.
Reassured the community that 911/police and fire will respond to short-term-rental problems at any hour.

cases.name: Approval of Town Board Minutes — February 25, 2026
cases.summary: Under old business, the board approved the minutes of its February 25, 2026 meeting by voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Final Payment Requisition No. 1 — Southern Industries Corp. (Water District No. 4 / School Street Extension)
cases.summary: The board considered the final payment requisition (~$33,900, including ~$11,600 miscellaneous additional-work allowance and a mobilization charge) to Southern Industries for the Water District No. 4 (School Street) extension, plus receipt of a general release. Councilman Berra questioned paying a mobilization charge to a contractor the town released for underperformance when a replacement contractor also had to be paid to mobilize. Supervisor Rende and Attorney Roland explained the release was a negotiated arrangement to separate quickly before winter and avoid a surety dispute. The requisition was approved by voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Objected that paying mobilization twice 'doesn't make sense' for a non-performing contractor and could not locate the original agreement; accepted the explanation but flagged it 'for the future.'
Defended the negotiated release as securing 'the benefit of the bargain' and getting the work done before snowfall, citing surety-company risk.

cases.name: Alcohol Permit — Katona Classic Stage Reception at Whippoorwill Hall
cases.summary: The board approved an alcoholic-beverage permit for a Katona Classic Stage reception at Whippoorwill Hall on March 14 and 28, 2026, by voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Alcohol Permit — Atlantic Westchester Company Picnic at Lombardy Park
cases.summary: The board approved an alcoholic-beverage permit for an Atlantic Westchester company picnic at the Lombardy Park pavilion on May 30, 2026, by voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Special Permit — Troy's Nursery Garden Design LLC (Easter Event & Fall Festival)
cases.summary: The board received and approved a special-permit application from Troy's Nursery for an Easter event (March 29, 2026) and a fall festival (Sundays in October 2026). Under the town's new streamlined policy, such applications are pre-reviewed by staff so applicants no longer need individual public hearings, which the board praised as a customer-friendly improvement.

memberPositions.evidence: Highlighted that streamlining removed the prior public-hearing requirement, saying the applicant 'couldn't be any happier.'

cases.name: Authorization to Execute Consent Judgment — Armac 80 Associates & 84 Business Park Associates (Tax Certiorari)
cases.summary: The board authorized the town attorneys to execute consent judgments in the tax-certiorari matters of Armac 80 Associates, LLC (Index No. 63577-21) and 84 Business Park Associates (Index No. 63574-21). Approved by voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Resolution on Proposed SEQRA Amendments in the 2026 State of the State / Executive Budget
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (at request of Assemblyman Chris Burdick)
cases.summary: A late-added resolution urged the Governor to pursue proposed State Environmental Quality Review Act (SEQRA) reforms — including housing exemptions and a two-year EIS timeline — as a standalone bill open to municipal input rather than embedding them in the executive budget, to protect home rule. Town Planner Adam Kaufman explained the request originated with Assemblyman Chris Burdick. Councilwoman DiGiacinto and Councilman Berra pushed for softer, less-restrictive language (e.g., 'supports streamlining' and broader tolling wording), while Supervisor Rende and Councilman Hussain argued the resolution's sole purpose was to keep the reform out of the budget and that detailed language edits were premature. On a roll-call vote the resolution was adopted 4-0 with Councilman Berra abstaining (citing insufficient time to discuss).

memberPositions.evidence: Argued the tolling language was 'too narrow' and 'ties our hands,' said the board was 'putting the cart before the horse,' and abstained on the roll call because there 'wasn't enough time to really discuss it.'
Supported the intent and home rule but wanted the recital changed to 'may support'/'supports streamlining' and worried the tolling remedy wasn't broad enough to protect the town.
Pressed to move forward, stressing the resolution's only goal was a standalone bill giving municipalities input and that April 1 budget timing made it urgent.
Said he was 'supportive with the overall intention' and 'okay with the wording as is,' preferring to keep the resolution simple.
Asked how the reform arose and confirmed the resolution simply lets the town/elected officials have a say; voted aye on the roll call.

cases.name: Resolution — TAP Grant Application for North Broadway Pedestrian Improvements
cases.address: North Broadway, North White Plains (Reservoir to Sir John's Plaza)
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (Town Planner Adam Kaufman / grant writer)
cases.summary: A late-added resolution supported a Transportation Alternatives Program (TAP) grant application to NYSDOT for up to $8,620,000 and authorized the Supervisor and Town Attorney to sign, with the package due the next day. The ~$8.5M project (an 80/20 grant, ~$1.7M town match) would build new sidewalks, curbs, street trees, bus shelters, pedestrian lighting on both sides of North Broadway plus a signalized crosswalk at the Nethermont path. The board discussed how it would fund the match (fund balance vs. bonds) and confirmed the scope cannot be reduced arbitrarily once awarded. Adopted by voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Supported the grant but pressed that the board be genuinely comfortable with a funding path (bond or fund balance) before committing to the 20% match.
Sought clarification on the 20% commitment and funding options and signaled comfort with bonding or fund balance.
Asked about design drawings, who builds the sidewalks, project scope/length, and whether the town could spend less; confirmed comfort with the funding commitment.
Probed the scope/cost relationship and whether the town could spend less than $8M; helped clarify that grant scope can't be arbitrarily reduced.
Called the project a 'game changer' for North White Plains safety and appearance and credited the pre-application effort.

cases.name: Indemnity Agreement — Sustainability Committee Table on Cleanup Day
cases.summary: A late-added item authorized the Supervisor to sign a standard indemnity agreement (with DeCicco's/Chico's) allowing the Sustainability Committee to set up a table on town-wide cleanup day to sell food-scrap composting kits and distribute cleanup supplies. The agreement had not been posted to the agenda; Attorney Roland's two language concerns (including removal of the word 'sole') were resolved. Because the committee's event falls on a date before the next meeting, the board approved it by voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: As sustainability liaison, described the committee's cleanup-day table (composting kits, orange bags, grabbers) and his own participation in the cleanup.

cases.name: Contract Award — Land Christen Co. for Water District No. 2 Rehabilitation of Wells 3 and 4
cases.summary: The board awarded a contract to the Land Christen company for rehabilitation of Water District No. 2 wells 3 and 4 and authorized the Supervisor to sign, funded from Water District No. 2's fund balance. Water superintendent 'Sal' explained the spec includes priced worst-case alternatives (e.g., extra surging hours) to avoid later change orders, described declining production in the wells, and noted well 3 had a failed pump requiring investigation. Approved by voice vote; work must start within two weeks of award.

memberPositions.evidence: Asked how additional work beyond the bid is handled and praised the built-in worst-case pricing that reduces the need for change orders; asked about well production impacts on residents.
Commended the procurement-policy approach of pricing alternatives up front and confirmed the work is funded from the district's fund balance, not the general fund.

cases.name: Personnel Actions — Appointments and Terminal Leave
cases.summary: The board approved three personnel actions by voice vote: the probationary appointment of William Etzel as Librarian 1 at the North Castle Public Library (eff. March 16, 2026), the probationary appointment of Jeffrey (Highway Department, eff. March 16, 2026), and a terminal-leave payment to Michael Cromwell of the Building Department. A consensus agenda was also approved.

cases.name: Town Board Liaison Updates, Public Announcements & Closing in Memory
cases.summary: The board delivered opening announcements (town-wide cleanup day March 21/22 with shredder and e-waste, local sports championships, the 'delay until 8' business program April 20-26, and an Association of Towns documentary featuring intern Jenny Hsu's award-winning essay on North Castle's Revolutionary War history) and closing liaison updates. Updates covered library board expansion and volunteer recruitment, library e-book access workarounds, cleanup-day logistics and an invasive-vine event, resumed field work and spring curb repairs, and praise for highway/parks storm response. Supervisor Rende and Councilwoman DiGiacinto closed the meeting in memory of longtime Armonk resident Herb Sidney (age 94).

memberPositions.evidence: As library liaison, reported the library board's planned expansion to add members and its call for volunteers (especially from Armonk and those with project-management skills), and pressed on e-waste staffing/dumpster logistics.
Gave detailed cleanup-day guidance (attire, safety, bag/grabber returns, three hamlet pickup locations, e-waste eligibility) and promoted a Sunday invasive-vine removal event.
Explained library e-book borrowing limits from the Westchester Library System and the new Hoopla/Kanopy alternatives; helped close the meeting in memory of Herb Sidney.
Praised highway and parks staff for stellar storm response and delivered an extended tribute closing the meeting in memory of resident Herb Sidney.
Had no additional liaison update to add when polled.

themes.note: Public hearing and adoption of the short-term rental local law was the meeting's centerpiece, driven by resident complaints.
TAP grant ($8.62M) for North Broadway sidewalks with a $1.7M town match dominated the late additions.
SEQRA-reform resolution sparked the meeting's most contested debate over home rule and language.
Water District No. 4 final payment and Water District No. 2 wells 3 & 4 rehabilitation, both funded from district balances.
Cleanup day, sports congratulations, 'delay until 8' program, and the 250th-anniversary essay/documentary.
Routine alcohol and special-event permits approved, now streamlined via staff pre-review.
Streamlined permit policy and several late-added items not posted to the agenda.
Library and highway probationary appointments and a terminal-leave payment.
Consent judgments in two tax-certiorari matters.

staffInput.summary: Town Planner: summarized the short-term rental regulatory framework (permits, occupancy/vehicle/day caps, noise); explained the SEQRA-reform resolution's origin with Assemblyman Burdick; and presented the TAP grant details (scope, 80/20 split, $1.7M match) and the separate Lawler sidewalk application.

Advised on the short-term rental affidavit/affirmation and police enforcement authority, explained trespass/towing law to residents, handled the tax-certiorari consent judgments, reviewed the SEQRA resolution language, and cleared the indemnity-agreement wording.
Delivered public announcements (cleanup day, e-news), played the Association of Towns 250th documentary, managed hearing documents, and circulated the late indemnity agreement.

Water/Sewer superintendent: explained the wells 3 & 4 rehabilitation spec with priced worst-case alternatives to avoid change orders, described declining well production and a failed pump on well 3, and confirmed funding from Water District No. 2 fund balance.
Discussed grant-match funding options, coordinated e-waste staffing/dumpster logistics for cleanup day, and reported resumed field work and spring curb repairs (C-Click-Fix app).

meetings.attributionNote: Speakers were identifiable from context and a roll-call vote. ASR mangled several names: 'Endy'/'Jose' (presiding) = Joseph Rende; 'Barra' = Jose Berra; 'Visage'/'Vitage' = Sonny Vataj; 'Hussein' = Saleem Hussain; 'Celine'/'Selenium' = Saleem Hussain; 'Digacinto' = Barbara DiGiacinto. 2026 board confirmed as Rende, DiGiacinto, Hussain, Berra, Vataj — Matt Milim is no longer on the board and did not appear. The only roll-call vote (SEQRA resolution) recorded DiGiacinto/Vataj/Hussain/Rende aye with Berra abstaining (4-0); all other items passed by voice vote. Full board present; no absences noted.

meetings.meetingSummary: The Town Board opened with the promotion of Sergeant Joel Thomas to police lieutenant and a Women's History Month '250th history moment' presented by a local sixth-grade student. It held a public hearing and adopted a special use permit for the Virgin Mary & St. Damian Coptic Orthodox Church to enable handicap access, and authorized up to $1,000 for the 250th anniversary art-contest reception. The board approved a slate of routine items (payment applications, bonds, referrals, conference travel, personnel actions), a state records-management grant application, the police chief's employment agreement, and a highway general-foreman stipend that passed 3-0 with Councilman Berra abstaining. An audit engagement letter was tabled over concerns about its risk-of-misstatement language, and liaison reports covered townwide cleanup day and several capital projects.
meetings.durationNote: Councilman Sonny Vataj absent (traveling); quorum of four present (Rende, DiGiacinto, Hussain, Berra). Noted by the board as a short meeting.

cases.name: Promotion of Sergeant Joel Thomas to Police Lieutenant
cases.summary: The police chief presented Sergeant Joel Thomas (NCPD since 2005, senior sergeant, accreditation program lead and de facto IT officer) for promotion to administrative lieutenant to fill a vacancy created by the chief's own recent promotion, effective March 26, 2026. The board unanimously adopted the promotion (all in favor) and the supervisor administered the oath of office with Thomas's family present. Celebratory, no dissent.
cases.publicComment: A large contingent of police department members and Thomas's family attended in support; congratulatory tone throughout.

memberPositions.evidence: Praised how much he enjoys promotions in the department, moved the oath, said he had interacted with Thomas a lot and is very proud of him.

cases.name: 250th History Moment — North Castle's Revolutionary War Women (Women's History Month)
cases.summary: As part of the town's 250th-anniversary commemoration, sixth-grader Zelda June Topolski of H.C. Crittenden Middle School delivered a Women's History Month 'history moment' on the roles and sacrifices of North Castle women during the Revolutionary War, including Widow Ann Miller and the Miller House (Washington's headquarters). No action was taken; the supervisor also announced a new high-school civics spotlight program featuring student Paloma Hussain. Purely ceremonial and community-focused.
cases.publicComment: Student presentation warmly received ('excellent, excellent, excellent'); no resident dissent.

memberPositions.evidence: Praised the presentation and used it to launch a new monthly high-school student spotlight program showcasing town boards and committees.

cases.name: Special Use Permit — Virgin Mary & St. Damian Coptic Orthodox Church
cases.applicant: Virgin Mary & St. Damian Coptic Orthodox Church (Father Paul)
cases.summary: The board opened and held a public hearing on a special use permit for a church operating since 1913 that had never received one; the permit is a prerequisite for the planning board to approve a site plan allowing construction of a handicap-access sidewalk to the church basement for elderly parishioners. Town Planner Adam Kaufman explained the procedural background and the clerk read the notices, including a well-received historical memorandum from resident Nora Emanueli. Father Paul confirmed no exterior/structural changes beyond accessibility. The board received the planning board recommendation, closed the hearing, and adopted the resolution granting the special use permit (all in favor).
cases.publicComment: Father Paul spoke in support, describing elderly parishioners unable to attend due to stairs; tone appreciative and supportive.

memberPositions.evidence: Clarified for viewers that there is no change to the structure, only handicap access, and thanked Father Paul for the accommodation.

cases.name: Authorization of Funds — North Castle 250th Art Contest Committee Opening Reception (not to exceed $1,000)
cases.applicant: North Castle 250th Celebration Arts Committee (Marianne Hamilton, chair)
cases.summary: Committee chair Marianne Hamilton requested up to $1,000 to fund the April 9, 2026 opening reception of a 250th-anniversary art contest exhibit at the library (33 submissions, 13 from students), covering prizes/gift certificates, framing/hanging materials, PR, and reception costs. Councilman Hussain probed the proportionality of spending (e.g., prizes shouldn't crowd out other categories) and asked that Town Administrator Kevin be given discretion to align reimbursements with the stated categories. The board unanimously authorized the funds (all in favor), with reimbursement via submitted receipts.
cases.publicComment: Marianne Hamilton presented enthusiastically, recounting committee work and a story of a resident who resumed painting after 30 years; strongly positive.

memberPositions.evidence: Fully supported it but asked for proportional spending across prizes/framing/PR and that the town administrator be given discretion to ensure reimbursements align with what was agreed.
Championed the 250th effort, encouraged residents to contribute, and looked forward to displaying artwork permanently around town.
Noted as having attended several 250th committee meetings; supportive of the exhibit and reception.

cases.name: Audit Engagement / Consensus Letter (Agreements A & Consensus B) — Tabled
cases.summary: The supervisor announced that the audit engagement item (Agreements A) and the related consensus letter (B) would be tabled for further consideration. Councilman Berra flagged that the engagement letter identified 'management override of controls' as a significant risk of material misstatement and was inconsistent with the 2024 agreement with the same firm. The supervisor and counsel agreed it was inappropriate to debate a tabled item, but confirmed Berra's concerns were valid, had been communicated to Town Administrator Kevin, and would be addressed at a meeting the next day.

memberPositions.evidence: Raised the 'management override of controls' risk language and inconsistency with the 2024 agreement, wanting to ensure the issue is addressed before adoption.
Agreed the item should be tabled and that discussing it while tabled was inappropriate, but acknowledged Berra's points were correct and would be addressed.

cases.name: Approval of Town Board Minutes — March 11, 2026
cases.summary: Routine approval of the town board minutes from the March 11, 2026 meeting. Moved, seconded, and approved with no discussion.

cases.name: Payment Application No. 7 — Papadino Construction (Water District No. 4 New Well Project)
cases.summary: The board approved Payment Application No. 7 to Papadino Construction Company Inc. for site work performed at the Water District No. 4 new well project. Routine consent-style approval, moved and seconded, all in favor.

cases.name: KSCJ Consulting Recommendation — Younger Star Residence Wetland Bonds (14 Tall Woods Road)
cases.summary: On the town engineer's recommendation, the board voted to release the wetland mitigation bond and extend the five-year monitoring and maintenance bond through August 2029 for the Younger Star Residence project. Routine approval, moved and seconded, all in favor.

cases.name: Street Address Assessment — Madonna Subdivision (130 Mount Kisco Road), E911 Referral
cases.summary: The board received a March 5, 2026 memo from KSCJ Consulting regarding assessment of new street addresses for the Madonna subdivision at 130 Mount Kisco Road and referred it to the town E911 coordinator. Routine, moved and seconded, all in favor.

cases.name: Interim MS4 Stormwater Reports (period ending January 2, 2026)
cases.summary: The board accepted the interim MS4 stormwater reports for the period ending January 2, 2026 from the town engineer and authorized the supervisor to sign the reports. Routine compliance item, moved and seconded, all in favor.

cases.name: Hospital for Special Surgery — Use of Town Roads for Bike HSS Community Event (Sept 19)
cases.summary: The board approved a request from Hospital for Special Surgery to use town roads for the Bike HSS bike-and-walk/run community event on Saturday, September 19, with the motion amended to refer the request to professional staff. The supervisor voiced strong personal support, crediting HSS with a successful ACL surgery. Clarified the date as September 19th, not the 9th.

memberPositions.evidence: Said he 'fully supports this,' noting he is walking around with an ACL that HSS put in and did a great job.

cases.name: Resolution — NYS Archives Local Government Records Management Improvement Fund Grant Application (up to $75,000)
cases.summary: The board adopted a resolution authorizing a New York State Archives Local Government Records Management Improvement Fund grant application for the conservation of historical records in an amount not to exceed $75,000, and authorized the supervisor to sign the application. Moved, seconded, all in favor.

cases.name: Employment Agreement — Chief of Police Reagan Hufnagle (effective Jan 1, 2026)
cases.summary: The board authorized the supervisor to sign the employment agreement with Chief of Police Reagan Hufnagle, effective January 1, 2026. Moved, seconded, all in favor with no discussion.

cases.name: Annual Stipend — Jamie Norris, Highway General Foreman (effective Jan 1)
cases.summary: The board considered an annual stipend for Highway General Foreman Jamie Norris, effective January 1, prompted by the discovery that compensation for his additional duties had been unilaterally removed by a prior supervisor and never restored. Councilman Berra praised Norris but objected to setting compensation mid-year rather than during budget sessions and abstained ('stood'). On a roll call the measure passed 3-0 (DiGiacinto aye, Hussain aye, Rende yes; Berra abstained; Vataj absent). A lengthy exchange followed between Rende and Berra on the meaning and propriety of abstention, with counsel explaining an abstention is a non-vote that still effectively counts against passage since a majority of the full board is required.

memberPositions.evidence: Said he fully supports reviewing Norris's comp in the next budget session and supports Jamie tremendously, but abstained because compensation decisions should be made during budget, not mid-year; defended abstention as legitimate against the supervisor's criticism.

Voted yes; argued the mid-year action was justified because prior removal of the compensation was only just discovered, and criticized frequent abstention as 'abdicating' a board member's responsibility to vote.
Voted aye on the roll call.
Voted aye on the roll call.

cases.name: Town Clerk Allison Simon — 2026 NYS Town Clerks Association Conference (Albany, Apr 19-22)
cases.summary: The board approved Town Clerk Allison Simon's attendance at the 2026 New York State Town Clerks Association Conference in Albany, April 19-22, 2026. Moved, seconded, all in favor. The supervisor expressed interest in a scheduled NYS Department of Health session.

cases.name: Library Staff — American Library Association Conference (Chicago, Jun 25-28)
cases.summary: The board approved attendance by Library Assistant Director Angela Cook and librarian Roxanne Guzman at the American Library Association conference in Chicago, June 25-28, 2026. Moved, seconded, all in favor.

cases.name: Terminal Leave Payment — Lisa Larson, Parks & Recreation Department
cases.summary: The board approved a terminal leave payment to Lisa Larson of the Parks and Recreation Department. Routine personnel item, moved and seconded, all in favor.

cases.name: Reappointment — George Tropeau to the Conservation Board (term to March 11, 2028)
cases.summary: The board reappointed George Tropeau to the Conservation Board for a two-year term expiring March 11, 2028. The motion was made 'with appreciation and thanks,' seconded, all in favor.

cases.name: Townwide Cleanup Day — Liaison Report
cases.summary: Councilman Berra, sustainability committee liaison, gave a detailed report on the successful townwide cleanup day the prior Saturday: 182 residents dropped off paper for shredding, roughly two-and-a-half containers of e-waste were collected, and 88 orange trash bags were gathered across Armonk, Banksville and North White Plains. He thanked residents, staff (Allison, Kevin, Eliana, Josephine), Jamie Norris and the highway department, and noted a resident request to repeat the event later in the year. Light banter followed about deer ticks and DiGiacinto's participation across multiple years.

memberPositions.evidence: Delivered an enthusiastic detailed report with statistics, thanked residents and staff, and relayed a resident request to hold the event again later in the year.
Recognized for participating in most or all years of the cleanup and joining the Quarry Heights park walk-through.

cases.name: Capital Projects & Parks Update — Liaison/Supervisor Report
cases.summary: The supervisor and administrator reported on several projects: the School Street water-line extension is complete, restoring potable water and reopening the bathrooms at Lombardi Park after several years; Quarry Heights park improvements are planned using in-house staff and saved topsoil; the turf-field project (delayed by snow) expects turf delivery in mid-April with completion and a ribbon-cutting by late May; and Clove Road work resumes soon, with repaving planned at Lombardi and North White Plains community park lots. Also reported: NC Vine Cutters cleanup by The Eagle, recreation hiring for camps/pools (lifeguards, staff over 16), and an emergency-managers/EOC meeting covering the county's expiring five-year hazard-mitigation plan and potential FEMA funding. Berra asked whether FEMA funds could help dredge Byron Brook to alleviate School Street flooding.

memberPositions.evidence: Reported completion of the School Street water line, restored potable water at Lombardi Park, and progress on turf field, Quarry Heights, and repaving; also thanked Parks staff for coping with non-potable water during the project.
Asked about working with FEMA on a grant to dredge Byron Brook to help alleviate School Street flooding.

themes.note: Lieutenant promotion, police chief agreement, highway foreman stipend, conference travel, terminal leave, and a board reappointment dominated the agenda.
250th anniversary threads: history moment, art-contest reception funding, cleanup day, and student civics spotlight.
School Street water line, turf field, Quarry Heights, repaving, and Water District 4 well payment.
Recurring tension over mid-year spending vs. budget-session discipline, most sharply on the highway stipend and tabled audit letter.
Extended Rende-Berra exchange on the meaning and propriety of abstention, plus tabling procedure.
Lieutenant promotion, chief employment agreement, and an emergency-managers/EOC briefing.
Coptic church special use permit public hearing enabling handicap access.
Cleanup day, wetland bond, MS4 stormwater reports, and hazard-mitigation/FEMA discussion.
Papadino payment application and chief agreement adopted; audit engagement letter tabled over risk language.

staffInput.summary: Town Planner (via Zoom) explained the procedural background of the Coptic church special use permit — the church has operated since 1913 without a permit, and the town board must adopt the SUP before the planning board can approve a site plan for the handicap-access sidewalk.

Gave community announcements (E-News/NIXLE sign-up, volunteer opportunities) and read the publication of notice, affidavits, and correspondence into the record for the church public hearing, highlighting resident Nora Emanueli's historical memorandum.

Advised that art-contest funds would be reimbursed against submitted receipts and was given board discretion to ensure spending aligns with agreed categories; provided detail on capital projects and cleanup logistics.

Advised that discussing a tabled item is inappropriate, and explained on the highway-stipend roll call that an abstention is a non-vote that still effectively counts against passage because a majority of the full board (three votes) is required. (Speaker could alternatively be special counsel Bob Spolzino; counsel identity not certain from ASR.)
Presented Sergeant Joel Thomas's qualifications and formally requested the board promote him to administrative lieutenant to fill the vacancy created by the chief's own recent promotion.

meetings.attributionNote: Speakers were identified with good confidence. The presiding/supervisor voice is Joseph Rende (ASR 'Rende/Ende'). Saleem Hussain appears mangled as 'Celine'/'Salim'/'Hussein' (he raised the art-contest proportionality point and is the parent of student Paloma Hussain). Jose Berra appears as 'Vera'/'Barra' — he led the cleanup-day report, raised the audit-letter concern, and abstained on the highway stipend; disambiguated from Supervisor Rende by role (Berra is the member polled in roll call).
