cases.summary: The board authorized the supervisor to execute an agreement with Axon Enterprise, Inc. for the purchase of body-worn cameras and a five-year associated service plan for the police department. Approved by motion, second, and voice vote with no discussion recorded.

cases.name: Personnel Actions — Parks & Recreation Appointments, Librarian Resignation, Library Board Appointment
cases.applicant: Recreation & Parks Department; North Castle Public Library
cases.summary: The board approved the provisional appointment of a Senior Office Assistant in Recreation & Parks effective June 29, 2026 (noted as already budgeted in the 2026 budget), the probationary appointment of Ruri Corden as Parks Groundsman effective July 6, 2026, received with regret the resignation letter of lead librarian Stephanie Paul effective June 15, 2026, and appointed a new library board member to a five-year term. All items passed on individual motions, seconds, and voice votes (aye).

themes.note: Extended public-comment exchange on pickleball court status, Winkler Park tennis-court conditions, Lombardi Park feasibility, and the town pool renovation as a competing funding priority.
Swearing-in of two new police officers plus routine parks, library, and library-board personnel actions.
Two tax certiorari consent judgments, a WSP dam engineering contract, and the Axon body-worn-camera agreement, all passed with little discussion; one unclear board recusal.
Letter regarding the Bosey's water main and the possibility of a future water district serving Quarry Heights/Old Orchard Road residents.
Swearing-in of two new officers and approval of body-worn camera technology for the department.
Byron Hill(s) Boys Tennis Team championship parade/sign unveiling, a student Flag Day history presentation, and the announced July 4th 250th-anniversary celebration.
Ethics Board annual report: no complaints/investigations, growing use of advisory opinions, and a newly found code discrepancy to be discussed with counsel.
June 10 minutes tabled over a factual dispute about the parking-district hearing record; a member's development-related comments were ruled out of order.

staffInput.summary: Responded to the pickleball-court public comment by describing the town pool renovation bid timeline as the immediate funding priority and acknowledging communication had been imperfect; separately announced the paving program timeline (late July/early August), completion of the town's dot-gov website/email security migration, and details of the July 4th 250th-anniversary celebration.

Explained the history and ownership of the Westchester Joint Water Works main built to serve the Bosey's property, why it cannot currently connect other Old Orchard Road residents, and what forming a new water district and taking over the main would require.

Noted that redevelopment of the neighboring property would likely trigger extension of the water main to serve it, and offered that either he or special counsel Spolzino could assist the ethics board with the code discrepancy it identified.

As Ethics Board Chair, delivered the board's verbal annual report: no complaints or investigations this year, growing informal use of advisory opinions by board/committee members, and disclosure of a newly discovered code discrepancy to be addressed with counsel.

meetings.attributionNote: Barbara DiGiacinto and Jose Berra are directly named/addressed at several points and Joseph Rende is identifiable as the presiding supervisor, but much of the pickleball, ethics-board, and Quarry Heights cross-talk is unattributed overlapping dialogue in the ASR with no speaker labels; Sonny Vataj is never named anywhere in this transcript, and a mid-meeting recusal could not be confidently attributed to a specific member or even a specific agenda item.

meetings.meetingSummary: An unusually long (nearly three-hour) meeting that opened with public comment opposing renewal of the Marianis special-use permit pending new-town-hall site planning and a demonstration of a resident-built AI transparency tool (OpenNorthCastle.com), followed by authorization of RFPs for new town hall architectural/planning services, a zoning text amendment referral for a Main Street tutoring/school use, a contentious but unresolved request to excuse the 12 Maple Avenue restaurant project from a duplicate community-benefits payment now that a parking district is moving forward, a heated 4-1 vote extending the long-stalled Gateway/former-Marianis-Gardens special use permit for another year, formation steps for a new Rose Hill Drive sewer district connection, acceptance of Toll Brothers' Enclave water district improvements, and award of the North Castle Pool and Tennis Club deck renovation bid (with add-on sub-base protection and diamond-bright finish options).
meetings.durationNote: Supervisor Rende presided with Councilmembers Hussain, DiGiacinto, Berra and newly-elected Councilman Sonny Vataj (who replaced Matt Milim) present. Vataj's name is inconsistently transcribed by the ASR (as 'the Taj,' 'Bataj,' and 'Tony DiCaros' in different spots); Councilman Berra recused from at least one item.

cases.name: New Town Hall — Architectural and Planning Services RFP
cases.summary: Following public comment from the town's 're-imagination committee' chair urging more detailed site/engineering information in the RFP (and a related public comment urging the board not to renew the nearby Marianis special use permit until new town hall site planning is complete), the board authorized Director of Planning Adam Kaufman to issue RFPs for architectural and planning services for the 2026 town hall project. Board members debated whether to direct the RFP toward solar/green-energy features or revised square-footage targets before hiring the architect, ultimately agreeing those decisions should follow the architect's own analysis rather than being dictated upfront.
cases.publicComment: A resident urged the board not to extend the Marianis special use permit until town hall site planning is finalized, noting that site may be needed for redevelopment. The re-imagination committee chair (Alan Blum) said the town's initial RFP draft lacked sufficient site/engineering detail and had submitted written suggestions, most of which planning staff incorporated.

memberPositions.evidence: Argued that square footage and green-energy specifics should be left to the architect's analysis rather than dictated in the RFP, to avoid delaying the process further after 'going around in full circle' on the project for two years.

cases.name: 355 Main Street — PBO-2A Zoning Text Amendment (Tutoring/School Use)
cases.status: referred to planning boards; public hearing scheduled September 9, 2026
cases.summary: The board received the application, staff report, draft local law, negative declaration and declared its intent to act as lead agency for a zoning text amendment to the town's only PBO-2A district (355 Main Street, the former InterWire building) to permit tutoring-center and multi-tenant school uses, referring the matter to town and county planning boards and scheduling a September 9, 2026 public hearing.

cases.name: 12 Maple Avenue (Wren of the Woods) — Community Benefits Agreement Amendment Request
cases.status: received; referred to town attorneys for review, no decision
cases.summary: The applicant's principal argued at length that, since the Main Street parking district is now moving forward and 12 Maple Avenue would pay into it, the project's separate $100,000 Community Benefits Agreement parking-mitigation payment should be waived to avoid 'double-dipping' on the same parking-mitigation objective, citing planning department memos and a zoning board precedent. The board received the request and the applicant's July 6 litigation-hold letter, directed him to submit full written comments to the clerk, and referred the matter to the town attorneys for review; no vote was taken. Board members were sympathetic in principle but noted the CBA was negotiated with uncertainty about whether the parking district would ever materialize.

memberPositions.evidence: Acknowledged the fairness argument (calling the double payment potential 'double-dipping') and said it would 'probably be an approving thing' for the town to eventually release the CBA obligation, but deferred to town attorney review before any decision.

Said she voted for the original $100,000 CBA payment because, after 20 years of parking-district discussions going nowhere, she doubted a district would ever actually be built, but agreed the current situation risks 'double-dipping.'

cases.name: Gateway Residential Development (former Marianis Gardens) — Special Use Permit Extension
cases.summary: After public comment from neighboring Wampus Lake Estates residents citing an unsecured, unfinished excavation site as a safety hazard and nuisance, and from a board member (Vataj) proposing a shorter 120-day extension conditioned on immediately filling the hole and installing a proper fence, the town attorney advised that state case law entitles the vested special use permit to a full one-year renewal absent a material change in conditions. The board adopted the fourth consecutive one-year extension 4-1 (DiGiacinto opposed), with Supervisor Rende disclosing that some project principals have contributed to his campaign but stating the approval predates his tenure and he could remain impartial. The applicant's attorney denied the permit had ever lapsed and said a new, experienced developer (RMA Development/Ralph Rossi) is now driving the project forward, expecting visible progress within about 120 days and committing to level the excavation and improve fencing in the interim.
cases.publicComment: A Wampus Lake Estates HOA representative and a board member/former resident both described the unsecured excavation ('pile of dirt and a hole') as a longstanding safety hazard, especially given nearby children, and expressed frustration at years of inaction since 2023 approvals.

memberPositions.stance: conditionally opposed to a full one-year extension
memberPositions.evidence: Proposed limiting the extension to 120 days tied to immediately securing the site (leveling the hole, fencing), arguing the town has legal authority to require site safety regardless of special-use-permit renewal timing; ultimately voted aye on the resolution after being advised the shorter term was not legally supportable.
Cast the lone dissenting vote on the fourth consecutive one-year extension.

Publicly disclosed that certain 45 Bedford Road principals had contributed to his reelection campaign, stated this did not preclude his vote since the underlying approval predated his time on the board, and voted to approve the extension while pressing for the fence/hole to be addressed.
Voted aye on the roll call for the one-year extension.

cases.name: Local Law Amending Chapter 340 — Wetland/Watercourse Protection Mitigation Monitoring Fees
cases.summary: The board scheduled a public hearing on a local law adding wetland-mitigation-plan monitoring fees to the master fee schedule (to reimburse the town engineer for multi-year post-construction review of mitigation plantings/compliance) and minor conservation-board-proposed text cleanups to the wetlands chapter. One board member pushed back on the need for town-engineer-billed oversight on top of existing certified engineer/architect sign-offs, questioning the value versus cost to applicants, while others defended it as necessary independent verification that mitigation plans are actually being maintained.

cases.name: 9 Rose Hill Drive — Petition to Join Sewer District Number Two
cases.summary: The board received the petition, engineering letter, map/plan/report and environmental assessment for extending Sewer District 2 to 9 Rose Hill Drive and scheduled an August 12, 2026 public hearing. A board member disclosed living on the same block and having worked years earlier with a neighbor to help bring sewers to the area, but did not see a conflict.

cases.name: The Enclave (Toll Brothers, formerly Airport Campus/MBIA site) — Water District Improvements Acceptance
cases.summary: The board adopted a resolution accepting and dedicating water district improvements (pump station, water tank, mains) built as part of the Enclave's 125-townhome redevelopment of the former MBIA/airport campus site, including a temporary-power provisioning plan pending permanent ConEd service, so the developer can obtain certificates of occupancy for units already under contract (first phase of 19 townhomes closing in August). Board members noted the project's community benefit of bringing new municipal water capacity to the area and that the development will be fully taxed rather than under a PILOT arrangement.

cases.name: North Castle Pool and Tennis Club — Pool Deck Renovation Bid Award
cases.address: North Castle Pool and Tennis Club
cases.summary: The board awarded the pool deck renovation contract to (Tony) Casali/Casal Inc., approving both add-on items recommended by the town engineer: a roughly $29,700 sub-base protection allowance (to avoid uncapped change-order exposure if subsurface conditions are poor) and a roughly $49,000 upgrade to a longer-lasting 'diamond bright' pool finish, which also offers darker color options that help retain water warmth. The base bid came in well under the $5 million bond originally authorized (roughly $3.2 million), prompting discussion (unresolved) of using leftover bond capacity for bathroom/locker-room improvements or the adjacent parking lot rather than reducing the bond outright. Work is slated to begin around September 8, with 180 days to complete, targeting a Memorial Day reopening.

memberPositions.evidence: Suggested not borrowing the full original bond amount and instead considering using savings for bathroom/locker-room improvements while staying under the original budget envelope.

RFP process for architectural/planning services, tied to the Marianis site debate.
Toll Brothers Enclave dedication and Rose Hill sewer district petition.
Pool deck renovation bid award, under original bond estimate.

meetings.attributionNote: This was an exceptionally long (~2h48m) meeting; analysis focused on the most substantive agenda items (roughly 8-9 cases) and did not exhaustively cover every routine NYS Association of Towns resolution, minor personnel action, or consensus-agenda item. ASR transcript is un-diarized and garbled the new councilman Sonny Vataj's name multiple different ways ('the Taj,' 'Bataj,' 'Tony DiCaros'); attributions to him carry medium confidence based on contextual self-identification ('Sunny') and topical continuity. Roll-call votes provided high-confidence attribution for DiGiacinto, Hussain, and Rende; a fourth councilman's roll-call name was not clearly transcribed.
